before.name: ClearGov
before.description: Budget building and transparency software for local governments and schools - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: ClearGov sells cloud-based software that local governments and school districts use to manage the finance cycle, and it counts more than 2,000 of them as users. Published documents are a large part of the job, with budget books, ACFRs, PAFRs, annual reports, and CIP books built from guided templates.

Department heads submit capital requests through web-based forms that collect consistent data and feed a central dashboard. Finance staff can build and compare different budget scenarios before settling on a plan. Approved work can be published to automatically updated Public Project Pages carrying timelines, financials, maps, photos, and announcements. A strategic plan can likewise be turned into a website so constituents can follow progress over time. Outputs are generated ADA-compliant for sharing, publishing, or print-ready PDF distribution.

The company reports $540B in managed budgets. It also cites a 98% customer satisfaction figure. Its customer success team includes former local government finance officers. For counties, a built-in checklist maps to the criteria for the NACo EDGE Excellence in Strategic Planning Award.

before.name: Acentra Health
before.description: Medicaid enterprise systems, care and utilization management for states - exhibited at Healthcare IT Connect 2026, NAMPI 2026

paragraphs: Acentra Health builds health technology and clinical services for government healthcare programs. Its Medicaid Enterprise System takes in professional, institutional, and dental claims and encounters, whether they arrive by electronic data interchange or on paper.

An automated adjudication engine sends processed claims on for payment and flags the ones that need further review. The rules behind those decisions can be entered without code, so administrators can reflect policy changes and mandates as they arrive. A separate provider management module handles enrollment through a configurable intake application. Before a provider is enrolled, a credentialing service verifies licensing and looks for sanctions. External Quality Review services sit alongside the software.

The company claims more than 30 years of public sector health experience. Its claims platform, it says, has earned CMS certification back to day one of operations with zero CMS findings. The provider module is described as CMS certified and compliant with National Institute of Standards and Technology requirements. A federal claims product is described as carrying an Authority to Operate in secure federal data centers.

paragraphs: SewerAI sells a platform for sewer inspection work, aimed at utilities, contractors and engineers. It covers the work from inspection through rehabilitation.

PIONEER, the record-keeping side, brings inspection records, asset histories, maintenance logs and compliance documentation into one platform. It also builds capital plans, letting users lasso-select segments on a map and apply budget constraints and cost guidance.

The site says the platform is used by more than 2,000 cities nationwide. The company describes 400 years of combined experience pulling cable, running cameras and managing programs. Its detection draws on more than 425,000 NASSCO surveys and 40,000 manhole assessments. SewerAI states that it is SOC 2 Type II certified.

before.name: Azora Software
before.description: Short-term rental compliance: finds unpermitted rentals, automates permitting and tax enforcement - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Azora Software sells short-term rental compliance software to local governments. The problem it targets is that ordinary permitting systems only capture the rentals that volunteer to apply, leaving the rest unseen.

To close that gap the platform aggregates data from more than 75 sources, cross-references listings against property and parcel records, compiles verifiable evidence and connects to a city's code enforcement operations. Permitting then runs against that discovered address list, covering applications, renewals, status tracking and enforcement actions. Separate tools handle transaction reporting and statement reconciliation to support tax auditing and remittance. For enforcement and appeals, the platform generates PDFs and consolidated evidence of rental activity on demand.

Cities are the customer, and other government technology vendors also bring Azora in for short-term rental work beside the platforms those cities already run. The company says it was founded by three experienced professionals with complementary expertise and runs on a lean structure. One of them is a former city manager of Garden City, Utah. The same team previously built STR Helper, which the about page says was acquired by Host Compliance in 2019. Each customer keeps a named project manager who moves from launch into ongoing support.

paragraphs: Adobe sells creative software, and the tools it names first are Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere. A second line covers documents, using AI to make edits, answer questions, share information and produce polished content. For companies the pitch is to unify data, content and workflows and to personalize at scale.

Firefly is the generative AI piece, a creative space for making and editing images, video, audio and vector graphics from text prompts. It carries Adobe's own models next to partner models from Google, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Luma AI and Runway. Adobe says those models are trained on licensed Adobe Stock and public domain content, and that it does not train on users' personal or generated content. Prompts are accepted in more than 100 languages, and audio and video translation covers more than 20.

The audience Adobe names for Firefly is designers, photographers, video editors, marketers and social media creators. Students and teachers are offered a discount on the creative tools. The company says Firefly has been used to generate over 18 billion assets globally. Its catalog page notes that a purchase can be cancelled within 14 days for a full refund.

paragraphs: Everbridge sells a platform for managing physical and digital threats from end to end. Some of it protects traveling and remote employees. Other parts are built to inform and protect citizens at scale.

The method is to identify threats, work out who and what is affected, coordinate the response, communicate, and learn from every incident. Detection draws on risk intelligence, geospatial analysis, operational data and verified external and internal sources. Messages go out across multiple channels, with more than one delivery method per contact. A separate product centralizes business continuity planning, risk assessment, dependency mapping and testing. The main platform is available in three packages aimed at different kinds of organization.

The company states it has more than 6,500 global customers. Mass notifications are put at 6 billion a year. A customer story describes Fairfax County delivering multilingual safety alerts to over a million people. It cites a Forrester study putting average return on investment for the platform at 358 percent.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AWS is the world's most comprehensive cloud, enabling organizations to accelerate innovation, reduce costs, and scale more efficiently" The URL is factually correct and does NOT violate the parent-domain rule: aws.amazon.com is AWS's own canonical property (its own brand, console, pricing, docs and its own careers page at https://aws.amazon.com/careers/, HTTP 200), not Amazon's corporate site at amazon.com. The govtech tie is on-domain too: https://aws.amazon.com/government-education/ (HTTP 200) is AWS's public sector page, and the homepage names 'AWS GovCloud (US-East)' and 'AWS GovCloud (US-West)'. MY JUDGMENT ON WHETHER THE BOARD SHOULD CARRY THIS AT ALL - the URL passes but the record is still risky, for a reason the URL check cannot fix: aws.amazon.com/careers/ does not host jobs, it hands off to https://www.amazon.jobs/en/business_categories/amazon-web-services. That feed is tens of thousands of global AWS engineering/PM/ops roles, of which SLED account executive roles are a tiny fraction. Any homepage- or careers-page-level scrape of this record will flood SLED JOBS with irrelevant listings - the same practical damage the parent-domain rule exists to prevent, arriving by a different route. Recommendation: keep the URL if AWS is wanted on the board, but the record must be wired to

competitors.why: Body cameras, in-car video and cloud digital evidence management - the incumbent LensLock is bid against in nearly every department camera RFP.

paragraphs: LensLock sells body-worn cameras, in-car video, and CJIS-compliant evidence management to law enforcement agencies. Its pitch to departments is plain: evidence that holds up, upload and redaction that is FBI-compliant, and support staff who answer the phone. The products are designed around how officers work in the field, and a mobile app for iOS and Android handles in-field tagging and review.

The body cameras run a full shift on one battery, start recording on up to 8 auto-activation triggers, and offload video automatically. Docking stations charge up to 20 cameras at a time while pushing footage to LensLocker, the company's cloud evidence system. In the car, the Titan V system pairs a 4-channel mobile DVR with up to 2 terabytes of storage, GPS with geofencing, and cellular or WiFi offloading. Once footage is in LensLocker, officers can share it with the district attorney and redact faces, plates, and IDs.

Storage sits on Microsoft Azure Government Cloud, which the company describes as FBI CJIS-compliant and staffed by screened US citizens only. A license plate recognition feature scans video and flags matches from approved watchlists. The site notes that feature availability varies by device and configuration. Jon Handy founded LensLock in 2015 and now serves as Executive Vice President, Sales and Chairman of the Board of Directors. Chief Conrad Pepperman of the Rockaway Borough Police Department in New Jersey is quoted praising the customer service.

before.name: Alertus Technologies
before.description: Emergency mass notification hardware and software for schools and agencies - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Alertus Technologies sells emergency notification hardware and software that organizations install to warn everyone on a site at once. The company positions itself as a single source for mass emergency notification systems and critical communication needs. Its stated goal is to help colleges and universities, K-12 schools, corporations and government organizations solve unified mass notification problems.

The approach is network based, using an organization's existing IP network to turn VoIP phones into alerting devices. Hardware fills the gaps, including a wall-mounted alerting device meant for places with no existing notification endpoints. Outdoor coverage is handled by high power speaker arrays.

The company traces its origin to 2001, when an F3 tornado ripped through the University of Maryland campus. Alertus was founded the following year. It reports serving more than 2,500 organizations across more than 40 countries. Those customers are described as spanning higher education, K-12, industrial, corporate, healthcare, government and military sectors.

paragraphs: Alivia Analytics sells software and services that help health plans and government agencies cut the losses caused by fraud, waste, abuse and payment errors. Its platform, Alivia 360, gathers pre-payment and post-payment work into one suite.

Before a claim is paid, a claims manager scores high-risk providers and applies configurable pend-and-review triggers with compliance checks. After payment, a lead-finding tool feeds special investigations units while a case manager handles the volume of cases and the workflow around them. A separate data service standardizes claims data into analytics-ready formats and takes in whatever the payer sends. The company frames its AI as an assistant rather than a replacement, with human oversight and ethical use.

Buyers span Medicaid, Medicare and state programs as well as private health plans, third party administrators and self-insured employers. The company says it began by helping state Medicaid programs and Blues organizations speed up post-pay recoveries. A leadership page lists a full slate of officers, among them a chief information security officer.

before.name: 120Water
before.description: Lead service line inventories, sampling, and compliance software - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: 120Water sells compliance software to public water utilities and to the state agencies that oversee them. The company describes one shared system that standardizes water data and requirements into reporting and community communications. The argument for it is that utilities and agencies otherwise track assets and water quality across disconnected tools, which hurts data integrity.

The platform gathers the programs and data a team needs to manage compliance from start to finish. That includes asset records and service line inventories, sampling schedules, lab results, resident communications, and program reporting. Programs run on it include service line inventories, monitoring, school and childcare sampling, backflow, consumer request sampling, and statewide 3Ts programs. It is built to fit an existing data ecosystem, with lab integrations and APIs for syncing locations, assets, and records. Most utility and state clients onboard in weeks, with the company handling data migration, configuration, and training.

Public water systems, state drinking water programs, schools, childcare facilities, and local governments are named as the customers. The company states that every module is built with current security standards and role-based permissions meant to meet or exceed state and federal program requirements. Its stated mission is to protect public health by giving communities confidence in their water. before.name: Unite Us
before.description: Social care coordination network connecting health and social service referrals for govs and payers - exhibited at MESC 2026

hiring.note: Strategic Sales Director - West Co (United States)

paragraphs: Unite Us sells software and data infrastructure for coordinating whole-person care across healthcare, government and community-based organizations. Its named audiences include public health and human services agencies. Managed care and Medicaid plans are also on that list.

The core product is a closed-loop referral system for sending and receiving electronic social care referrals within a network of community partners. Staff can run social needs screenings, after which the platform automatically suggests resources or referrals. A secure chat feature lets users at partner organizations message each other about shared referrals, cases and clients. Integrations let organizations share resources and send referrals without leaving their own system.

Alongside referrals, the company sells predictive analytics meant to predict long-term risks and measure impact. Its Population Insights tool combines social, economic, environmental and health information with modeling to identify at-risk populations. It also automates payments to community-based organizations. The company states that it partnered with Presbyterian Health Plan to create New Mexico's first statewide closed-loop referral system.

before.name: AssetWorks
before.description: Fleet, fuel, and enterprise asset management software for governments and universities (Volaris) - exhibited at NAFA I&E 2026

paragraphs: AssetWorks builds software, hardware and consulting services for organizations whose work centers on assets and infrastructure. The buyers run commercial fleets or public infrastructure and want to control operating costs.

The fleet system, FleetFocus, is a central platform for maintenance, asset lifecycle tracking, fueling and reporting. A companion product, FuelFocus, watches fuel levels and transactions in real time so discrepancies surface immediately. A mobile extension puts inventory and work order management in the hands of technicians and storekeepers. A Power BI connection supports custom dashboards, advanced reporting and lifecycle analytics on the same data.

The company puts its own history at more than 40 years and the home page counts over 1,000 organizations using the products. Listed offices include one in Berwyn, Pennsylvania and a San Antonio location for education facilities, real estate and planning software. Case studies describe a county internal services department managing roughly 20,000 vehicles. Another covers a regional public transit agency running a fleet of more than 427 active vehicles.

before.name: Gainwell Technologies
before.description: Medicaid MMIS, pharmacy and program integrity systems for states - exhibited at AIRA 2026

paragraphs: Gainwell sells the systems that run state Medicaid programs, tying together claims and encounter management, provider contracts, capitation and member benefits. Pharmacy is a separate line aimed at medication management and the total cost of care. Another line helps payers avoid and recover improper payments while detecting fraud.

The claims, encounters and financials module is presented as a modernization step built on automation and interoperability. An EDI gateway lets providers submit all their claims centrally, which the company says simplifies Medicaid billing. Its analytics platform is shaped around Medicaid data and federal compliance requirements. Provider management can be modernized in phases with Provider Flex, replaced outright with Provider+, or extended across state lines through a cross-state provider network.

The analytics page cites 52 state Medicaid programs. A case study on the home page covers provider enrollment in Vermont. That case study claims an 87.5% reduction in enrollment processing time. Its centralized credentialing platform is described as NCQA accredited. The company points to longstanding experience keeping Medicaid programs running with accurate data for decision making.

before.name: EarthDaily
before.description: Satellite earth-observation imagery and change-detection analytics for agencies, insurance, and ag - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: EarthDaily is a geospatial company selling satellite imagery and analytics to governments and enterprises whose work depends on the physical world. Its stated purpose is daily monitoring of the earth's surface for broad area change detection.

Raw satellite data is captured through a purpose-built constellation and ground system. That data is then processed, calibrated and quality-controlled into scientifically accurate image products. One product, AiRD, is analysis-ready observation data engineered from the start for machine learning. Its spectral bands are calibrated to match Sentinel-2 and Landsat specifications. A second product, Maritime, is tuned for fast processing and detection of anomalies at sea.

The company focuses its products on agriculture, financial services, infrastructure, forestry and governments. Security organizations, analytics providers and coastal agencies are the named audience for the maritime data. A company timeline states that it was created in partnership with Antarctica Capital. The same timeline lists an acquisition of Descartes Labs and funding from Trinity Capital. It also records more than 500 agreements signed. A news item states the company achieved CEOS Analysis Ready Data compliance.

before.description: Source-to-pay eProcurement suite with dedicated public sector and higher-ed verticals - exhibited at NACUBO 2026, GFOA 2026

paragraphs: JAGGAER sells procurement software that carries an organization from sourcing a supplier through contracts, invoicing and payment. It aims at complex buyers, and names manufacturing, public sector and higher education among the industries it is built for.

The unified product is JAGGAER One, which brings source to pay and procure to pay into a single system. Public sector workflows called out include cooperative purchasing and contract vehicles. Grant-funded and project-based procurement is listed as another. Integration runs through pre-built connectors to SAP, Oracle, Workday, Infor, NetSuite and other business applications. An embedded AI assistant is governed by stated rules, among them that customer data is never used to train foundation or derivative models. Data is stored and processed only within selected regions. The AI framework claims alignment with ISO 42001 compliance standards.

The company states that over 1,300 enterprises worldwide use it to manage $2.9 trillion in annual spend. A customer panel names the State University of New York among higher education users. Another names the University of Virginia. That panel reports invoice processing reduced from hours to about one minute.

before.name: Better Impact
before.description: Volunteer management software for parks, libraries and government agencies - exhibited at Animal Care Expo 2026

paragraphs: Better Impact sells volunteer management software used by organizations to automate scheduling, track hours and communicate with volunteers. A membership product manages member profiles, automates renewals and supports engagement across the member lifecycle. A client product works alongside the volunteer system to coordinate volunteer and client interactions.

Coordinators get self-scheduling, automated communications, online training modules and one-click reports. The broader promise is streamlined scheduling, less administrative burden and hour tracking in one system. A separate offering called Volunteer Link is built for corporate social responsibility teams that want to engage employees, strengthen community partnerships and measure impact. It gives employees access to over 200,000 volunteer opportunities across the US and Canada. Reports come export-ready for ESG disclosures, board presentations and annual CSR summaries.

The company says more than 85,000 organizations use its software. Its published case studies include a hospice rethinking how it coordinates care. In March 2026 it announced the acquisition of Get Connected by Galaxy Digital, another volunteer management software provider. Leadership is listed as chief executive Houston Goodwin and president Tim Sarazen.

paragraphs: PowerSchool sells software that school districts run from home to classroom to central office, covering the records, communication, and back-office work of running a school system. The company says its software reaches over 60 million students in 90 countries.

The student information side pulls scattered records into one accurate student record, so staff and families are working from the same source. Teaching and learning products sit alongside it, among them a learning management system. For the central office, finance, human resources, and operations are brought into one connected system. A separate data practice centralizes information that would otherwise sit in district silos.

PowerBuddy, the company's AI assistant, is described as built for students, families, teachers, and administrators. It is also pitched at IT staff and data analysts working with district data. PowerSchool states that PowerBuddy won a 2024 GESS Education Award. In districts already using its products, the company says teachers are reclaiming at least 10 hours a week.

before.name: Gaggle
before.description: Monitors school email/docs for self-harm and threat signals - exhibited at CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Gaggle sells student safety services to schools, with a stated mission of ensuring the safety and well-being of students and schools through people and technology. Its core product uses machine learning and trained safety experts to analyze student-created content in school-issued accounts and devices.

A web filter blocks inappropriate content and automatically categorizes new sites as it scans them. A therapy service connects students with licensed mental health professionals for weekly teletherapy sessions. A round-the-clock service called ReachOut gives students direct access to confidential care whenever they need support. An archiving product stores files and communications in one searchable, cloud-based system so districts can meet compliance obligations.

The company says it has been supporting student safety and well-being for more than 20 years. Its founder started the company as a secure student email provider in 1998. It describes itself as the pioneer in helping K-12 districts manage student safety on school-provided technology. The home page puts its reach at over 1,500 K-12 districts, and one case study describes a district choosing the therapy service to meet growing student mental health needs.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© Copyright 2026 Concur Technologies, Inc. All rights reserved." Fetched https://www.concur.com (curl with browser UA, HTTP 200, 170KB; WebFetch got 403 so I used curl). Page title: "Spend Management Software for Travel, Expense, Invoice | SAP Concur", canonical https://www.concur.com/. Rule 3 check PASSED: this is NOT sap.com. It is the brand's own domain, copyright held by Concur Technologies, Inc., with its own product navigation (Concur Expense, Concur Travel, Concur Invoice, Concur Request, Concur TripLink) and its own solutions nav including "Government", "Government contracting" and "State & local governments". Matches the description (travel, expense and invoice software). CAVEAT the board operator should know: https://www.concur.com/careers 302s off-domain to https://jobs.sap.com/search (unfiltered, all-SAP job search). So the URL is correct as the company's identity page, but any scraper that follows the careers link will inherit SAP's entire global req list rather than SAP Concur roles. Recommend the record carry the site but not auto-scrape jobs.sap.com/search unfiltered.

paragraphs: SAP Concur sells software for handling business expenses, travel and supplier invoices. The pitch is a single platform that gives a company better visibility and control over spending. The company says the products are designed for businesses of all sizes.

Concur Expense is cloud-based expense management software covering the stretch from submitting a receipt to being reimbursed. Key details are pulled from receipts and card transactions automatically, so staff key in less data by hand. Submitted expenses are checked against company rules before they move any further along. A companion product handles the step before money is spent, automating requests and approvals against travel and expense policy. A separate audit product applies machine learning to fraud and compliance risks both before and after reimbursement.

The platform is meant to sit on top of systems a customer already runs, with hundreds of pre-built connectors and open APIs for anything custom. The company says its models are trained on one of the largest expense datasets in the industry and improve as more transactions pass through. Expense pricing is published in US dollars and varies with monthly commitment. The top tier is set aside for businesses that need the most advanced capabilities.

before.name: Catalis
before.description: PE-backed govtech rollup: courts, land records, tax/CAMA, licensing, and citizen payments - exhibited at APPA Probation 2026, IAAO 2026, NASWA 2025, 3CMA 2026

paragraphs: Catalis sells software and payment services to government agencies. One line covers tax and CAMA work, supporting local billing, collection and management alongside appraisal and assessing. Another handles courts and land records, automating filings and widening public access to justice.

On the resident-facing side, the company offers municipalities a package covering website design, development, hosting and maintenance. Its notification tool distributes messages by email, text, social media and voice phone lines. Administrators can also automate alerts drawn from Alert Ready, NOAA and IPAWS. Permitting and licensing tools let residents apply online and route the reviews to staff.

The stated customer base spans municipalities, counties, states and federal agencies. The website design team says it has been doing this work since 1999. It claims more than 1,000 municipal websites built to date. The notification platform is described as incorporating 20 years of municipal experience.

before.description: Cloud treasury: debt management, GASB 87/96 lease accounting, and cash management for gov finance - exhibited at NACUBO 2026, GFOA 2026

paragraphs: DebtBook helps finance teams manage debt, cash, leases and subscriptions with cloud-based software built for governments and nonprofits. The buyers it names are state and local government, higher education and healthcare organizations.

The debt product consolidates treasury and debt accounting data in a single, cloud-accessible location. It also tracks and completes continuing disclosure filings. Cash management is aimed at full control over cash flow to minimize risk, reduce costs and improve financial performance. A lease module targets GASB 87 compliance while simplifying lease management and accounting. Another covers GASB 96 and subscription-based IT arrangements. A contracts module collects post-signature contracts across departments.

The about page states a base of 2,100 customers nationwide. The company says its platform is designed by former government and nonprofit finance professionals who spent decades in that world. It tells buyers that implementation leaves a team fully operational in 90 days or less.

before.name: VODA.ai
before.description: AI pipe-failure prediction for main replacement planning - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: VODA.ai sells decision support software to water utilities. The point is helping engineers decide which pipes to replace, assess, monitor or investigate next.

Projects start from data a utility already keeps, such as GIS records, pipe attributes, historical break records, work orders and service line information. Machine learning then flags pipes with an elevated likelihood of failure, including ones that have never broken. Utilities do not need clean records to begin. Initial model outputs, risk scores and prioritized watch lists are often available within three to six months. The same approach supports lead service line programs, sorting likely galvanized lines and prioritizing field verification before replacement work.

The company is Boston-based and was founded in 2017. It says it has worked in 31 states and eight countries and analyzed more than a million miles of pipe. Executives from 78 water utilities at the Smart Water Summit picked it as best smart water solution. Published case studies include lead compliance work in Rock Hill, South Carolina.

paragraphs: Fort Orange Press is a printing and mailing company, family-owned and operated since 1905. It handles the production, printing, and mailing of essential documents for federal, state, county, and local governments. Election ballot printing and mailing services are a central part of that work.

Services run from planning, design, printing, and variable data-processing through inserting, finishing, fulfillment, mailing, shipping, tracking, and reporting. For elections, the company has developed tools that can better format and prepare voter databases. Printing and inserting pass through a security crosscheck system that uses barcodes and multiple cameras to match all components of the ballot package. A proprietary reporting platform gives clients real-time production and USPS tracking data. That platform also lets voters look up and track their ballot through the mail stream.

Beyond ballots, government agencies order property tax statements, appraisal notices, utility bills, and business licenses. Work is produced from a manufacturing facility in Albany, NY. The company calls itself a proud union shop. It also describes itself as a second-generation business. It states that it is SOC 2 Type II compliant, tested annually. Since 2012 it has held a G7 Master Qualified status for proofing and press equipment.

quote.text: Partner with states to uphold Democracy by ensuring that every ballot is printed and mailed according to the highest standards of accuracy, security and transparency.

before.name: Deckard Technologies
before.description: Rentalscape: AI parcel data for short-term rental compliance and tax recovery in 400+ jurisdictions - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Deckard Technologies sells software that local governments use to deal with residential property problems in their jurisdictions. The products cover short-term rentals, long-term rentals, and foreclosed and vacant properties.

The short-term rental product monitors a jurisdiction by analyzing more than 15 million listings from over 10,000 rental websites in real time. The vacancy and foreclosure side watches court records and mortgage reassignments instead. Other tools handle transient occupancy tax filings and payments. A published case study describes a city adopting the Rentalscape platform in 2024 with a structured letter outreach campaign, in which the vendor develops the mailing list and generates, prints and mails the letters to identified hosts.

The company was founded in May 2018 by Greg Rose, Jess Flanagan and Tony Moriarty, starting in both Australia and the United States. It now keeps offices in the United States, Colombia and Australia. Its own count of customers is more than 500 jurisdictions worldwide. The company timeline records several seed rounds, among them a Seed-4 raise.

quote.text: aims to empower local governments with the data, insights, and tools they need to maximize compliance and unlock vital public revenue.

before.name: FlashVote
before.description: Statistically valid rapid resident surveys - community input in 48 hours - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, 3CMA 2026

paragraphs: FlashVote sells rapid opinion surveys to local governments, promising statistically valid public input in 48 hours on any issue. The company claims its professionally designed scientific surveys are up to 90% faster, easier and more affordable for local governments.

The service works by getting large samples of representative residents to answer professionally designed questions. It reaches those residents by email, text and phone. Results are reported 48 hours after a survey launches. To keep outsiders from skewing the numbers, the system filters results by physical addresses.

The company says it works with local governments in more than 30 states. Its customers are described as counties, cities, towns and special districts. FlashVote is the first good-government service offered by the Governance Sciences Group.

before.name: Envision Technology Partners, Inc.
before.description: WebIZ immunization information system for state and local immunization registries, now sold as part of InductiveHealth's public health platform - exhibited at AIRA 2026
before.source: research pass: HHS conference exhibitor research 2026-08-25

paragraphs: WebIZ is an immunization information system sold to state and local government public health agencies. The registry is now offered inside InductiveHealth's public health platform. It is built to meet CDC standards for tracking and administering immunizations in any jurisdiction.

The system follows vaccine inventory from ordering through delivery and administration. Clinic record systems send administered doses straight into the registry, which cuts duplicate entry. Embedded dashboards report coverage rates by ZIP code, vaccine type, age group and provider. School entry rules are configured once for a state and then applied to every student and grade. Residents pull their own immunization records from a secure portal with multi-factor authentication.

The company says the product has served more than 20 jurisdictions across two decades. Under a shared development model, one jurisdiction's funded enhancement reaches the rest in the next monthly release. InductiveHealth dates its founding to 2013. It works with federal, state, tribal, local and territorial jurisdictions on disease surveillance. Staff include epidemiologists and public health experts alongside engineers and technologists.

paragraphs: Palo Alto Networks sells cybersecurity products across network, cloud, security operations, AI and identity. The company says more than 70,000 customers use them, backed by its Unit 42 threat intelligence group.

Its network security platform monitors, analyzes and prevents sophisticated threats in real time with less complexity. An identity platform adds a control plane that discovers risk, applies privilege dynamically and governs access from first session to last. In a May 2026 release the company announced it had closed its acquisition of Portkey, described as a pioneer in AI gateways. That gateway watches token usage against runaway costs and adds runtime protection against malicious or unintended AI behavior.

Customer stories are filed by industry, and state and local government is one of the categories. One story describes VINCI standardising on Cortex XDR across 200,000 endpoints worldwide. The company runs executive briefing centers where customers meet its executives and product leaders. Briefings run from half a day to several days and are tailored to the visiting organization. Palo Alto Networks is listed on the Nasdaq under PANW.

before.name: Samsara
before.description: IoT telematics and video safety for government fleets (public co) - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, PRIMA 2026, NAFA I&E 2026

paragraphs: Samsara sells a platform to organizations that run vehicles and equipment, pitched on improving safety, lowering costs and changing how operations work. For fleets it covers live GPS tracking, vehicle diagnostics, fuel analytics and compliance reporting. The company presents this as one platform working across every part of an operation rather than separate tools.

Its cameras pair safety detections with video that managers can pull on demand. The company says the system watches for drowsiness, distraction, tailgating and forward collision risk. It states that these are caught in real time and trigger an in-cab alert before a manager is involved. A multicamera option adds up to four auxiliary HD feeds for visibility around the vehicle. A separate site product brings third-party cameras at facilities into a cloud dashboard for onboarding and troubleshooting.

The camera pages list transportation and logistics, field services, construction, public sector and essential services among the industries served. For school districts the company describes arm-mounted cameras that enforce school bus stop-arm compliance during pickups and drop-offs. Among its customer stories is one saying the City of El Paso recovered $1.3M in assets and reduced accidents by 29%. A site camera gateway is listed as compliant with the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2019.

before.name: Apptegy
before.description: Thrillshare K-12 communications: district websites, apps, notifications, branding - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Apptegy sells a communications platform to K-12 school districts, gathering the tools and training that district staff use to reach families. The pitch to district leaders is that the school brand stays at the front of every message.

Districts get a branded website managed through a drag-and-drop editor with page permissions for contributors and analytics. A district-branded mobile app for iOS and Android carries school information and two-way messaging for families. Alerts go out by email, push notification, SMS, text-to-speech, voice call and social media from one place. Automated translation is offered for more than 100 languages, and websites are built to meet WCAG 2.1 A and AA standards.

The home page states that 5,273 districts have switched to the platform for their communications. Beyond software the company publishes SchoolCEO magazine, with guides and original research for district leaders. One study listed there was done jointly with NSPRA on the relationship between superintendents and school communicators.

before.name: Deledao
before.description: Real-time AI content filtering and self-harm detection for schools - exhibited at CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Deledao sells web filtering to K-12 schools, built on patented technology the company says analyzes each webpage as a human would. The product line later grew to cover student safety and classroom management.

The filter blurs, mutes, and screens inappropriate images and video frame by frame. It detects gaming behavior from keyboard and mouse activity without logging keystrokes. Proxy sites students use to bypass filtering are caught automatically. Teachers get visibility into student tabs or screens. Websites can be allowed or blocked by group or by individual student. The wellness product looks for cyberbullying, self-harm, and toxic language across platforms. High-risk alerts receive human review and escalation to the district.

The company names Shuang Ji as its chief executive. Its first product, a web filter using real-time AI, launched in 2019. It says it now supports schools in the United States, Canada, Europe, New Zealand, and Australia. Case studies on the site describe schools adopting the filter for CIPA compliance and student safety.

paragraphs: FIDO Tech sells water leak detection built on artificial intelligence to utilities, municipalities and businesses. The company describes itself as a global water technology company.

before.name: GovPilot
before.description: Cloud permitting, licensing, code enforcement, and GIS workflows for local governments - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: GovPilot sells cloud-based management software to municipal and county government departments. The pitch is to put a government's data and its departments on a single platform. Local governments of all sizes have deployed it.

A government picks the modules it needs, then unifies data across departments and lets residents report concerns, apply, pay and track requests online. The catalog runs to more than 125 templated digital modules, with mobile apps and a GIS map on the same cloud platform. A parcel-level view called PropertyProfile shows records held by different departments about the same property. Two mobile apps, GovAlert and GovInspect, accompany the digital forms and automated workflows.

Case studies on the site cover work such as building and construction permitting. Short-term rental property registration is another documented use. Pricing is set by population and by the number of modules a government selects. The company says it has been named a GovTech 100 company for eight consecutive years. It also points buyers to its Capterra reviews from government users.

before.name: Buddi
before.description: UK-based electronic monitoring tags for justice and corrections agencies - exhibited at APPA Probation 2026

paragraphs: Buddi supplies electronic monitoring tags and software to criminal justice agencies, with solutions developed alongside police, prisons, probation and local government authorities. The company says its offender monitoring supports supervision, rehabilitation and the protection of local communities.

The system pairs a web-based monitoring platform called Eagle with modular hardware in the Buddi Smart Tag family. AlcoTag puts alcohol monitoring and GPS tracking in a single compact device. A radio frequency product handles curfew compliance in real time. There is also a domestic abuse monitoring product sold to authorities. Field staff work through Eagle Mobile and Eagle Installer on Android and iOS devices.

Buddi was founded in 2004. It reports over 250 clients globally, with products designed and manufactured in the UK. Customers are listed throughout Europe, the United States of America, Latin America and Asia Pacific. The company operates as a brand within Big Technologies Group plc. Its history page records a flotation on the London Stock Exchange's AIM market under the ticker AIM:BIG.

paragraphs: Workday sells cloud software that runs human resources, finance and IT processes for an organization. Its human capital management line is a suite of HR products meant to work as one. The company says the software is built for organizations of all sizes. A packaged version is aimed at midsize businesses.

Inside the HR suite sit time tracking, absence, scheduling and payroll. Payroll is automated to pay workers accurately and in line with local rules. Recruiting covers the full talent acquisition lifecycle. The company argues the value comes from a single data model and one codeline rather than systems stitched together. It claims native localization for more than 175 countries.

More than 10,000 organizations use Workday, including a majority of the Fortune 500 by the company's own count. Customer stories on the site include Panera. Workday also cites Gartner recognition for cloud HCM suites.

before.name: ClassLink
before.description: Single sign-on, rostering and usage analytics for public school districts - exhibited at CoSN 2026, EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: ClassLink sells identity, access and analytics software to school systems that have accumulated more educational technology than they can easily manage. The best known piece is LaunchPad, a single sign-on portal that puts a student or teacher's apps behind one login with multi-factor authentication.

Behind the portal, OneSync handles account creation and management and is pitched at tech teams losing hundreds of hours to that work by hand. Roster Server delivers class rosters and carries 1EdTech certification for interoperability. An add-on called DataGuard masks personally identifiable fields before roster data leaves for a vendor. A separate product, ThreatScan, watches the dark web for district credentials that have already been exposed. Analytics reports digital engagement from the district level down to the individual student.

The company says over 3,000 school systems use its products. It describes itself as the single sign-on platform chosen by over 25 million users. ClassLink states that it connects to more than 6,000 digital learning resources.

quote.text: Identity first schools are safer, faster, and easier to run

provenance.quote: From access and analytics to cybersecurity and identity management, ClassLink’s affordable and reliable solutions help you use technology in ways that promote and support learning.
LaunchPad provides quick SSO access to a personalized portal of digital apps and resources while protecting sensitive data with secure Multi-Factor Authentication
OneSync takes the guesswork out of managing student data and saves tech teams from spending hundreds of hours on manual account creation and management
Roster Server is 1EdTech Certified for interoperability
DataGuard allows schools to mask and replace key PII fields with meaningless letter scrambles before sending data to a vendor through ClassLink Roster Server.
ThreatScan automatically scans the dark web for compromised accounts linked to your school district.
ClassLink Analytics and Analytics+ present this data from the district level, down to the individual student
See why over 3,000 school systems love learning with ClassLink.
the SSO platform chosen by over 25 million users
ClassLink connects to more than 6,000 digital learning resources

paragraphs: CITIZ3N Government Solutions builds modular platforms for government agencies that oversee Affordable Care Act marketplaces, Medicaid, health and human services programs, and health benefits for government employees. It is a subsidiary of Softheon and one of three brands in that portfolio.

There are two platforms: MARKETPLACE, a set of stand-alone modules meant to integrate into marketplace exchanges for government, and VERIFY, which handles eligibility determinations and combats fraud, waste, and abuse in Medicaid and HHS programs. Both are delivered as cloud-based software as a service. The architecture is cloud-native and uses an enterprise service bus for communication and interoperability between systems. The company says the platforms scale to more than a million transactions per day.

The buyers are local, state, and federal agencies. The company states compliance with HIPAA and regular security audits against frameworks such as NIST 800-53 and MARS-E 2.0. Its annual audits are listed as SOC 1 and 2, PCI AOC, a NACHA audit, penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and code security scanning. Support is described as implementation assistance, training programs, and ongoing technical help.

before.name: BlueConduit
before.description: Machine learning lead service line inventory and prediction for water utilities - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: BlueConduit sells predictive modeling tools to water systems that need to manage risk and make data-driven decisions about their distribution assets. The customers are municipalities and water utilities.

One product builds community-specific models that pinpoint high-risk lead and galvanized service lines, which lets a utility classify its inventory and prioritize replacements. Another scores every main segment in a network for likelihood and consequence of failure. A third uses statistical models to confirm the absence of lead in a water system. The company says model processes, important features, and performance metrics are always shared with customers. Output is integrated with Esri ArcGIS.

The work started at the University of Michigan, where faculty and student researchers saw a use for data science in removing toxic lead from the water supply. In Flint the company used predictive analytics to identify where to dig for lead service lines. A published case study describes Des Moines Water Works classifying unknown service lines and reducing uncertainty by 75% in six months. BlueConduit cites ongoing relationships with EPA and state regulators. Its stated mission is to empower communities to prioritize health and sustainability through data science.

before.name: LeadsOnline
before.description: Investigation database: pawn/secondhand transactions plus ballistics ID for agencies - exhibited at Michigan Sheriffs Association 2026

paragraphs: LeadsOnline sells investigative software and forensic tools to law enforcement agencies, aimed at solving crimes faster, recovering stolen property, and building cases that hold up in court. Its two main lines are digital evidence analysis and crime gun intelligence, and the company says the tools are built to work together. The company says it works alongside law enforcement worldwide.

On the digital side, the tools turn raw data, from stolen property records to digital evidence, into answers an agency can act on. Cellular and social media analysis links call records, GPS, and activity data through visualizations meant to identify suspects. When a firearm or cartridge case turns up at a scene, the ballistics products give forensic examiners a way to link firearms to crimes and connect evidence across agencies. Triage tools identify the number of firearms and calibers involved and preserve trace evidence for later steps.

One case study describes a detective at the Plano, TX Police Department recovering a stolen iPhone and obtaining a warrant for the suspect using LeadsOnline. Another, from the Tyler, TX Police Department, credits CellHawk analysis with leading to the arrest of a murder suspect. In the testimonials, Detective Jeff German of the Joliet Police Department says NightHawk helped find evidence in millions of lines of data. The company puts its reach at thousands of agencies and millions of investigations.

quote.text: We exist to help global law enforcement agencies advance cases faster with our unique data, well-designed technology, and exceptional teamwork.

before.name: Electro Scan
before.description: Machine-based pipe defect and leak assessment for municipal sewer and water - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Electro Scan sells leak detection and lead pipe location work for water and sewer systems. The company says municipal sewer utilities and sewer contractors use it to pin down the location, measurement and flow of defects inside a pipe before a repair or replacement job.

The method rests on a simple claim: pipe defects that leak water also leak electricity, so a defect shows up whether or not it happens to be leaking during the inspection. A low voltage conductivity probe travels through the pipe at 45 to 60 feet per minute, locating and measuring defects as it goes. Crews can then create summary and detail level reports for a team to review. The flagship probe is built for gravity mains between 6 and 30 inches in diameter, and the company says agencies and contractors use it worldwide.

Electro Scan lists ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management systems. Its case studies page includes a North American benchmark study comparing closed-circuit television inspection with focused electrode leak location on gravity sewer mains. Other write-ups describe a Florida utility dealing with excessive inflow and infiltration in its gravity collection system.

paragraphs: AchieveIt sells software for moving a written plan into measurable progress. It pitches itself to public agencies and other organizations that find performance hard to measure. The idea behind it is connecting people, plans and data in one place.

A plan is structured to match whatever methodology a customer already uses, from pillars and objectives down to initiatives, KPIs and milestones. Update requests then go out on a chosen cadence, asking owners for status, percent complete, commentary and metric values that flow into dashboards and roll-up reports. A tree view shows how each item in a plan lines up with the rest. Custom dashboards can display information drawn from any plan in the organization. A multi-plan view lets a customer filter, segment and drill into progress across everything at once.

AchieveIt says strategy consultants and customer success managers work alongside each customer. Onboarding, training and hands-on help come with the move away from manual tracking. The site sorts prospects by sector so a buyer can see how the software fits their way of working. One page groups its public sector claims under a heading about proven results.

paragraphs: Clearview AI sells facial recognition software that law enforcement agencies use to generate leads and identify suspects, witnesses and victims. The company states its mission as reducing crime, fraud and risk, and it also points the technology at national security and military defense. Development is U.S.-based, the site says, with certification for data security and cybersecurity policies.

The company states that its law enforcement database holds more than 70 billion images. It says the model was trained on the largest and most diverse dataset. The homepage adds that the algorithm has been tested by NIST and performs in challenging photographic conditions. In a company blog post, Clearview says its algorithm achieved greater than 99 percent accuracy across all demographics in NIST's 1:1 FRVT test.

Success stories listed on the site include the Miami Police Department locating a fleeing homicide suspect. Another describes the Hernando County Sheriff's Office solving a case the company says could have gone cold. A press release dated July 1, 2026 announces that Clearview GovCloud reached FedRAMP In Process designation at the High Impact Level. Another, dated August 11, 2026, notes a third consecutive year on the Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies.

paragraphs: Off Duty Management administers off-duty work programs for law enforcement agencies, their officers, and community businesses. Its OfficerTRAK® platform handles Police, Fire, or EMS off-duty job requests. Officers clock in and out, view job history, and get real-time notifications in the OfficerTRAK® app. The businesses hiring officers request shifts, receive invoices, and pay online through a portal.

Off Duty Management charges nothing to agencies and officers. It takes on the financial risk of late or non-payment by the off-duty employer, and says officers and agencies are paid weekly regardless of customer payment status. The company reports partnering with over 200 primary agencies and 300 backup agencies across the nation.

In Arizona, it deploys trained SSO officers across jurisdictions to help school districts fill School Safety Officer shifts. The Arizona Department of Education sets a curriculum officers must complete to be eligible for those shifts. Superintendent Tom Horne extended that partnership with Off Duty Management through 2026. Retired Austin Police Chief Brian Manley joined the company as President.

It is sold into healthcare, higher education, K-12, state and local government, and enterprise.

Each vendor is vetted through what the company calls a proprietary onboarding system before a payment is approved. That onboarding sits on top of a payee network the site puts at more than 1.5 million authenticated payees. Compliance work is automated alongside it, covering sanctions checks, continuous monitoring, W9 and 1099 information, and audit trails. The site states that ACH payments made through the platform are indemnified, with additional coverage available.

Published case studies include the University of North Texas. Another describes a county that fell victim to a $2.5M scam after a request to change vendor banking details. The company says it offers a payments security warranty for fraudulent payments. Its about page introduces a leadership team including a co-founder whose patent work in data management led to the founding of the company.

paragraphs: FieldWare sells cloud-based software for judicial professionals, community supervision teams, and public safety personnel at city, county, and state agencies. Its modules cover pretrial, parole, and probation supervision, workforce management with a companion mobile app, and court notification and attendance.

The CourtNotify suite centralizes subpoena processes for courts, prosecutors, defense attorneys, public safety officials, and civilian witnesses, and can serve one agency or unite several. A companion CourtNotify mobile app for iOS and Android carries court notifications in real time and uses geofencing to record officer check in and check out times at courthouses.

FieldWare hosts in an Azure Government environment it describes as FedRAMP-compliant and runs continuous BreachLock penetration testing. A testimonial attributed to Lt. before.name: Just Appraised
before.description: AI workflow for county assessors: deed processing, exemptions, taxpayer communication (YC S17) - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, IAAO 2026

paragraphs: Just Appraised sells AI software that local government offices use to get through their paperwork. The buyers are county assessor and clerk offices, and the company says more than 300 counties in over 30 states use it. Some workflows are built for particular states, including Prop 19C in California.

The deeds product automatically imports deeds and recorded documents from the clerk's office. AI then reads those documents and extracts data fields, populating the county's CAMA system. A taxpayer portal lets residents submit forms online, or lets clerks scan paper forms in. Reviewed form data then pushes into the CAMA at the press of a button. A valuations product structures income and expense submissions into searchable financials.

The deeds page names Cobb County, Georgia as a customer. Williamson CAD in Texas is also listed there. Montgomery CAD in Texas appears on the forms page. Other testimonials are attributed without naming the office, such as a Director of Deeds at a Florida county.

paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. The home page announces the completed acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which the company describes as a counter-drone technology firm.

before.name: EagleView
before.description: Aerial imagery and property data analytics for county assessors, GIS, and insurers - exhibited at IAAO 2026

paragraphs: EagleView sells aerial imagery and property data drawn from an archive the company puts at more than 3.5 billion high-resolution images. Public agencies are one audience, with the imagery aimed at tax assessment, zoning enforcement, emergency response and infrastructure planning.

The subscription imagery product refreshes annually at 2-inch resolution, with an option to upgrade. The company says its 1-inch imagery carries nine times more detail than 3-inch imagery. Captures include straight-down orthogonal views for mapping and measurement and angled oblique views of building sides. A separate archive holds more than 25 years of imagery covering 96 percent of the United States population. New content is added daily, with annual refreshes across metro areas and high-growth regions. Customers view imagery in a browser tool or pull it through API connections into GIS, CAD, CAMA or analytics systems.
The site states that 20 of the top 20 insurers rely on the company. Governments, insurers, utilities, AEC firms and environmental professionals are named as users of the imagery archive.

before.name: Civica
before.description: Regulatory, licensing and planning software for public sector authorities - exhibited at PLA 2026

paragraphs: Civica makes software that public bodies use to deliver critical services to citizens around the world. It says over 6,000 public bodies use that software to help provide critical services to over 100 million citizens.

Its solutions span local and central government, health and community care, housing and social care, libraries and education, and regulatory and compliance services. The company describes integrated cloud platforms that automate workflows, support data-driven decision-making and reduce operational costs. Named products include Spydus, a library management system. Civica also sells master data management for state and local government. It says it is an approved supplier on major government frameworks.

Civica was established in 2001 and describes itself as one of the UK's largest software companies. Its team has grown to 5,500 colleagues, one-third of whom have worked in the sectors it serves. Acquisitions are part of the strategy, with more than 37 completed in the last 10 years. The company reports delivery in the UK, Australia, New Zealand, India, North America and Europe. Customer stories on its site include delivering a single citizen view for the State of Alaska.

before.name: HHAeXchange
before.description: EVV and homecare management for state Medicaid and MCO programs - exhibited at Healthcare IT Connect 2026

paragraphs: HHAeXchange sells homecare software built as one platform connecting providers, payers, and caregivers. Homecare agencies rely on it to be more efficient in their day-to-day operations.

A flexible electronic visit verification system with a GPS mobile app handles caregiver clock-ins and clock-outs. On the revenue side, agencies validate patient pre-authorizations, monitor authorization usage, and stay on top of expirations. The CarePay payroll product runs on the same visit data, so shift differentials, wage parity, and blended overtime calculate automatically with tax filing on every paycheck. A separate offering for intellectual and developmental disability agencies covers documentation, billing, care coordination, and staff operations.

The company states it serves over 32,000 US providers, more than 180 managed care organizations, and 30 state Medicaid programs. Payroll and employee data is encrypted to bank-level standards that the company says meet or exceed HIPAA and SOC 2.

paragraphs: Averhealth provides substance use monitoring and treatment solutions. Its work is built around the needs of criminal justice-based substance use monitoring programs.

Samples ship to the company's laboratory in St. Louis the same day, and results come back the next business day after testing. The laboratory is led by a PhD toxicologist. The company states that the lab is CAP-FDT, CLIA, and DEA accredited. Testing covers more than 1,500 substances in urine, oral fluid, hair, and sweat. Its software, Aversys, supports automated, individualized treatment and supervision programs in a paper-free form.

The company describes itself as more than just a drug testing provider. Its stated goal is to support customers as they work to drive sustainable behavioral changes. Averhealth, Avertest, and Aversys are registered trademarks or service marks of Avertest, LLC.

before.name: Cyvl
before.description: Vehicle-mounted lidar + AI for pavement condition, sidewalk ADA, and street asset inventories - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Cyvl sells a sensor and software platform that shows cities what needs attention across every street, sidewalk and asset. Counties are a second audience, using it to keep sprawling road networks current.

A city team mounts the LiDAR and 360 degree imaging rig on a vehicle it already owns, and the drive itself does the collecting. Each drive becomes pavement scores, asset inventories and a ranked list of needs. The results live in one shared platform for public works, city leaders and residents. Coverage reaches past pavement to sidewalks and curb ramps assessed for an ADA baseline.

Cities and towns are described as capturing their entire right-of-way in a single pass. Counties are described as using the record to hold developers and utilities accountable for the condition they leave roads in. The company says Atlanta moved downtown pavement from 64 to 75, from fair to good, while potholes fell 60 percent.

quote.text: Scan the network, turn current conditions into a plan, show what changed, then repeat so the city’s picture never goes stale.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

before.name: Holly
before.description: AI classification & compensation for local gov HR: job specs, salary benchmarking (Harvard-born) - exhibited at GFOA 2026, PSHRA 2026

paragraphs: Holly sells an AI-powered classification and compensation platform for government human resources departments. It is built for HR teams that manage hundreds of classifications, compete for talent and negotiate pay.

The platform scores an existing job spec for clarity, completeness and equity, calling out outdated duties, dense sentences or qualifications that screen out strong candidates. Its similarity scoring compares actual job duties across more than 45,000 public sector roles rather than titles alone. Drafts move through subject matter expert, HR, management and final approval steps, with reviewers commenting the way they would in a shared document. Market data is turned into recommendations for council meetings and union negotiations.

The users are local government HR staff, and one published case study follows Long Beach, California, a port city of about 450,000 residents. Its workforce numbers roughly 6,000 employees across close to 350 civil service classifications. Holly was started by Brendan Hellweg and Cherie Chung, who met as graduate students at Harvard Business School and Harvard Kennedy School. The company says it is supported by J2 Ventures, Roble Ventures, Gaingels and angel investors.

before.name: GovWell
before.description: AI permitting and licensing platform: 24/7 resident assistant, AI code-compliance review - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, Maryland Municipal League 2026

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

before.name: Aquatic Informatics (Veralto)
before.description: Water data management (AQUARIUS, WaterTrax) for utilities and environmental agencies - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Aquatic Informatics makes water data management software covering the full water cycle, sold to utilities, cities and monitoring agencies. The pitch is consolidating scattered data sources so an agency can report against regulations with an audit trail behind it.

Aquarius covers environmental monitoring data from acquisition through management to web based publication and decision support. WaterTrax centralizes sampling schedules, remote data collection and compliance reporting for municipalities. Linko handles fats, oils and grease programs, industrial pretreatment and hauled waste records. Tokay is aimed at cross connection control and backflow prevention programs. Hach WIMS stores process data in a central database that provides an audit trail and preserves historical records.

A module named HydroCorrect applies machine learning inside Aquarius to speed up reaction to environmental events. The company says Hach handed it the WIMS platform in 2021, citing more than twenty years of experience in water data management systems. Aquarius Cloud is offered as a fully managed service hosted on Amazon Web Services.

quote.text: One Water. One Platform.

provenance.quote: Water Data Management Software for the Full Water Cycle
Easily display and correct integrated data sources for compliance reporting with a defensible audit trail.

Aquarius is analytics software for natural environments that provides an integrated suite from data acquisition, to data management, and right through to web-based data dissemination and decision support.
WaterTrax compliance and electronic reporting tools for municipalities is a true cloud solution that centralizes sampling schedules, remote data collection, and compliance reporting
Linko simplifies the management of fats, oils and grease programs, industrial pretreatment, and hauled waste records.
Tokay is tailored to your Cross Connection Control program’s specific requirements
Process data is automatically stored in a central, secure database that provides an audit trail, preserves historical records
HydroCorrect™ is a predictive analytics module for Aquarius that uses Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) to help Aquarius users react faster to environment events
In 2021, Hach entrusted Aquatic Informatics with managing the WIMS Platform, leveraging AQI's 20+ years of experience in water data management systems.
Aquarius Cloud is a fully managed, cloud-based SaaS solution hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

before.name: Go Vocal
before.description: Community participation platform: surveys, ideation, participatory budgeting (ex-CitizenLab) - exhibited at 3CMA 2026

paragraphs: Go Vocal sells a community engagement platform that governments use to collect input from residents. The company states that its mission is to build stronger democracies by making public decision-making more inclusive, participatory, and responsive.

Agencies run surveys, voting, mapping and budgeting in one place rather than across separate departmental tools. Input gathered in person can be digitized, and speech can be converted to text. AI features are offered to organize responses and to build reports that can be shared with stakeholders.

The about page describes a global team of more than 50 local experts working with over 500 local governments and organisations across 20 countries. The company was founded in Belgium under the name CitizenLab, and its first pilot project was with the city of Hasselt. It describes itself as a B Corp certified SaaS company. paragraphs: Geographic Solutions makes online software for agencies in workforce development, economic development, education, corrections, human services, and unemployment insurance. The company frames that work as case management, labor exchange, and service delivery.

Its VOS Sapphire suite handles federally funded partner programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act, along with job aggregation, labor market information, fund tracking, federal reporting, and unemployment insurance benefits. The Virtual OneStop line is sold on a SaaS basis under annual or multi-year agreements covering hosting, maintenance, and upgrades. A map on the site lists the client systems built for each state.

Founder and President Paul Toomey started the business in 1992. The company timeline dates the first labor market information system in the country to a 1994 launch in North Carolina. The software suite has achieved StateRAMP/GovRAMP Authorization. Geographic Solutions also states that it is currently SOC1 Type II, SOC2 Type II, and SOC3 certified. Among its listed affiliations is membership in the National Association of Colleges and Employers.

paragraphs: Motive sells fleet software and hardware as one integrated suite built around AI. The buyers are commercial fleets, which the company describes as ranging from five or ten vehicles up to companies running thousands of them.

On the safety side, cameras and AI flag more than twenty kinds of event on the road. High-confidence events go straight to managers, while a safety team reviews the low-confidence ones to remove false positives. Vehicle tracking uses real-time GPS with traffic updates and weather overlays for route planning. Compliance work such as electronic logs, driver qualification, IFTA and CSA sits in the same platform. Equipment monitoring shows what share of the time an asset is in use and how long it sits dormant. Telematics from various equipment manufacturers is centralized in a single platform.

The company points to operations running from waste services to construction. It says it was named number one in fleet management across every segment. It also cites top rankings for equipment monitoring in G2 asset tracking reports for summer 2026. Its fleet card is issued by Sutton Bank under a license from Mastercard International.

before.name: Imprivata
before.description: Identity and access management software - exhibited at IACP 2026, NSA 2026, North Carolina Sheriffs' Association 2026

paragraphs: Imprivata sells access management software that gives people, partners and AI agents secure access to the systems and data they need. The company describes delivering passwordless, zero trust access.

For frontline workers who rely on shared devices, it provides single sign-on and multifactor authentication suited to specialized workflows. Authentication can use face, PIN, passkeys and badges, with identity verification for high-risk events like enrollment and resets. A mobility product helps organizations optimize their use of shared iOS and Android devices. A separate line secures digital identities and remote access so vendor connections to critical systems can be monitored. A newer offering manages AI agents like identities with zero trust access.

For state and local government, the company markets satisfying CJIS compliance for law enforcement. Healthcare is a named focus, where the aim is quicker clinical access with less cyber risk. The company states that it regularly performs audits and maintains HIPAA, NIST and SOC compliance. One customer story on its site describes Mackenzie Health using Imprivata to improve accountability.
