paragraphs: Concourse Tech builds software for public institutions, tailored to how each organization actually works. The company names state agencies, cities and counties, and school districts among the bodies it serves. Its offering is organized as a module library rather than a single product.

The permitting and licensing module covers applications, reviews, inspections, and renewals. A utility billing module manages water, electricity, and other utilities from meter to bill. Procurement work brings solicitations, contracts, vendors, and obligations together. For courts, case management holds dockets, filings, parties, and outcomes in one record. Projects begin with discovery sessions, since the company says no two entities are the same. Implementation, training, and ongoing support are included.

The site says deployments are built with SSO, MFA, AES-256 encryption, and zero-trust access. Agencies purchase Concourse through cooperative purchasing. The about page describes a team of people who have served in federal, state, and local government. One case study covers a state procurement deployment holding 1,500 statewide contracts. Case studies span states, cities, transit agencies, and school districts.

Edupoint reports 5.5 million students in 21 states. Bob Weathers founded the company in 2003. Recent announcements list districts switching over, among them Port Chester Public Schools in New York, replacing eSchoolPlus. before.name: Emburse
before.description: Expense management and payment software - exhibited at NIGP 2026, NACUBO 2026

paragraphs: Emburse sells travel and expense management software to finance teams. The platform covers expense, travel, accounts payable, cards, invoices and ACH payments, with localization for more than 100 countries.

Receipts are read by optical character recognition, whether the paper original or a digital copy. Spend is sorted automatically across dozens of categories, with VAT reconciliation and multiple currencies handled along the way. Policies are written once and enforced across the organization rather than checked afterward. A compliance layer examines receipts before and after submission, applying policy consistently and flagging risk early. For travel, the company sits alongside a customer's existing travel management company rather than replacing it, rebooking air and hotel when prices fall under rules the customer sets. It also connects to ERP, finance and accounting systems.

The company states that it serves over 20,000 organizations in 200 countries and territories. Those customers are described as large enterprises, smaller businesses, public sector agencies and nonprofits. Marne Martin is the chief executive. In July 2026 the company announced that it had been named to CNBC's list of the world's top fintech companies for that year.

paragraphs: BI Incorporated makes electronic monitoring technology for community corrections. The devices are used to supervise people on parole, probation or pretrial release rather than holding them in custody.

before.name: Klir
before.description: Permitting, compliance, and workflow software for water utilities - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Klir sells compliance and operations software built for drinking water and wastewater utilities. The argument for it is that administration and paperwork take up more than half the working time of utility scientists, engineers and operators. The platform holds that work as centralized, accessible data in one place.

On the drinking water side it manages SDWA permit adherence from start to finish. For wastewater it manages NPDES permit adherence. Pretreatment teams track industrial user details, permits and data. Staff reach it anywhere through a cloud platform with mobile inspections and field data entry. It is described as configurable and compatible with a Microsoft Azure stack alongside LIMS, GIS and SCADA.

Co-founders David Lynch and Elaine Kelly met while working with European drinking water and wastewater utilities and regulators. The company says large water and wastewater organizations in the United States, Canada and Australia now use it to centralize and automate compliance reporting. The team has grown past 60 people across the United States, Canada, Brazil and Ireland. The company lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and NIST compliance, and sells directly, through the Microsoft Azure Marketplace or on cooperative contracts.

brands.description:
Simpleview sells destination-marketing technology and marketing services to the organizations that promote places. Its own homepage now carries the title "Granicus Destinations | Marketing Solutions | CVB Tourism Software" and the line "From small towns to big countries, Granicus Destinations is the tourism software partner to help you engage stakeholders, attract visitors, and win bids for conventions and events." The product menu lists Simpleview CMS, "designed by and for DMOs"; Simpleview CRM, an industry-specific CRM with "seamless integration with more than 20 programs"; Simpleview DAM for digital assets; Destination Canvas; an Online Booking & Referral Engine branded Book > Direct that "lets visitors book directly with your partners and stakeholders"; Partner Engagement & Website Monetization (DTN), which "facilitates targeted advertising on destination websites" so DMOs can earn revenue; user-generated content; mobile apps; digital accessibility; email marketing and automation via Act-On; digital proposals; event management; short-term rental solutions; and a data tier of Simpleview Data Engine, dashboards, pace reporting and a meetings and groups database. Alongside the software it sells agency work: website design, visual identity, SEO, paid media, digital strategy, a Digital Maturity Model, DMO partner engagement, the Digital Influence Report and training. The acquisition release describes the buyers as "convention bureaus, venues, tourism boards, destination marketing organizations, and attractions." Granicus's destinations page states that "more than 500 DMOs use our CMS," that "1,000-plus destinations" use the CRM, and that 400M+ people visit those websites annually.

Both sites confirm Simpleview is part of Granicus, so the careers redirect is corroborated rather than relied on. Granicus's destinations FAQ asks "Is Simpleview now part of Granicus?" and answers "Yes. Simpleview was acquired by Granicus, and the legacy Simpleview products, services, expertise, and thought leadership are now a part of the Granicus portfolio serving destination marketers," then explains the two-site split: the solutions "remain at simpleviewinc.com" during a transition and "The two websites will be combined in the near future." Granicus's own office list gives Tucson, AZ, 8950 N. Oracle Road as "Simpleview, now part of Granicus" - the address in Simpleview's footer. Simpleview's Our Story page says plainly "We were acquired by Granicus." The Granicus press release of September 5, 2024 announced the acquisition, said Simpleview "works with more than 1,000 premier destinations," quoted Simpleview CEO Ryan George, and put the combined company at more than 7,000 organizations and roughly 2,000 employees. A May 5, 2026 release then announced Granicus Destinations as "a dedicated business segment" with its own leadership and the DXC platform, "supporting more than 1,000 destinations worldwide, including all 11 FIFA World Cup host cities." Our Story dates the business to 2001 as 220 Solutions, founded by Ryan George, Bill Simpson and Scott Wood; the first web-based CRM built for DMOs in 2002, with Visit Lauderdale as first client; a 2007 merger with cvbTV at 100 clients; New Media Gateway in 2010; Software Management, Inc. in 2014, adding 92 DMOs; and later 2Synergize, Jackrabbit Systems, Eventsforce and the MINT+ meetings database.

profile_research.description:
Granicus sells cloud software and services that governments use to communicate with the public, publish and stream meetings, run websites and forms, and manage records and permits. Its own site frames the offering as two platforms: the Government Experience Cloud (GXC), split into Service Cloud ("Deliver services without friction"), Engagement Cloud ("Grow and activate audiences") and Operations Cloud ("Automate workflows and reduce costs"), and the Destination Experience Cloud (DXC) for destination marketing. Layered on those are Government Experience Agent (GXA), described as an AI-powered digital agent built for government, a Federal Experience Cloud, and the GXI Enterprise and GXI Foundations intelligence tiers. The solution pages group the underlying products into agenda and meeting management, websites and CMS, digital services and forms, digital communication and engagement, permitting and licensing, and public records and short-term-rental compliance. The product directory names each tool with its legacy brand in parentheses: Communications (govDelivery), Websites & CMS (govAccess, OpenCities, Intranet), Records Request Management (GovQA and GovQA Legal), Short-Term Rentals (Host Compliance), Forms & Workflow (OpenForms), Service Request Management (govService and OneView), Permitting, Compliance & Licensing (AMANDA and SmartGov), Land & Official Records (govRecords), Sentiment & Feedback (EngagementHQ), Video (self-managed, and Swagit partially and fully managed), Boards and Commissions, and agenda management under the Legistar, OneMeeting and Peak names. The buyers named under "Who we serve" are local government, state government, federal government, education, special districts, elected officials and destinations, with country sites for Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia & New Zealand, India, and Latin America & the Caribbean. Granicus also sells consulting and digital agency work through the Granicus Experience Group (GXG).

Granicus is the parent of this family rather than a member of one. Its company page states "more than 2,000 employees across the globe supporting more than 7,000 public sector organizations," and the careers page repeats "about 2,000 of us" spread across "eight countries" in a remote-first workplace; that page's "Explore roles" button points at careers-granicus.icims.com, the iCIMS board the Simpleview careers page also lands on. The homepage figure block claims 7,000+ public sector customers, 360M people in the Granicus subscriber network, 100% of U.S. federal cabinet-level agencies, 48 of the 50 largest U.S. cities, 30B digital experiences and 22B government messages delivered annually, 8B government website views, 3.5M online forms submitted, 2M record requests served and 123K government meetings streamed each year. The company page carries a timeline headed "Organic and inorganic growth through best-in-class acquisitions": Granicus and GovDelivery were independently founded in 1999 and merged in 2017; Vision Internet arrived in 2018; a London-based government service provider in 2019; Bang the Table, OpenCities and GovQA in 2021 alongside Australia/New Zealand expansion; a full-service video provider and a government CRM in 2022 with entry into Latin America and the Caribbean; Simpleview in 2024; and GXA's launch in 2025. The same page names Vista Equity Partners as an existing investor joined by Harvest Partners in 2020. The trust-center office list gives Denver, Washington DC, Tucson, Ottawa, London, Melbourne, Auckland, San Juan and Bengaluru.

before.description: Hyperconverged cloud infrastructure software - exhibited at NACo 2026, MESC 2026

paragraphs: Nutanix sells infrastructure software that lets organizations build, manage and optimize IT across on-premises, edge and public cloud environments. At the core is a platform with hyperconverged compute, storage, virtualization and networking.

The storage layer consolidates file, object and block storage into one platform with integrated cyber security and ransomware protection. A database service automates provisioning, patching, cloning, backup and recovery, and supports Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL and MongoDB. paragraphs: 4Sight Labs sells a biometric monitoring system for correctional facilities, meant to help staff watch over the health of people held in custody. Its main product, OverWatch, is presented as the core of a unified correctional biometric platform built for settings where ordinary monitoring falls short.

People in custody wear sensors that track heart rate, blood oxygen, skin temperature and motion, along with other indicators of physiological distress. Readings are processed as they arrive, so that anomalies produce structured notifications instead of an after-the-fact review. Thresholds can be set by the facility so staff hear about a pattern that points toward a crisis.

The company says the platform is built for county detention centers, state systems, private facilities and complex housing units. It also states that the technology is designed and manufactured in the United States, with a controlled hardware and firmware supply chain. The site reports that the Harford County Sheriff's Office publicly announced putting OverWatch into its custody and safety strategy.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

paragraphs: City Detect sells a camera and software service that helps municipalities and counties find and address urban blight before complaints pile up. Cameras ride on a city's existing fleet vehicles and collect images of properties as those vehicles drive their normal routes. The company's PASS AI then detects and maps signs of urban blight and decay from the public right of way.

Roof-mounted data collection units capture street-level imagery during routine city operations. Once the images are processed, each detection is assigned a severity score from 1 to 4 and placed on an interactive map. The conditions it picks up run to illegal dumping, tire accumulations, snipe signs, and graffiti. Staff can export timestamped, image-backed reports in a few clicks.

The company says it was founded in 2021. One published case study describes Cathedral City partnering with City Detect in June 2025. For each municipality the company performs local calibration meant to cut false-positive detections and match local rules.

before.name: Common Sense AI
before.description: AI agents for gov back office: FOIA/records processing and meeting management - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Common Sense sells AI building blocks for local government, aimed at the administrative work that piles up in agencies. The modules cover public records and meeting management, with more beyond those two. Each module is meant to fit an agency's existing setup and account for the policies and laws that apply to it.

On records requests, the software triages, processes, and responds to incoming requests with full audit trails. It searches document management, email, and IT systems to find responsive records instead of asking each department to dig through its own files. Integrations named include Laserfiche, OnBase, Outlook, and Gmail. Redactions are prepared by the software, but staff review and approve them before documents go out. A second module runs the entire council meeting preparation process. After a meeting it drafts a plain summary of what was discussed and decided. A third module, Composer, builds workflow systems from a description written in plain English.

The departments named as users run from police and fire to the city clerk, legal, public works, and finance. The company says it is SOC 2 Type II certified and built for public-sector compliance. It states that the meeting product is co-built with the City of Peachtree Corners, Georgia and Starbase, Texas.

paragraphs: Securly sells student safety software to K-12 schools and districts, bringing content filtering and wellness visibility into a single platform. The company describes itself as parents, former educators, and technologists working on school safety.

Its content filter is described as the first cloud-native filter built specifically for K-12. A safety monitoring product analyzes online activity for signs of cyberbullying, self-harm, and violence. A classroom tool lets teachers share screens, lock devices, and push resources during a lesson. A digital hall pass product now folds in tardy management, visitor management, and PBIS. A newer layer puts guardrails on student AI use in the same way the web is filtered.

Published case studies name districts such as Ysleta ISD, which the company says uses its AI transparency tools across 34,000 students. For evidence of how widely it is used, Securly cites the EdTech Top 40 report from LearnPlatform by Instructure. Its board includes a managing director from Golden Gate Capital.

paragraphs: Euna Solutions sells a purpose-built, cloud-based set of financial software designed exclusively for the public sector. The buyers it names are cities, counties, states, school districts and publicly funded healthcare organizations of all sizes.

The budget product carries planning through publication, letting teams publish digital budget books and ACFRs to an interactive public portal. It is written to meet GFOA, GASB and accessibility standards. The grants product offers over 25,000 federal, state, municipal, local and foundation funding opportunities to search. On the spending side, the procurement product streamlines the purchase of goods and services with an emphasis on compliance. The company also offers integrations with ERPs including Workday, SAP, Carahsoft and Oracle.

The home page cites more than 3,600 organizations. For budgeting alone it cites 1,000+ organizations supported. Many staff are said to come from the public sector, with first-hand experience of government, education and nonprofits. A Euna Budget Enterprise option is aimed at larger governments and public agencies.

before.name: Caselle
before.description: Connect fund accounting, utility billing, and payments for small and mid-size cities - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: Caselle makes government accounting, ERP, and payments software. It is right-sized, in the company's words, for small to medium local governments, cities, and districts.

Accounting, utility billing, and reporting run in one system whose modules pass data to each other. Built-in tools produce audit-ready statements and track budgets in real time. Payroll and human resources are covered as well. So are permits and code enforcement. Business licensing and tax collection sit in the same system. A further set of tools is meant for sharing information with residents and collecting feedback.

Caselle dates its commitment to community to 1978. The company says its story began with Duane Hutchings, a CPA in Spanish Fork, Utah. Working with his sons and Spanish Fork City, he developed software to improve the workflows of people in local government. In 2024 Caselle joined Govineer Solutions. A published case study describes a city choosing Caselle after an extensive RFP process. That study says McPherson, Kansas explored six different government accounting software solutions before choosing Caselle. It reports the city saved four full workdays each month after the transition.

before.name: Geotab
before.description: Fleet telematics with one of the largest municipal footprints - exhibited at NAFA I&E 2026

paragraphs: Geotab sells fleet management technology that commercial vehicle operators use to track vehicles and run their operations from one system. The company describes what it offers as an open platform for safe, sustainable and cost-effective mobility powered by AI and data intelligence. Video safety is part of the same package, with dash cameras feeding into the MyGeotab software.

The GO tracking device plugs into a vehicle's onboard diagnostics port. Once driving begins it records location, speed, engine idling and distance. Dash cam footage and alert data upload to the cloud so managers can review video later. An analytics layer standardizes data from every vehicle source and enriches it with context such as road conditions, driver history and maintenance records. Developers can extend the platform with sample code and custom add-in pages.

Police and first responders are among the industries the site lists. Geotab reports more than six million connected vehicles. It also claims 26 years of fleet expertise. The company states that the platform is backed by ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II certifications and that its AI aligns with the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Support is described as staffed around the clock by experts who are in-market rather than offshored.

before.name: SimpliGov
before.description: Workflow automation, online forms and eSignature for state/local agencies - exhibited at Healthcare IT Connect 2026

paragraphs: SimpliGov sells a workflow platform for government agencies, built around the applications, approvals and casework that programs run on. Its stated scope is anything that moves through approvals, whatever the department.

Intake starts with online forms that meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Program teams lay out the steps on a drag-and-drop stage builder instead of writing custom code. The engine routes applications and decisions by rule, data threshold and the agency organizational structure. Approvals are signed inside the workflow with native e-signature tools. Dashboards track processing times, bottlenecks and audit trails.

Agency examples include New Castle County processing $322.8 million in emergency grants and passing its audit with zero findings. Another describes a California city automating more than 70 workflows and saving 17,000 labor hours a month. The forms page cites a federal accessibility mandate, 28 CFR Part 35, that larger public entities must meet by April 26, 2027. The platform is described as cloud-native and meeting government data privacy, security and accessibility mandates.

before.name: Lightspeed Systems
before.description: Web filtering and student safety monitoring for school districts - exhibited at CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Lightspeed Systems sells a connected platform of K-12 edtech products that give schools visibility and control across safety, security, compliance, device management, and analytics. Its filter covers every digital interaction on and off the network, protecting students from cyber risks and distractions while keeping access and compliance in place.

Filtering is enforced on the device itself, with an on-device SmartAgent and SmartShield DNS filtering covering school-managed, BYOD, and IoT devices. Lightspeed Alert monitors online activity, flags concerning behaviors, and enables intervention before a tragedy occurs. Those alerts are backed by round-the-clock monitoring from the company's own safety specialists. Lightspeed Classroom gives teachers visibility into and control over student activity to minimize distractions and maximize instructional time. Lightspeed StopIt is an anonymous reporting system for safety, misconduct, or compliance concerns. An analytics product shows granular app and device usage down to the grade and student level.

The company states that 28 of the 50 largest US school districts use its software, naming Los Angeles Unified, Houston ISD, Miami-Dade County Public Schools, and Fairfax County Public Schools. It puts the wider count at 31,000 schools around the world. The filter is described as designed for CIPA, FERPA, and NIST-aligned environments, with exportable audit trails and long-term retention.

paragraphs: Bentek sells benefits administration software purpose-built for the public sector. The company describes it as designed exclusively for states, local governments and educational institutions. It says its focus is the benefits administration needs of schools, counties and city governments.

The platform is put to work through configurable workflows, automated processes and adaptable reporting tools. It integrates with HRIS and payroll systems so data moves between platforms with less manual entry. Bentek says the platform carries more than 5,000 business rules. A library of more than 60 ready-made reports covers enrollment, engagement and compliance. Self-service enrollment handles active employees, retirees and COBRA participants.

Bentek says it was founded to serve public sector organizations. The company says its story began in 2006. It started when a local school district struggled to manage its benefits. The company puts its experience in the public sector environment at more than 20 years. It says it serves more than 300 employers in the public sector. One story on the site describes helping the Government of the U.S. Virgin Islands transform its benefits administration in four months.

before.name: ASTERRA
before.description: Satellite-based leak detection and underground pipe assessment - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: ASTERRA sells insight into what lies beneath the ground, produced without breaking ground using patented algorithms and artificial intelligence to detect leaks. Water and wastewater utilities use it for leak detection to reduce non-revenue water and for analysis of potable and wastewater systems. The same approach maps excess soil moisture near or under dams, levees, roads, railways and mining operations.

The company images a customer's system with polarimetric synthetic aperture radar to sense and evaluate soil moisture. The same regions are revisited every few days or weeks as needed to monitor vast expanses. Results land in EO Discover, described as the repository for all insights from a customer's ASTERRA projects. There, detections, hotspots and network risk appear in a single view. MasterPlan scores pipe segments that show non-surfacing leaks and analyzes leak clusters over time. EarthWorks uses synthetic aperture radar to detect soil moisture up to 10 feet below the surface.

Field crews log investigation results, leak location and other data using U-Collect or the Esri ArcGIS Field Maps app. Within five minutes that reporting is available in EO Discover. The company ties EarthWorks, MasterPlan and Recover to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. MasterPlan is available in the Advise level of an ASTERRA Recover subscription.

before.name: Klir
before.description: Permitting, compliance, and workflow software for water utilities - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Klir sells compliance and operations software built for drinking water and wastewater utilities. The argument for it is that administration and paperwork take up more than half the working time of utility scientists, engineers and operators. The platform holds that work as centralized, accessible data in one place.

On the drinking water side it manages SDWA permit adherence from start to finish. For wastewater it manages NPDES permit adherence. Pretreatment teams track industrial user details, permits and data. Staff reach it anywhere through a cloud platform with mobile inspections and field data entry. It is described as configurable and compatible with a Microsoft Azure stack alongside LIMS, GIS and SCADA.

Co-founders David Lynch and Elaine Kelly met while working with European drinking water and wastewater utilities and regulators. The company says large water and wastewater organizations in the United States, Canada and Australia now use it to centralize and automate compliance reporting. The team has grown past 60 people across the United States, Canada, Brazil and Ireland. The company lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 and NIST compliance, and sells directly, through the Microsoft Azure Marketplace or on cooperative contracts.

paragraphs: SewerAI sells a platform for sewer inspection work, aimed at utilities, contractors and engineers. It covers the work from inspection through rehabilitation.

Its AutoCode product reviews every frame of CCTV footage, identifies NASSCO observations and assigns PACP, LACP or MACP codes automatically. The company says this runs on the CCTV equipment a crew already owns. PIONEER, the record-keeping side, brings inspection records, asset histories, maintenance logs and compliance documentation into one platform. It also builds capital plans, letting users lasso-select segments on a map and apply budget constraints and cost guidance.

The site says the platform is used by more than 2,000 cities nationwide. The company describes 400 years of combined experience pulling cable, running cameras and managing programs. Its detection draws on more than 425,000 NASSCO surveys and 40,000 manhole assessments. SewerAI states that it is SOC 2 Type II certified.

before.name: Fulcrum (Spatial Networks)
before.description: Mobile field inspection and asset data collection for public works

paragraphs: Fulcrum sells a field operations platform that organizations use to run, record and close out work done away from an office. The pitch is aimed at teams still working from paper forms and a scatter of separate point tools.

Crews are given location-enabled apps on ordinary mobile devices in place of paperwork. They capture points, lines and polygons using the device's own GPS or a Bluetooth receiver. The collected records move into ArcGIS or other systems through APIs and formats such as shapefiles and GeoJSON. The company treats working without a signal as a baseline rather than an add-on.

State and local government is one of the named audiences, alongside utilities, construction and public works, with inspections and documentation for community projects. The home page states nearly 3,000 companies and 50,000 users in over 100 countries. On security, the company points to SCIM and SOC 2 compliance, and its timeline records an independent SOC 2 Type 1 certification. Spatial Networks Inc. is named as the maker of Fulcrum, and the company reports acquiring Wildnote to deepen environmental compliance work.

before.name: InfoSense
before.description: SL-RAT acoustic sewer line assessment tools for municipal sewer agencies

paragraphs: InfoSense sells the equipment, software and services that let a city work out which sewer pipes actually need cleaning before crews are sent out. The centrepiece is a handheld acoustic device that scores blockage conditions in small diameter gravity sewer lines.

A transmitter goes on one open manhole and a receiver on the next. Within a few minutes the display returns a rating from zero to ten showing whether the pipe is clear or obstructed. Nothing touches the flow and nobody has to enter a confined space. The company reports that two people can cover fifty to sixty segments in a day. Readings feed a companion platform that records, organises and maps the results. Data can be pushed out to mapping and spreadsheet tools already in use.

Buyers are public works departments and utilities moving away from cleaning on a fixed calendar toward cleaning based on measured condition. The company states that more than 1,350 utilities have used the tool. One published case study covers a small town serving just under ten thousand people. That town is reported to have cut its cleaning workload by more than half.

quote.text: Turn Hours into Minutes and Dollars into Sense

provenance.quote: We help municipalities take control of their sewer maintenance with equipment, software, and services that turn invisible conditions into actionable assessments.
The SL-RAT is a portable acoustic device engineered to assess blockage conditions in small-diameter gravity sewer lines.
First, set the SL-RAT transmitter device on the open manhole lid. Place the receiver on the other manhole.
The display shows whether the sewer pipes are good or blocked, with a score ranging from 0 to 10.
no flow contact, no confined space entry

SL-DOG is the digital platform that captures, organizes, and visualizes SL-RAT inspection data
Export data to ArcGIS, Google Earth, or Excel to work in existing systems.
It supports a shift to condition-based maintenance, where cleaning decisions are based on actual system conditions
More than 1,350 utilities have used the SL-RAT® to shift from fixed-schedule cleaning to data-driven maintenance.
Serves a population of just under 10,000
has reduced cleaning by over 50% and has saved over $180k

before.name: Aquatic Informatics (Veralto)
before.description: Water data management (AQUARIUS, WaterTrax) for utilities and environmental agencies - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Aquatic Informatics makes water data management software covering the full water cycle, sold to utilities, cities and monitoring agencies. The pitch is consolidating scattered data sources so an agency can report against regulations with an audit trail behind it.

Aquarius covers environmental monitoring data from acquisition through management to web based publication and decision support. WaterTrax centralizes sampling schedules, remote data collection and compliance reporting for municipalities. Linko handles fats, oils and grease programs, industrial pretreatment and hauled waste records. Tokay is aimed at cross connection control and backflow prevention programs. Hach WIMS stores process data in a central database that provides an audit trail and preserves historical records.

A module named HydroCorrect applies machine learning inside Aquarius to speed up reaction to environmental events. The company says Hach handed it the WIMS platform in 2021, citing more than twenty years of experience in water data management systems. Aquarius Cloud is offered as a fully managed service hosted on Amazon Web Services.

quote.text: One Water. One Platform.

provenance.quote: Water Data Management Software for the Full Water Cycle
Easily display and correct integrated data sources for compliance reporting with a defensible audit trail.

Aquarius is analytics software for natural environments that provides an integrated suite from data acquisition, to data management, and right through to web-based data dissemination and decision support.
WaterTrax compliance and electronic reporting tools for municipalities is a true cloud solution that centralizes sampling schedules, remote data collection, and compliance reporting
Linko simplifies the management of fats, oils and grease programs, industrial pretreatment, and hauled waste records.
Tokay is tailored to your Cross Connection Control program’s specific requirements
Process data is automatically stored in a central, secure database that provides an audit trail, preserves historical records
HydroCorrect™ is a predictive analytics module for Aquarius that uses Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML) to help Aquarius users react faster to environment events
In 2021, Hach entrusted Aquatic Informatics with managing the WIMS Platform, leveraging AQI's 20+ years of experience in water data management systems.
Aquarius Cloud is a fully managed, cloud-based SaaS solution hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

before.description: Satellite-based leak detection and underground pipe assessment - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: ASTERRA sells insight into what lies beneath the ground, produced without breaking ground using patented algorithms and artificial intelligence to detect leaks. Water and wastewater utilities use it for leak detection to reduce non-revenue water and for analysis of potable and wastewater systems. The same approach maps excess soil moisture near or under dams, levees, roads, railways and mining operations.

The company images a customer's system with polarimetric synthetic aperture radar to sense and evaluate soil moisture. The same regions are revisited every few days or weeks as needed to monitor vast expanses. Results land in EO Discover, described as the repository for all insights from a customer's ASTERRA projects. There, detections, hotspots and network risk appear in a single view. MasterPlan scores pipe segments that show non-surfacing leaks and analyzes leak clusters over time. EarthWorks uses synthetic aperture radar to detect soil moisture up to 10 feet below the surface.

Field crews log investigation results, leak location and other data using U-Collect or the Esri ArcGIS Field Maps app. Within five minutes that reporting is available in EO Discover. The company ties EarthWorks, MasterPlan and Recover to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. MasterPlan is available in the Advise level of an ASTERRA Recover subscription.

before.name: ADS Environmental Services (IDEX)
before.description: Sewer flow monitoring and I&I analytics for municipal wastewater utilities

paragraphs: ADS Environmental Services provides flow, level and rainfall monitoring for wastewater, storm and surface water systems. The buyers are municipal owners who need to know what is happening in their collection systems when it rains. The problems addressed include sanitary sewer overflows, sewer cleaning, combined sewer overflows and inflow and infiltration.

Monitors in the sewer feed software for visualizing, analyzing and managing the network. An agency can buy the equipment and run the program with its own staff. At the other end of the range, the company handles everything from placing the equipment to sending the alerts. A newer offering applies machine learning to spot developing blockages early enough to act on them.

Peter Petroff established the company in 1975 after a NASA career as a lunar guidance system engineer. A network of more than 400 monitors in Sydney, Australia in 1990 is described as a milestone in the company history. Product quality management certifications have been held since 1994, including an ISO 9001:2015 certificate issued by CSA Group. Offices sit across North America and Australia, with the corporate office in Huntsville, Alabama, and open roles are posted within IDEX Corporation.

before.name: Aquanuity, Inc.
before.description: AquaTwin digital twin software for water and sewer hydraulic modeling, surge analysis, and asset management, sold to water utilities and engineering consultants - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Aquanuity sells water, wastewater and stormwater modeling and asset management software that runs inside Esri ArcGIS Pro. Buyers are utilities and the engineering consultants working on their systems across the asset lifecycle.

AquaTwin Water models a distribution network so users can forecast demand, tune tank and pump operation, cut energy use and look into water quality problems. AquaTwin Sewer covers planning, design and analysis of stormwater, sanitary and combined sewer systems. That product is built on the EPA SWMM 5 engine. An extension named ATLive ties a model to SCADA so it can run against live readings from sensors and control systems. AquaTwin Asset turns condition and risk work into prioritized, costed capital improvement projects.

The company publishes benchmark papers, one of which reports its sewer solver outperforming the SWMM5 dynamic wave method by at least a factor of eight. It also states that the two-dimensional module did well in the UK Environment Agency hydraulic model benchmark test cases. Aquanuity frames its purpose as helping achieve environmentally, economically and socially sustainable water and wastewater infrastructure.

quote.text: The software can effectively be used by both water utilities and their engineering consultants in all phases of the water infrastructure asset lifecycle.

provenance.quote: Built exclusively on ArcGIS Pro®, AquaTwin Asset is a powerful feature-packed software for intelligent asset management of water, wastewater and stormwater systems.
The software can effectively be used by both water utilities and their engineering consultants in all phases of the water infrastructure asset lifecycle.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

before.name: Envirosight
before.description: Sewer inspection crawlers and push cameras for municipal wastewater agencies

paragraphs: Envirosight makes inspection equipment for the pipes that carry sewage and stormwater underground. That equipment is sold to cities and to the contractors who do the same work for them.

The core of the line is a wheeled camera crawler built for the conditions of underground work. Specialty crawlers and attachments fit the same platform, so one system can be adapted to different pipe sizes and inspection types. Operators code what they see at the controller using standard defect catalogs. Finished inspections, including video and images, upload to a web service for sharing and storage.

The company states that more than four thousand of these crawler systems operate worldwide. Alongside the hardware it publishes material for the market, including whitepapers, webinars, blog posts, infographics and case studies.

before.description: AI operations and forecasting software for water and wastewater utilities - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Aquasight sells analytics software for the people who run water and wastewater utilities. The company says the software runs in the cloud and calls for no new hardware.

One product is a digital twin for sewer mains, lift stations and combined sewer overflow facilities. It forecasts flows, compares them with expected patterns, picks out unexplained anomalies and estimates inflow, infiltration and capacity limits. A second product joins mapping and maintenance management data so that asset risk keeps updating. From that it recommends whether to inspect, repair or replace, and supports capital planning and financial forecasting.

The company states that it has partnered with over 120 utilities. It says the tools are shaped for operators, engineers, directors and compliance officers alike. A news item announces the company exhibiting and speaking at Weftec in New Orleans in September 2026.

paragraphs: Extra Duty Solutions administers extra duty programs for public safety agencies such as police departments, sheriff offices, state agencies, and fire departments. It also gives law enforcement agencies access to public safety scheduling software from Jivasoft, its IT division. Today it provides scheduling software and administrative support for agencies across the country.

The about page dates the business to 2015, when it served large corporations and coordinated extra-duty officers for executive protection, factory security, and logistics needs. In 2016 the focus shifted to serving the agencies themselves. In 2017 the company exited the corporate market entirely, which it says removed the conflict of interest that arises when one firm represents both the agency and the corporate customer.

Extra Duty Solutions acquired Jivasoft, a Texas-based company in law enforcement scheduling software, which brought the On-Duty and Xtra-Duty platforms into its lineup. Milestones listed on the same page include initiating service with a 100th agency. Later entries record surpassing $150M in annualized extra-duty invoicing. The most recent listed milestone is a 250th agency partnership. According to its own news release, the company was ranked No. 2740 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies in America.

paragraphs: Extra Duty Solutions administers extra duty programs for public safety agencies such as police departments, sheriff offices, state agencies, and fire departments. It also gives law enforcement agencies access to public safety scheduling software from Jivasoft, its IT division. Today it provides scheduling software and administrative support for agencies across the country.

The about page dates the business to 2015, when it served large corporations and coordinated extra-duty officers for executive protection, factory security, and logistics needs. In 2016 the focus shifted to serving the agencies themselves. In 2017 the company exited the corporate market entirely, which it says removed the conflict of interest that arises when one firm represents both the agency and the corporate customer.

Extra Duty Solutions acquired Jivasoft, a Texas-based company in law enforcement scheduling software, which brought the On-Duty and Xtra-Duty platforms into its lineup. Milestones listed on the same page include initiating service with a 100th agency. Later entries record surpassing $150M in annualized extra-duty invoicing. The most recent listed milestone is a 250th agency partnership. According to its own news release, the company was ranked No. 2740 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies in America.

paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. paragraphs: First Arriving sells a real-time information platform that connects the critical systems an agency already runs. The site claims 1400+ Fire, EMS, Law Enforcement & Local Government Agencies as users. The same information shows up at the station on the big screen, in the office on a desktop, and on a tablet in the field.

The platform centralizes data from 130+ systems into one operational view. Connected sources include CAD, RMS, staffing, fleet, facilities, GIS, scheduling, training, and alerts. Alerts can be pushed with required acknowledgments so the right people act immediately. Individual user accounts and role-based views mean each member of a team sees what they need.

The law enforcement version is designed for police departments, sheriff's offices, campus safety, and agencies of all sizes. It carries things like daily shift briefings and watch commander notes. A local government version covers council meetings, facility schedules, emergency alerts, and public notices. Lobbies, public counters and reception areas are named as display locations. The company notes that its marketing division is now ResponderMAX.

before.description: Incident records and ePCR data platform for EMS and fire agencies

paragraphs: ImageTrend sells software that fire departments, EMS agencies, and hospitals run their emergency response operations on. Its core product is ePCR software built for how medics actually work, with AI-assisted documentation, configurable workflows, and real-time intelligence for agencies at any scale.

The platform connects scheduling, documentation, compliance, unified analytics, operational readiness, and hospital data exchange in one system. NEMSIS, NERIS, NTDB, and TQIP compliance is built into every workflow, with software filling and validating fields while staff review and confirm before submission. A scheduling product, ImageTrend Slate, addresses the demands of EMS, fire departments, and other critical services. It manages time-off requests, shift trades, and employee availability. Separate pre-plan software digitizes floor plans, hazard locations, water supply points, and utility shutoffs so responders have instant access to tactical data on scene.

The company reports 9,000 agencies, 43 state repositories, and more than a billion records processed. It says its sales engineering team is entirely former fire and EMS. It cites 24/7 US-based support and a 96.5% satisfaction rate, backed by 25 years in the field.

before.description: State-specific policy manuals, training, and wellness content for public safety

competitors.why: Training LMS, policy/accountability content and Guardian Tracking sold to the same chief and training bureau on the same annual content subscription Lexipol bids.

paragraphs: Lexipol sells policy manuals, training, wellness resources, performance reporting, and grant support to public safety agencies, delivered through one system. Its buyers are the people running those agencies, from fire and police chiefs to risk managers, dispatch supervisors, and city administrators. An agency can begin with a single product, such as Policy or Wellness, and add others as it goes.

The policy product is the core: state-specific manuals researched and written by policy and legal professionals, then kept current as laws and standards change. Personnel acknowledge each policy electronically, which creates an audit trail for accreditation, audits, or legal reviews. Daily Training Bulletins turn those policies into practice through short scenario-based lessons. The LexOne platform ties training assignments to policy, warns leaders when licenses or credentials are about to expire, and tracks the data agencies need for reporting. Online courses carry accreditation from organizations such as IADLEST, POST, and CAPCE.

Lexipol was created in 2003 by two attorneys who were also former law enforcement officers. Co-founder Gordon Graham still records a weekly two-minute video tip for public safety and local government personnel. The company says its wellness product alone supports more than 1,000 agencies across the U.S. and Canada. Among the chiefs quoted on the site, Edward Delmore of the Gulf Shores (AL) Police Department compares a subscription to having another full-time administrator assigned to policy.

before.name: First Due
before.description: Cloud fire department suite: pre-incident planning, RMS, scheduling, and response

paragraphs: First Due sells cloud software that fire and EMS agencies use to run records and daily operations in one place. The suite pulls incident reporting, prevention, pre-incident planning, scheduling, assets, hydrants, training and mobile response behind a single login.

Incident documentation is built around the national fire reporting standard, with dynamic forms and error checking at submission. The patient care record is written to the NEMSIS data standard. It reads from cardiac monitors so crews do not key the same values twice. Pre-incident plans hold hazardous materials detail down to chemical location and quantity. Those plans can layer in GIS data through an Esri partnership.

The site describes CAL FIRE moving from a December decision to a July go-live. A county fire department is described using it to coordinate inspections and share preplan information with response crews. The company claims it accounts for nearly half of all NERIS submissions nationwide.

quote.text: Born in the cloud and built to run your entire operation in one place.

provenance.quote: Born in the cloud and built to run your entire operation in one place.

Consolidate NERIS, ePCR, fire prevention, pre-incident planning, scheduling & personnel management, asset & inventory, hydrants, training, community engagement, mobile response, and more into a single application with a sole login
Ensure accuracy from the start with dynamic forms and real-time error checking upon submission, powered by built-in NERIS and state data validation.
First Due is NEMSIS Data Collect v3.4 and 3.5 compliant
Avoid duplicate data entry by integrating your cardiac monitors such as ZOLL, Phillips, and Stryker.
Get detailed data on on-site hazardous materials, including chemical location, quantity, 704 info

paragraphs: MCM sells software that helps public safety agencies stay ahead of risk, increase safety and maintain compliance by managing assets, certifications, maintenance and inspections in one connected platform. The product is framed as intelligent operational readiness for public safety.

Asset tracking keeps a full lifecycle history from procurement through retirement. Issuance and chain of custody let staff issue serialized assets and consumable inventory in the same transaction. Work orders are created automatically when an inspection fails. Custom templates can be built for any inspection type, including vehicles, weapons, jump bags, respirators, facilities and sites. Agencies that would rather not administer the system themselves can buy managed services, pitched as maximum impact without the administrative overhead.

paragraphs: Esri builds ArcGIS, its geographic information system software for mapping and spatial analysis. The company describes itself as the global market leader in GIS software, location intelligence, and mapping. Its stated audience is business, government, and society.

ArcGIS is presented as enterprise technology that integrates and connects data through the context of geography. The premise is that hidden patterns, trends, and relationships emerge once data is visualized and analyzed on a map. Beyond maps and analysis, the company says its technology speeds data sharing and collaboration. For agencies that want to keep everything in house, there is a self-hosted edition for mapping, analytics, and data management.

Esri says it has supported customers with geographic science and geospatial analytics since 1969. Officials working in public safety, transportation, infrastructure, health and human services, and other fields use the technology to support high-level decisions. At the local level, the company says community leaders apply it to economic development, public works, and urban planning. Published stories include the US Census Bureau modernizing its entire census process with GIS.

paragraphs: Skydio makes autonomous drones, along with the docks and software to run them, and sells drone programs to customers from energy networks to neighborhood precincts to battlefields. Those programs cover Drone as First Responder, automated inspection and site security. Dock for X10 positions Skydio X10 drones at a site so that missions launch remotely without anyone present. The smaller Skydio R10 puts eyes indoors before officers enter.

Skydio states that more than 1,500 public safety agencies use its drones. In a Drone as First Responder program, Skydio says its drones launch in under 20 seconds and reach incidents autonomously in under 90 seconds. DFR Command is the software from which remote operators launch and manage drones, respond to multiple calls and stream live video to patrol and command. It integrates with RapidSOS and CAD at dispatch, Axon Fusus for live operations, and automatic evidence upload into Axon Evidence. Skydio's customer stories include Brookhaven PD, which it says reached 30 second response times after deploying 8 Docks.

Skydio Site Security uses the same dock-based drones to verify alarms, patrol perimeters and deliver live visibility across a site. Video streams into Genetec or Milestone, and flights launch automatically when triggered by alarms or access control events. Skydio says its data is encrypted in transit and at rest and that it aligns to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and NIST frameworks.

paragraphs: Peregrine builds what it calls Operational AI for High-Criticality Organizations. The product is a full-stack platform that turns disconnected data into complete operational context and puts actionable intelligence in front of every person in an organization. Law enforcement is listed as a solution area, and the platform is positioned for public safety work.

The site lists organizations that include the Atlanta Police Department, the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor's Office, Eagle Fire Department, and Northern Arizona University. Also named are Manatee County Emergency Management, East Pierce Fire-Rescue, the Merced County District Attorney, and Pinellas County Safety & Emergency Services. The Fairfax County Police Department is quoted alongside a case described as a child abduction suspect identified in 13 minutes.

The platform is laid out in numbered steps: forward deployed engineering, data ingestion and enrichment, organizational context, semantic ontology, intuitive interfaces and AI, and data governance. On governance, the company states that a customer keeps complete control over its data, full visibility into how that data is used, and granular access controls. A banner on the site announces a $250 million Series D.

before.name: Applied Information
before.description: Connected-vehicle ITS and the Glance smart-city platform: signal monitoring, preemption, school beacons

paragraphs: Applied Information makes traffic technology that turns intersections, school zones and connected vehicles into one real-time system. The customers are cities, which manage their traffic and ITS assets through a web-based application called Glance.

Glance monitors intersection cabinet equipment, reporting AC power, battery back up, cabinet flash, stop time, conflict monitor status, door switches, fan status and vehicle detectors. For emergency vehicles, an in-vehicle unit uses a cellular signal to tell the system a route has started. The system works out the route and talks wirelessly to the traffic cabinet to clear traffic ahead of the vehicle. School beacon flashers and their schedules can be viewed and controlled from anywhere. A connected vehicle product communicates over C-V2X, 4G LTE cellular and 900MHz.

The company states its hardware is designed, assembled and tested in Alpharetta, Georgia, with components meeting domestic content thresholds. A connected school bus system warns drivers approaching an active school safety zone or exceeding the speed limit. A smartphone app, Glance TravelSafely, extends the technology to residents.

quote.text: The drivers know they’ve got a green light in front of them, they know that everyone else has a red light, and they know the traffic is going to move ahead of them.

before.name: HAAS Alert
before.description: Safety Cloud digital alerting for DOT, fire and public works fleets

paragraphs: HAAS Alert sells a collision prevention service that sends real-time digital alerts warning drivers about nearby emergency vehicles and roadway hazards. Its customers are fleets that work at the roadside, including tow trucks, utility vehicles, waste management trucks, school buses and snowplows.

The system is wired to a vehicle's warning light bar or master switch, so alerting begins when crews turn on their lights and stops when they turn them off. Motorists install nothing, because alerts are broadcast directly to the navigation platforms they already use. Fleets can activate the service through three primary methods, depending on their existing setup. The company says drivers get up to 30 seconds of advance warning to slow down and move over.

The company traces its start to 2015, when co-founder and CEO Cory Hohs was almost struck by an ambulance on the road. He co-founded the business with Noah Levens and Jigar Patel. Its timeline notes that the United States Department of Homeland Security awarded $1.1 million toward development for digital alerting. It also states that digital alerting was codified and funded in the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act.

quote.text: Built in America for first responders and roadside workers so everyone gets home safely.

before.name: Tablet Command
before.description: Mobile incident command and response for fire/EMS departments

paragraphs: Tablet Command makes mobile incident command and response software for fire and EMS agencies. Commanders run an incident on a digital command board, dragging and dropping unit assignments.

The software is built on the iPad platform. A commander can tap and drag responding apparatus onto a scene, track progress against critical checklists, and time-stamp every maneuver and benchmark. Maps carry pre-plans and custom layers for hydrants, hospitals, landing zones, flood hazards and fire trails. The app is native and designed to run entirely independent of internet connectivity. It connects to CAD systems and integrates Esri GIS map layers, pre-plans, FireMapper and AVL.

The site reports over 250,000 incidents managed, covering everyday calls and multi-agency coordination. The product is also positioned as a complete replacement for mobile data terminals in the fire service. San Bernardino County Fire is named as using it in every front line response unit. A case study describes Stockton Fire Department turning to it as an MDT replacement and fire ground accountability tool.

paragraphs: PSTrax sells digital inventory and asset management software built for first responders. The system tracks inspections of vehicles, stations, equipment, supplies, controlled substances and blood products.

Rather than handing over a toolkit, the company builds and implements each system for the department and to that department's specs. Systems are meant to be ready to roll out in a matter of weeks. Ongoing support for changes is unlimited and comes at no extra cost. A one-year money back guarantee is offered to customers.

PSTrax, short for Public Safety Tracking Systems, was founded by Scott Bergeron and Cliff Long in 2009. It is headquartered in Littleton, Colorado, with 22 full-time employees. The company says it serves more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. That count includes more than 850 Fire-EMS agencies across the United States, Canada and Australia. It is privately held and says it answers to customers rather than to VC firms or shareholders. It reports a 98.5% customer retention rate.

paragraphs: Vector Solutions sells online training courses and the software to assign, track and report them, to schools and campuses, industrial employers, and fire, EMS and law enforcement agencies. For the fire service that means a training management system that tracks all training, EMS recerts, skill evaluations and ISO requirements in one place. Crews can accept callbacks and shifts from a mobile device, and a companion app handles truck checks, PPE inspections, controlled substance tracking and equipment maintenance. Law enforcement agencies get a training management system built around FTO/PTO and in-service training, plus POST and regulatory management, officer shift scheduling, policy management, BWC audits and accreditation management. A Professional Standards and Early Intervention tool gives agency leaders a way to manage performance and step in early.

In education, the company sells educator and staff training, a student safety and wellness program, and software to manage evaluations and professional development. Colleges get faculty and staff training, campus climate surveys built for VAWA compliance, and incident and EHS management. Industrial employers get a learning management system and course libraries in food safety, industrial skills, paper manufacturing, energy and HR compliance. Federal and military training management, fire marshal and POST training and compliance, and fire and law enforcement academy automation complete the list.

before.source: ICMA 2025; NACo 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: AchieveIt sells software for moving a written plan into measurable progress. It pitches itself to public agencies and other organizations that find performance hard to measure. The idea behind it is connecting people, plans and data in one place.

A plan is structured to match whatever methodology a customer already uses, from pillars and objectives down to initiatives, KPIs and milestones. Update requests then go out on a chosen cadence, asking owners for status, percent complete, commentary and metric values that flow into dashboards and roll-up reports. A tree view shows how each item in a plan lines up with the rest. Custom dashboards can display information drawn from any plan in the organization. A multi-plan view lets a customer filter, segment and drill into progress across everything at once.

AchieveIt says strategy consultants and customer success managers work alongside each customer. Onboarding, training and hands-on help come with the move away from manual tracking. The site sorts prospects by sector so a buyer can see how the software fits their way of working. One page groups its public sector claims under a heading about proven results.

before.name: CredibleMind
before.description: Behavioral health and wellbeing content, screening, and care-navigation platform deployed by public health departments, health plans, and health systems for their communities - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: CredibleMind partners with health plans, health systems, employers, and communities to break down the barriers of stigma, navigation, and cost that keep people from mental health care. Its platform blends evidence-based self-care, early intervention, and screening-based navigation into one integrated experience.

People start with validated assessments, and each customer configures referral rules and custom questions that triage higher-acuity needs to in-network care. The catalog runs to over a dozen assessments and more than 100 content topic centers. Behind those sit more than 10,000 evidence-rated resources that the company describes as grounded in science. The experience is designed for accessibility and available in 38 languages. APIs and EHR integrations tie the platform into clinical workflows.

The company says it works with more than 150 partners and supports over 40 million lives. Its stated partners include public sector agencies and community organizations. Deryk Van Brunt is a co-founder of the company and serves as its chief executive. Marcos Athanasoulis, also a co-founder, serves as chief technology officer.

quote.text: Our team of designers, data scientists, behaviorists, content creators, and clinicians share a passion for lighting the path to better mental health, for everyone.

before.name: CHESS Health
before.description: Digital substance use disorder prevention, intervention, and recovery support platform for treatment providers, state and county health agencies, drug courts, and Medicaid plans - exhibited at NatCon 2026

roles.title: Sales Director, Public Sector & Provider SUD

paragraphs: CHESS Health sells digital health software aimed at the substance use disorder crisis, for providers, health plans, and public sector organizations. Its public sector buyers are described as state health and behavioral health departments, county, tribal and local governments, drug courts, and correctional facilities. On the clinical side the site lists SUD providers, detox facilities, hospitals and emergency departments, clinics, FQHCs, and CCBHCs. Payers listed include managed care organizations, Medicaid plans, and commercial insurance.

Connections, the patient-facing app, offers 24/7 access to peer support, meetings, and recovery tools. Patients can be signed up automatically, with every patient invited to the app through EHR integration. A second product, eIntervention, is described as streamlining referrals and access to support services for substance use and mental health. A third, eRecovery, covers patient communication, progress tracking, and 24/7 peer support.

Published case studies include a county coalition in Hancock County, Ohio expanding its reach through community engagement. In one clinic case study, 83% of new patients using the app were still in treatment against 61% of those not using it.

paragraphs: Motorola Solutions builds and connects technologies to protect people, property and places, supporting the collaboration between public safety agencies and enterprises. Its public safety lineup includes APX portable and mobile radios and ASTRO radio systems. On the command center side it sells NG911 call routing and call handling and Computer-Aided Dispatch. The company also designs video security and access control systems.

For police users the APX NEXT smart radio comes in single-band and multi-band configurations. The APX 8500 all-band mobile radio adds interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity and Bluetooth in the vehicle. Vehicle routers keep first responders connected to broadband so they can reach real-time intelligence on the road. Its broadband products can run on FirstNET or on commercial carrier LTE networks. Managed, support and professional services are sold alongside to keep those systems secure and current.

Customer stories on the site include the Ouachita Parish Sheriff's Office, Peel Police, Nampa PD and York Regional Police, which serves 1.2 million residents. Hutto Independent School District uses the VB400 body camera to capture evidence in its schools. The home page announces the completed acquisition of D-Fend Solutions, which the company describes as a counter-drone technology firm.

paragraphs: NiCE sells Evidencentral, a cloud-based digital evidence management platform for public safety and justice agencies. The platform is meant to manage data from the moment an incident happens until a case is closed and prosecuted. For emergency communications centers that means incident recording and reconstruction, voice-to-text transcription, quality assurance and coaching, and PSAP performance reporting.

NiCE Inform automates incident reconstruction, evidence production, quality assurance and real-time performance metrics reporting. NiCE Investigate then brings evidence and associated information to investigators, patrol officers and criminal justice partners, with the stated aim of breaking down information silos. Further along the process, NiCE Justice and NiCE Defense help prosecution, defense and courts manage growing volumes of digital evidence. An Evidencentral Marketplace of technology vendors is designed to make it simpler and faster for emergency communications, law enforcement and criminal justice agencies to bring evidence together.

A customer story on the page comes from British Transport Police, attributed to its Senior Project Management for Digital Policing. The company describes the platform as powered by artificial intelligence and offers demos through the site.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Computer Information Systems, Inc. – Future Technology Today" www.cis.com (HTTP 200) is the site of Computer Information Systems, Inc., tagline 'Future Technology Today', and it hits all three products in the description verbatim: 'The CIS Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) System is a state-of-the-art program that enables dispatchers to efficiently and effectively manage incidents'; 'The CIS Records Management System (RMS) automates the records management functions of an agency'; and 'Jail Management System (JMS) provides comprehensive inmate management, facilities management, billing, and special programs.' Operating since 1985, serving police departments, sheriffs' offices and 911/fire centers across North America. Disambiguation check, since 'CIS' is a heavily contested acronym: this is NOT the Center for Internet Security (cisecurity.org) and NOT any other CIS - the domain's own pages ('Systems', 'Services', 'About' under cis.com) all carry the 'Computer Information Systems, Inc.' name with public safety content. One ownership note that does not change the verdict: a January 2025 announcement covers CIS partnering with investor Arcadea Group, but CIS retains its own brand and its own domain, so cis.com remains the correct record - do not repoint this at Arcadea.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AI-Powered Solutions Helping ALL First Responders Do Their Best Work" Fetched https://www.govworx.ai. The site is branded GovWorx and the quoted headline ties it directly to the 'software for first responder agencies' description. The buyer is named precisely — 911 Emergency Communications Centers: 'We deliver AI-powered solutions that help ECCs automate tasks and strengthen, guide, and support first responders.' Named products corroborate the sector rather than a same-name firm elsewhere: the CommsCoach suite (QA and call evaluations, pre-hire testing, training and simulations, real-time call guidance) plus MedAssist for paramedics and BluAssist for law enforcement, with claimed scale of 1.2M+ evaluations monthly across 475+ customers. Own primary domain. No concerns.

paragraphs: GovWorx sells CommsCoach, an AI-powered software platform that emergency communications centers use to hire, train, evaluate and support 9-1-1 telecommunicators. It is aimed at the ECC leaders responsible for improving the performance of 9-1-1 professionals. Its modules follow a telecommunicator from candidate through career, linking HIRE, TRAIN, QA and ASSIST in one system, with PROMOTE added for choosing supervisors.

CommsCoach HIRE measures aptitude, resilience, accuracy and composure through structured testing and AI-supported scoring, with tests run onsite or remotely. QA automatically pulls every eligible call and radio transmission, matches transcripts to CAD event data and scores them against the agency's own policies. During live calls, ASSIST listens, transcribes and prompts the call-taker with the policy-specific questions the situation requires. PROMOTE is an evidence-based assessment that identifies leadership potential in supervisor candidates and pairs each result with a personalized development pathway.

An emergency communications administrator at the O'Fallon Police Department in Missouri is quoted saying call-taking compliance rose from single digits to 96% with ASSIST, APCO guidecards and complete QA. In June 2026 APCO International and GovWorx announced a partnership to bring APCO's communications protocols into CommsCoach ASSIST. In August 2026 GovWorx added NEAL, an adaptive non-emergency call handling tool that escalates to a human telecommunicator whenever judgment is needed.

paragraphs: MCM sells software that helps public safety agencies stay ahead of risk, increase safety and maintain compliance by managing assets, certifications, maintenance and inspections in one connected platform. The product is framed as intelligent operational readiness for public safety.

Asset tracking keeps a full lifecycle history from procurement through retirement. Issuance and chain of custody let staff issue serialized assets and consumable inventory in the same transaction. Work orders are created automatically when an inspection fails. Custom templates can be built for any inspection type, including vehicles, weapons, jump bags, respirators, facilities and sites. An open REST API is offered for connecting other systems, and the integrations page claims to be the only platform that integrates directly with major radio manufacturers.

The company cites 300+ public safety agencies nationwide. For fire agencies the aim is to keep apparatus, gear and crew inspection-ready at every station and before the next call comes in. For government and utilities it gives full asset visibility and tracks grant-funded resources. A news post announces Anthony Rotoli as new CEO. Agencies that would rather not administer the system themselves can buy managed services, pitched as maximum impact without the administrative overhead.

before.name: RapidSOS
before.description: Intelligent 911 platform streaming device location and data to dispatch

paragraphs: RapidSOS connects public safety agencies, enterprises and large numbers of consumer and corporate devices so emergency information reaches responders. The company states it partners with over 250 enterprise companies and 23,500 public safety agencies.

The premise is that connected systems can share information with responders even before a 911 call is placed. One police department describes adopting a module built around AI-powered live text translation, transcription and call summarization. In an Atlanta deployment, translation covered over 37 languages by voice and over 200 by text. Another center is described using Harmony AI to handle non-emergency calls.

The homepage says agencies and enterprises on the network safeguard over 99% of the country. Published case studies sort customers into categories such as connected vehicles and telematics. One partner statement on the site is attributed to a VP of Safety at Norfolk Southern. A documented problem it addresses is waiting up to ten minutes for a translator on a 911 call.
