before.name: ADS Environmental Services (IDEX)
before.description: Sewer flow monitoring and I&I analytics for municipal wastewater utilities - exhibited at WEFTEC 2026

paragraphs: ADS Environmental Services provides flow, level and rainfall monitoring for wastewater, storm and surface water systems. The buyers are municipal owners who need to know what is happening in their collection systems when it rains. The problems addressed include sanitary sewer overflows, sewer cleaning, combined sewer overflows and inflow and infiltration.

Monitors in the sewer feed software for visualizing, analyzing and managing the network. An agency can buy the equipment and run the program with its own staff. At the other end of the range, the company handles everything from placing the equipment to sending the alerts. A newer offering applies machine learning to spot developing blockages early enough to act on them.

Peter Petroff established the company in 1975 after a NASA career as a lunar guidance system engineer. A network of more than 400 monitors in Sydney, Australia in 1990 is described as a milestone in the company history. Product quality management certifications have been held since 1994, including an ISO 9001:2015 certificate issued by CSA Group. Offices sit across North America and Australia, with the corporate office in Huntsville, Alabama, and open roles are posted within IDEX Corporation.

paragraphs: Forerunner sells software it calls a geospatial intelligence layer. The platform unifies geospatial data, field operations, and AI-powered workflows in one place. Local government is a core buyer, with compliance work across stormwater, floodplain, and code enforcement programs. The company also markets to energy and infrastructure operators handling inspections across active sites and assets.

At the base sits a map-first view holding every asset, permit parcel, violation, and environmental layer. On top of it run configurable workflows for inspections, permits, violations, and grant tracking. Inspection findings then generate corrective actions, and permit deadlines trigger notifications. The company says adoption brings no rip-and-replace projects and no major workflow disruptions. It claims teams are up and running in weeks.

Published case studies name the Puerto Rico Planning Board, which the company says replaced paper forms and spreadsheets for field inspections and code compliance. Another states that Lee County saves approximately 16 hours of staff time per week. A further case study describes Ponce Inlet centralizing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System workflows to reclaim 10 or more hours per week.

paragraphs: collectionHQ sells software that public libraries use to select, manage and promote their collections. Its stated point of difference is guidance on what action to take to improve the performance of a collection. The product rests on the Evidence Based Stock Management methodology, which the company says has been used in public libraries for over 21 years.

The company reports use in more than 8,000 public library branches worldwide. It reports managing more than 220 million items for public libraries in the United Kingdom, Ireland, U.S.A., Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Case studies name customers including Cuyahoga County Public Library and Marin County Free Library.

The company was founded in Glasgow, United Kingdom, and introduced to the public library market in 2008. It entered the academic library market in 2024 with cHQacademic. The pages describe it as a partner of public and academic libraries.

after.evidence: https://www.kovacorp.com/products

paragraphs.text: Kova Corp sells communication, recording and alerting software for public safety organizations and for enterprises.
paragraphs.quote: Kova Corp delivers reliable solutions for enterprise and security intelligence and alerting, efforts supported by our partnerships with global leaders in public safety.

paragraphs.text: The products page splits the catalogue into public safety solutions, enterprise workforce optimization solutions and an emergency alerting solution.
paragraphs.quote: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

paragraphs.text: KEANS, the KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System, links multiple locations, agencies, business partners and public address systems such as loudspeakers, bull horns and audio distribution repeaters.
paragraphs.quote: KEANS (KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System) provides reliable, simultaneous communication between multiple locations, agencies, business partners, and public address systems (such as loudspeakers, bull horns, and audio distribution repeaters).

paragraphs.text: KAMS, the Kova Alarm Monitoring Solution, handles hardware monitoring, captures SNMP alerts and OS events, and can monitor data streams such as CDR, P25 traffic and RTP.
paragraphs.quote: KAMS provides not only the typical Hardware monitoring (CPU usage, memory, drive space, temperature, etc.) along with capturing SNMP alerts and OS events, but also can monitor critical data streams like CDR, P25 traffic, and RTP.

paragraphs.text: The workforce optimization page offers contact centers a platform for multimedia recording, evaluation and archiving of calls, plus an Enterprise Feedback Management survey platform and a Workforce Management solution.
paragraphs.quote: Kova recording solutions for contact centers provide a high performance platform for the multimedia recording, evaluation, and archiving of calls.

paragraphs.text: The about page names 911 call centers and emergency responders as the people those public safety solutions serve.
paragraphs.quote: Our public safety solutions enable 911 call centers to function more efficiently, allow emergency responders to instantly share vital information, and make it possible to record and decipher data gathered.

paragraphs.text: The about page also cites a recorder installed for the Port Authority of NY/NJ after the loss of its Emergency Operations Center.
paragraphs.quote: KOVA offered immediate assistance to the Port Authority of NY/NJ, when it lost its Emergency Operations Center on 9/11. Within twenty-four hours, KOVA installed a new recorder at a temporary site.

quote.text: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

after.name: Job Machine
after.why: The four pages state plainly what the product does at each step, who it is built for, and how it is priced, so a write-up needs nothing beyond them; they carry no founding date, headcount or named customer organisation.
after.evidence: https://jobmachine.com

paragraphs.text: Job Machine sells an AI service that runs the job search for the people an organization is responsible for placing.
paragraphs.quote: How Job Machine runs the job search for thousands of people at once.

paragraphs.text: The service tailors each resume, searches job boards and company sites, applies on the candidate's behalf, schedules interviews, preps the candidate, and captures the offer letter and verification of employment.
paragraphs.quote: We capture the offer letter and verification of employment.

paragraphs.text: Onboarding is mostly text based, and each person completes a guided intake in under three minutes.
paragraphs.quote: Each person completes a guided intake in under three minutes, mostly over text, with no app to learn.

paragraphs.text: The buyers named on these pages are career colleges, community colleges, workforce boards, American Job Centers, veterans services and outplacement programs.
paragraphs.quote: Trusted by career colleges, workforce boards, and American Job Centers nationwide.

paragraphs.text: For workforce boards, AJCs and one-stops, the stated outcome is placing more people without adding staff.
paragraphs.quote: Place more people. Without adding staff.

paragraphs.text: Job Machine states that offer letters and verification are captured automatically and that proof of placement sits in the buyer's own system.
paragraphs.quote: Offer letters and verification captured automatically, not chased.

paragraphs.text: Pricing is consumption based, charged per activated candidate when someone onboards and applications begin.
paragraphs.quote: Consumption-based: you pay per activated candidate, only when someone onboards and we start applying for them.

paragraphs.text: Job Machine states that it passed government security and IT review, with no long-term commitment and payment only for activations.
paragraphs.quote: No long-term commitment Pay only for activations Passed government security and IT review

paragraphs.text: The homepage reports a pilot where placement went from roughly 10% to over 55%, and an average of 28 days from onboarding to a job.
paragraphs.quote: In a pilot with a workforce center serving dislocated workers, placement went from roughly 10% to over 55%, in the final 90 days before fiscal year end, with no new hires.

quote.text: We automate every step of getting a job. Except getting dressed for the interview.

paragraphs: Kova Corp sells communication, recording and alerting software for public safety organizations and for enterprises. The products page splits the catalogue into public safety solutions, enterprise workforce optimization solutions and an emergency alerting solution.

KEANS, the KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System, links multiple locations, agencies, business partners and public address systems such as loudspeakers, bull horns and audio distribution repeaters. KAMS, the Kova Alarm Monitoring Solution, handles hardware monitoring, captures SNMP alerts and OS events, and can monitor data streams such as CDR, P25 traffic and RTP.

The workforce optimization page offers contact centers a platform for multimedia recording, evaluation and archiving of calls, plus an Enterprise Feedback Management survey platform and a Workforce Management solution. The about page names 911 call centers and emergency responders as the people those public safety solutions serve. The about page also cites a recorder installed for the Port Authority of NY/NJ after the loss of its Emergency Operations Center.

quote.text: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

provenance.quote: Kova Corp delivers reliable solutions for enterprise and security intelligence and alerting, efforts supported by our partnerships with global leaders in public safety.

Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

KEANS (KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System) provides reliable, simultaneous communication between multiple locations, agencies, business partners, and public address systems (such as loudspeakers, bull horns, and audio distribution repeaters).

KAMS provides not only the typical Hardware monitoring (CPU usage, memory, drive space, temperature, etc.) along with capturing SNMP alerts and OS events, but also can monitor critical data streams like CDR, P25 traffic, and RTP.
Kova recording solutions for contact centers provide a high performance platform for the multimedia recording, evaluation, and archiving of calls.

Our public safety solutions enable 911 call centers to function more efficiently, allow emergency responders to instantly share vital information, and make it possible to record and decipher data gathered.
KOVA offered immediate assistance to the Port Authority of NY/NJ, when it lost its Emergency Operations Center on 9/11. Within twenty-four hours, KOVA installed a new recorder at a temporary site.

paragraphs: Katapult Engineering sells Katapult Pro, a platform that organizes the pole attachment process for utilities, engineers, and attachers. The platform brings application intake, field collection, engineering review, and approval into one record that each party can see. Stages in that workflow record entry and exit timestamps, and timeline tracking flags progress against FCC and PUC deadlines.

Field crews collect pole photos and measurements on a mobile device, and that record becomes the make ready plan. Engineering design runs pole loading analysis while a design is underway and flags clearance violations across a whole project. Clearances can be imported from NESC or GO95 and adjusted to a customer's own standards, and make ready reports separate simple work from complex work.

Utilities and co-ops, engineering firms, and telecom providers are the three audiences the homepage addresses. Subscriptions are month-to-month with fixed annual rates and no seat minimums. Onboarding usually starts with a pilot project scoped in a call with the customer's joint use lead.

quote.text: One workflow from application intake to post-construction inspection, with the utility, attacher and contractors seeing the same thing.

provenance.quote: Katapult Pro cleans up the mess of scattered data and manual workflows into a clean, organized process so utilities, engineers, and attachers can deliver with confidence.

paragraphs: Journal Technologies Inc. is an enterprise software company and a subsidiary of Daily Journal Corporation. The company makes software for courts and the justice system. Headquarters are in downtown Los Angeles, with approximately 298 employees and a major office in Logan, Utah.

The eCourt case management system covers appellate, superior, municipal, traffic, probate, and drug courts. eDefender provides case management for public defenders. eProsecutor provides case management for state, county, and city prosecutors, as well as Medicaid fraud control units. eSupervision provides case management for probation, parole, court services, pretrial, and diversion offices. eProsecutor Online is a cloud-hosted version of eProsecutor for small to mid-sized prosecutors.

Ancillary offerings include eFile-it, which lets justice partners, organizations, attorneys, and self-represented litigants file cases, documents, and other information electronically. ePay-it is a cloud-hosted payment portal for online payments of court-associated fees. The case studies page says courts, justice agencies, and government leaders solve problems with Journal Technologies. Named case studies include the State of Connecticut, the City of Spokane, Mohave County, Riverside County, and Los Angeles Superior Court.

quote.text: Our mission is to make and implement technology that is so well-designed and adaptable to daily workflows that it fades into the background, so busy people can focus on their mandates and not the tools.

provenance.quote: Journal Technologies Inc. is an enterprise software company connected as a long-time subsidiary with Daily Journal Corporation (NASDAQ: DJCO)

paragraphs: Kova Corp sells communication, recording and alerting software for public safety organizations and for enterprises. The products page splits the catalogue into public safety solutions, enterprise workforce optimization solutions and an emergency alerting solution.

KEANS, the KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System, links multiple locations, agencies, business partners and public address systems such as loudspeakers, bull horns and audio distribution repeaters. KAMS, the Kova Alarm Monitoring Solution, handles hardware monitoring, captures SNMP alerts and OS events, and can monitor data streams such as CDR, P25 traffic and RTP.

The workforce optimization page offers contact centers a platform for multimedia recording, evaluation and archiving of calls, plus an Enterprise Feedback Management survey platform and a Workforce Management solution. The about page names 911 call centers and emergency responders as the people those public safety solutions serve. The about page also cites a recorder installed for the Port Authority of NY/NJ after the loss of its Emergency Operations Center.

quote.text: Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

provenance.quote: Kova Corp delivers reliable solutions for enterprise and security intelligence and alerting, efforts supported by our partnerships with global leaders in public safety.

Whether your organization is searching for enterprise workforce optimization solutions, public safety solutions, or a emergency alerting solution, KOVA has the products and the know-how to customize a solution to fit your unique needs.

KEANS (KOVA Emergency Alert Notification System) provides reliable, simultaneous communication between multiple locations, agencies, business partners, and public address systems (such as loudspeakers, bull horns, and audio distribution repeaters).

KAMS provides not only the typical Hardware monitoring (CPU usage, memory, drive space, temperature, etc.) along with capturing SNMP alerts and OS events, but also can monitor critical data streams like CDR, P25 traffic, and RTP.
Kova recording solutions for contact centers provide a high performance platform for the multimedia recording, evaluation, and archiving of calls.

Our public safety solutions enable 911 call centers to function more efficiently, allow emergency responders to instantly share vital information, and make it possible to record and decipher data gathered.

paragraphs: gWorks sells cloud software for local government, covering financials, operations, and citizen services on one platform. The pages describe two product families, financials and operations, that a customer can start with in part and expand later. Financials covers fund accounting, utility billing, payroll, and citizen payments. Operations covers public works software for cities, counties, and utility agencies of every size.

The platform's fund accounting is described as GASB-compliant, with multi-fund tracking, encumbrances, grants, and audit-ready reporting. The Website module gives residents one login to pay utility bills, submit requests, check permit status, and renew licenses online. Citizen Engagement sends outbound notifications to residents by email, text, or automated voice call, including utility alerts and billing reminders. FrontDesk Payments takes payments online, by phone, and at the counter, and posts them to the same account and the same ledger.
The customer testimonials on the homepage are attributed to cities, counties, and utility districts. gWorks describes the product as cloud software built for small local governments on one platform.

quote.text: Software built for local government.

provenance.quote: Cloud software that powers communities across America: financials, operations, and citizen services.

before.description: Pole attachment and make-ready survey software for utilities and broadband builds

after.name: Katapult Engineering
after.description: Pole attachment and make-ready survey software for utilities and broadband builds

paragraphs: Katapult Engineering sells Katapult Pro, a platform that organizes the pole attachment process for utilities, engineers, and attachers. The platform brings application intake, field collection, engineering review, and approval into one record that each party can see. Stages in that workflow record entry and exit timestamps, and timeline tracking flags progress against FCC and PUC deadlines.

Field crews collect pole photos and measurements on a mobile device, and that record becomes the make ready plan. Engineering design runs pole loading analysis while a design is underway and flags clearance violations across a whole project. Clearances can be imported from NESC or GO95 and adjusted to a customer's own standards, and make ready reports separate simple work from complex work.

Utilities and co-ops, engineering firms, and telecom providers are the three audiences the homepage addresses. Subscriptions are month-to-month with fixed annual rates and no seat minimums. Onboarding usually starts with a pilot project scoped in a call with the customer's joint use lead.

quote.text: One workflow from application intake to post-construction inspection, with the utility, attacher and contractors seeing the same thing.

provenance.quote: Katapult Pro cleans up the mess of scattered data and manual workflows into a clean, organized process so utilities, engineers, and attachers can deliver with confidence.

paragraphs: LONG DBA Justice Systems is a design-build integrator of unified electronic security systems, specializing in government and public safety facilities. The services offered are design-build integration, competitive-bid integration, and follow-on maintenance, applied to new construction, upgrades, and retrofits. Retrofit and upgrade work covers general government buildings, courts, jails, juvenile facilities, secure mental health facilities, and prisons.

Integration is built on PLCs, described as enabling single-point responsibility for high-security buildings. The unified package covers door and elevator controls, video surveillance, intercommunications, paging, utility controls, and alarm monitoring. Justice Systems serves as engineer-of-record on a large percentage of its projects and holds professional engineering registration in multiple states.

Reported volume is 120 projects and $50 million in total systems value, counting only the contract value of projects performed. Follow-on service and support has covered approximately 70% of the facilities built or upgraded, some $7 million in maintenance services. Procurement can run through NASPO, where LONG is an authorized dealer in Washington, Colorado, and Alaska.

quote.text: We design, implement, and service integrated security systems that accelerate your project schedule, streamline your operations, and strengthen the safety of your building and the people inside.

paragraphs: Konveio sells an engagement platform built around planning documents and the full plan lifecycle. The platform is split into an Engagement Hub for public input and a Plan Hub that publishes a Plan Library. Organizations upload materials they already have and take comments on them in place. The company dates its inception to 2020.

Staff can export data to CSV or download annotated PDF reports. Comments from events, letters and emails can be imported and analyzed in one place. The viewer is described as mobile-friendly, WCAG compliant, and screen-reader accessible.

Local Governments are named as an audience, from early stage outreach through implementation stages. State agencies are named for work groups and for drafting policy and legislation. Consultants are named, with plans described as fitting tight budgets or project needs. Colleges, universities and school districts are named for community outreach projects.

quote.text: Konveio's mission is to help community builders get informed buy-in for their efforts to create a better tomorrow.

provenance.quote: Konveio is the Planner’s engagement platform, designed to simplify how communities engage with stakeholders throughout the full plan lifecycle and find answers in their complex framework of guiding documents.

Konveio’s Engagement Hub creates buy-in for planning projects, supporting public input from early stage workshops to draft reviews. And our Plan Hub enables users to publish engaging plans as an AI-connected Plan Library that is ready for questions.

paragraphs: IKE sells data acquisition and structural analysis software for power and communication infrastructure. IKE Device speeds up field data collection, and field data uploads to IKE Office Pro for management of pole records. IKE PoleForeman is a structural analysis tool for NESC compliance and pole loading analysis of overhead infrastructure.

The company names utilities, engineering firms, and communications companies among the industries it serves. The about page describes the business as a platform technology company for utility poles and the equipment and services they support. The same page ties those solutions to designing, constructing, and inspecting distribution assets, and to grid resiliency and fiber broadband expansions.

IKE also offers NESC and OSHA training courses for utility and communications workers. The about page lists 500+ enterprise customers across utilities, telecom, and engineering. The same page reports coverage in all 50 states, supporting critical infrastructure nationwide.

quote.text: We help utilities, telecommunication companies, and engineering firms design, manage, and optimize critical overhead infrastructure.

provenance.quote: Delivering actionable insights on power and communication infrastructure with advanced pole data and structural analysis

paragraphs: JuryQ sells jury management software that courts run from summons through selection to juror payment. The platform bundles summons templates carrying scannable QR codes, juror apps for iOS and Android, a web option for people without smartphones, a clerk dashboard, kiosk check-in and digital payment. Pricing is described as all-inclusive and set by county population tier, and every plan carries a 2-month pilot.

Courts are the named customer, and the homepage lists Callahan County, Collin County, Irion County and Angelina County in Texas. The testimonials are attributed to court clerks and administrators in those counties, one of them describing a pilot run across multiple court dates. Jurors use the same platform to register, check in and take payment, but the pages put courts on the buying side.

The about page presents JuryQ as the first piece of a broader plan that also names CourtQ for court case management and GovQ for state and local government management. Both of those are listed as coming soon, and the same page places the set on one platform for the public sector.

paragraphs: Ladris sells disaster evacuation modeling software to planners, responders, and residents. The about page lists Education, Government, Defense, Aerospace, Research, Manufacturing, and other organizations as the users the platform helps save time, reduce operating costs, and improve fixed asset visibility.

The about page says the company was founded in 2001 with a focus on developing data collection solutions, that its focus transitioned to RFID in 2004, and that its first RFID-based product was released in 2005. RFID is a data collection technology that uses radio frequency communication to collect data from RFID tags, which can uniquely identify objects such as assets or people.

paragraphs: INFODEV EDI develops and installs automatic passenger and people counting systems and has worked in this industry since 1993. The counting systems cover buses, trains, trams, subways, and railway and bus stations. Infodev EDI describes years of experience implementing automatic passenger counting projects in public transit. The home page describes ridership data for transit agencies that goes beyond basic passenger counts.

The DA-Series counting sensors are stated as accurate between 97.5% and 99.5%, at door level and without a correction factor. The DA-400 is a directional sensor that can be as thin as 13.5 mm for surface or inside-panel mounting above doors. The DA-200 is built to fit narrow doors and holds a single sensor in an aluminium case.

The GW-400 is a compact onboard counting computer that works with the DA-Series sensors to form an automatic passenger counting system. Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. Systems come in two architectures, a classical one that yields historical data for analysis and reporting and an enhanced one that yields real-time data.

quote.text: 97.5% to 99.5% Accuracy from Pure Counting Data in an Uncontrolled Transit Environment

paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. They capture vibration, temperature, runtime, and operational behavior, and the stated install time is 30 to 120 minutes on legacy and modern equipment. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Knaq describes the equipment it monitors as critical infrastructure across airports, transit systems, hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. For transit agencies the stated value is early identification of failures that lead to station outages and accessibility violations. paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Large real estate portfolios are listed as another buyer group, with tenant disruption and contractor performance named as concerns.

The about page names Sound Transit as a client that paired the platform with its own maintenance operation to reduce elevator and escalator unreported time. The platform connects to CMMS platforms and BMS through the Knaq API, so equipment data reaches systems facilities teams already run.

Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. paragraphs: INFODEV EDI develops and installs automatic passenger and people counting systems and has worked in this industry since 1993. The DA-Series counting sensors are stated as accurate between 97.5% and 99.5%, at door level and without a correction factor. Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. Systems come in two architectures, a classical one that yields historical data for analysis and reporting and an enhanced one that yields real-time data.

paragraphs: INFODEV EDI develops and installs automatic passenger and people counting systems and has worked in this industry since 1993. The home page describes ridership data for transit agencies that goes beyond basic passenger counts.

The DA-Series counting sensors are stated as accurate between 97.5% and 99.5%, at door level and without a correction factor. The DA-400 is a directional sensor that can be as thin as 13.5 mm for surface or inside-panel mounting above doors. The DA-200 is built to fit narrow doors and holds a single sensor in an aluminium case.

The GW-400 is a compact onboard counting computer that works with the DA-Series sensors to form an automatic passenger counting system. Data is usually transferred directly from the GW-400 via a wireless module to the ground data analysis server. INFODEV EDI also offers a software package alongside the counting hardware. Systems come in two architectures, a classical one that yields historical data for analysis and reporting and an enhanced one that yields real-time data.

paragraphs: collectionHQ sells software that public libraries use to select, manage and promote their collections. paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. They capture vibration, temperature, runtime, and operational behavior, and the stated install time is 30 to 120 minutes on legacy and modern equipment. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Knaq describes the equipment it monitors as critical infrastructure across airports, transit systems, hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. For transit agencies the stated value is early identification of failures that lead to station outages and accessibility violations. Large real estate portfolios are listed as another buyer group, with tenant disruption and contractor performance named as concerns.

The about page names Sound Transit as a client that paired the platform with its own maintenance operation to reduce elevator and escalator unreported time. The platform connects to CMMS platforms and BMS through the Knaq API, so equipment data reaches systems facilities teams already run.

paragraphs: LeakZon, established 2023, develops an analytical solution that reduces the water loss rate, also known as Non-Revenue Water. It collects and analyzes raw AMR, GIS maps, CIS and other relevant environmental data. Proprietary AI tools optimize the District Metered Areas and detect water anomalies such as leaks, metering inaccuracies, unauthorized consumption and abnormal usage.

Continuous analysis of meter and SCADA data flags leaks, bursts and night-flow anomalies as soon as they appear. The platform creates virtual DMAs that split a water network into virtual zones without physical works or new sensors. An onboarding wizard gathers data from GIS, meters, SCADA, billing and other sources and builds a digital picture of the network. Once onboarded, the platform monitors the network around the clock and turns each anomaly into a managed issue. The platform follows the AWWA M36 water audit methodology, classifying every drop from system input volume down to revenue and non-revenue water.

The homepage states that LeakZon serves the whole water ecosystem. Utilities are the audience for the alerts, dispatching crews to the locations the AI pinpoints. Water service providers are a second named segment, with LeakZon offered to them as a value-added service. LeakZon already operates across the United States, including Texas, California, Illinois, Pennsylvania and Florida.

quote.text: NRW is not only a water loss problem. It is a capital allocation failure caused by poor operational visibility.

paragraphs: InfraHub sells road management software, with a pavement survey that applies ASTM D6433 standards to identify distresses and calculate Pavement Condition Index from 0-100. Asset inventories cover roadside asset mapping and condition assessment, with 20+ asset types available, from stop signs to guardrails, sidewalks, and bike lanes. The road management platform provides tools for end-to-end management of maintenance workflows, including planning and job creation tools and a work management system for tracking project progress.

Data collection uses 360-degree cameras that gather image, GPS, and telemetry data along a road network. Images are processed by AI models that create inventories by identifying and assessing pavement distresses and road assets. Data from the cloud is surfaced in a web application where users can view, edit, and manage their road network. Generated data can be exported in formats including shapefiles and Excel files, and imported into any GIS software.

The pages name State DOTs, City and County DOTs, Municipal DOTs, DPWs, and MPOs, Civil Engineering Firms, and Regional TPOs as the groups served. Pricing is based on a per-mile rate tailored to the set of assets and distresses a customer needs identified. A 1,000-mile road network is typically processed within one month.

paragraphs.text: Reasons given for choosing the service include results correlated to IRI.

paragraphs.text: The page names county and municipal public works agencies as one group served.
paragraphs.quote: County and municipal public works agencies

paragraphs.text: Pavement maintenance service providers are named as the other group served.
paragraphs.quote: Pavement maintenance service providers

before.name: Job Machine
before.why: The four pages state plainly what the product does at each step, who it is built for, and how it is priced, so a write-up needs nothing beyond them; they carry no founding date, headcount or named customer organisation.
before.evidence: https://jobmachine.com

paragraphs.text: Job Machine sells an AI service that runs the job search for the people an organization is responsible for placing.
paragraphs.quote: How Job Machine runs the job search for thousands of people at once.

paragraphs.text: The service tailors each resume, searches job boards and company sites, applies on the candidate's behalf, schedules interviews, preps the candidate, and captures the offer letter and verification of employment.
paragraphs.quote: We capture the offer letter and verification of employment.

paragraphs.text: Onboarding is mostly text based, and each person completes a guided intake in under three minutes.
paragraphs.quote: Each person completes a guided intake in under three minutes, mostly over text, with no app to learn.

paragraphs.text: The buyers named on these pages are career colleges, community colleges, workforce boards, American Job Centers, veterans services and outplacement programs.
paragraphs.quote: Trusted by career colleges, workforce boards, and American Job Centers nationwide.

paragraphs.text: For workforce boards, AJCs and one-stops, the stated outcome is placing more people without adding staff.
paragraphs.quote: Place more people. Without adding staff.

paragraphs.text: Job Machine states that offer letters and verification are captured automatically and that proof of placement sits in the buyer's own system.
paragraphs.quote: Offer letters and verification captured automatically, not chased.

paragraphs.text: Pricing is consumption based, charged per activated candidate when someone onboards and applications begin.
paragraphs.quote: Consumption-based: you pay per activated candidate, only when someone onboards and we start applying for them.

paragraphs.text: Job Machine states that it passed government security and IT review, with no long-term commitment and payment only for activations.
paragraphs.quote: No long-term commitment Pay only for activations Passed government security and IT review

paragraphs.text: The homepage reports a pilot where placement went from roughly 10% to over 55%, and an average of 28 days from onboarding to a job.
paragraphs.quote: In a pilot with a workforce center serving dislocated workers, placement went from roughly 10% to over 55%, in the final 90 days before fiscal year end, with no new hires.

quote.text: We automate every step of getting a job. Except getting dressed for the interview.

paragraphs: LineVision sells an integrated intelligence platform that delivers Dynamic Line Ratings and Situational Awareness for transmission networks. Dynamic Line Ratings covers real-time and forecasted transmission capacity at every span across networks. Forecasted ratings extend hourly up to 240 hours, or 10 days. Items listed under Dynamic Line Ratings include FERC 881 and NERC FAC-008 compliance.

Situational Awareness provides real-time monitoring of physical risks and environmental conditions on critical transmission lines. That monitoring runs on RS-1 sensors that gather continuous, hyperlocal data around critical transmission rights-of-way. Detection and alerting cover conductor hazards including galloping, clashing, asynchronous motion, and unusual sag. Other alerts listed cover conductor icing, fallen trees, and unauthorized people or equipment in the ROW.

LineVision states that it works with 7 to the 10 largest utilities in the US. Named customers on these pages include National Grid, Xcel Energy, Avangrid, and New York Transco. Service capabilities listed include 24/7 customer support for operational DLR and EMS integration described as NERC-CIP compliant. The home page states that LineVision solutions are US-domiciled and NERC-CIP approved, with the SMS certified to ISO 27001:2022.

paragraphs: Munibit sells a website platform built for local governments, described on the homepage as built exclusively for small municipalities and counties. Document management, public notices, online payments and accessibility support are listed as built in and included without third-party plugins.

The pages name small local governments as the customer, listing cities, towns, townships, villages, boroughs, and counties. The platform is built to support WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, which the about page says aligns with ADA Title II requirements for local government websites.

paragraphs: MuniPro sells a workstation for municipal finance built on the record of each issuer's debt, covering every series and maturity, every refunding and defeasance, and obligations that never carried a CUSIP. Fourteen named tools sit on one system of record, and market data is sourced and stamped so results are reproducible.

The workspace groups debt management, debt structuring, refunding scenarios, market data, option pricing and bond holders, each reading from the same record. Debt structuring toggles between level debt, wrap-around and ascending structures and layers reserve funds, capitalized interest and bond insurance. Option pricing runs a Black-Derman-Toy binomial tree for option-adjusted spreads with custom volatility, short-rate and curve assumptions.

Five roles share one workspace: investment bankers, underwriters, credit analysts, municipal advisors and portfolio managers. Each module replaces a single-purpose subscription on a typical desk, and bought together they are described as cheaper than any two of the legacy tools. Government finance officers are pointed to BondGov, a free sister platform for state and local issuers, with no charge for any government in the U.S.

paragraphs: Novo Solutions sells an operations management system called NovoGov, described on its site as a web and mobile cloud-based software solution for streamlining operations. The homepage lists the software as tracking and maintaining assets, receiving and processing work orders and inspections, providing customer support, and reporting on outcomes and progress. Other functions on that page include viewing assets on a map with maintenance history, and mobile or website access for citizens to submit requests and receive notifications.

The about page states that Novo Solutions has provided customer-driven web solutions since 1999, with technology and pricing scaled to a single department or across multiple departments. The same page names ShareNet as a cloud based information management system launched in 2013, with apps for work order management, asset management, and inventory management.

The case studies page describes public works and utilities departments adopting NovoGov for asset tracking, work order history, and citizen complaints. One case study describes a police department that adopted NovoGov to modernize asset and inventory management after a surprise audit revealed gaps in real-time inventory and historical records. Another describes a township road department that gained maps of assets, digital pre-trip inspections, and automated preventive maintenance.

paragraphs: NorthStar Utilities Solutions sells customer information and billing software for utilities, together with a web-based customer portal and mobile workforce management software. The NorthStar Cloud is a hosted, managed cloud solution for the complete NorthStar CIS suite. SilverBlaze is a web portal designed specifically for utilities.

The customer information system is designed for small to medium-sized utilities and municipalities. Billing can be customized to cover multiple utilities on one statement, including deregulated or alternate energy sources. The system can be hosted on the utility's own server or on the NorthStar Cloud.

paragraphs: Navya Mobility sells turnkey autonomous mobility solutions for the transportation of goods and people, supported by a full range of services. Since 2014 the company has worked on autonomous and zero-emission transport for passengers and goods. Navya Mobility names four key markets: passenger transport, logistics, ports, and airports.

One product is the Autonom Shuttle Evo 3, a turnkey autonomous mobility solution designed for cities and private sites. That shuttle offers wheelchair access and capacity for up to 15 passengers. It is described as 100% electric and completely emission-free. The other product is the Autonom Tract AT135, a self-driving tow tractor for industrial and luggage flows.

The AT135 comes from Charlatte Autonom, a joint venture created in 2018 by Navya Mobility and Charlatte Manutention. Cities, companies and industrial players are the parties these pages invite to deploy autonomous transport solutions. Deployments are described as running in multiple countries worldwide.

quote.text: Navya Mobility delivers turnkey autonomous mobility solutions

paragraphs: Nexar sells dash cams for cars, paired with a phone app that saves and backs up the footage. The range is sorted by how much of the car is covered, from front only to front, cabin and rear. Recording runs from Full HD to 4K, and models with built-in LTE send alerts and live video without a paired phone.

Pages for each camera name the drivers it is for: rideshare and delivery drivers, parents with kids in the back seat, and daily commuters. The smallest model is aimed at compact-car owners, parents passing a car down to a teen driver, and first-time buyers. The 4K model is pitched at long-distance commuters, rideshare drivers, and owners of newer or higher-value cars. Live alerts, vehicle tracking and cloud backup sit behind a subscription the pages price at $9.99 a month.

quote.text: Nexar is more than a dashcam. It watches, warns, and proves so you never face the road alone.

provenance.quote: Nexar Pro GPS Dash Cam For drivers who want the road and cabin in one classic two-camera setup. Records in 1080p with built-in GPS and saves accident clips through the free Nexar Classic app.
Every Nexar camera protects what's in front of you. The question is how much of your journey you want covered.
It features built-in LTE connectivity with a multi-carrier SIM, enabling remote live streaming, real-time alerts, and 24/7 parking mode without needing your phone.
Rideshare and delivery drivers (the cabin camera records inside the car)
Parents passing a car down to a teen driver
Long-distance commuters and road-trippers
The Nexar Connect subscription is $9.99/month. You can save 20% by choosing annual billing. Your first month is free when you activate your dash cam.

paragraphs: Novotx sells Elements XS, a GIS-driven platform that its homepage says helps local governments and utilities manage infrastructure, assets, and public services. With Elements XS Asset Management, agencies can maintain roads, water systems, fleets, facilities, and more. Connect is a public-facing portal for residents to report issues, request services, and interact with an agency.

Connect can also be customized to handle payments and permit applications, according to the same page. Elements XS is presented as purpose-built for public works and utilities, simplifying asset and work management. The company describes Elements XS as a platform where GIS is the single source of truth for everything spatial, shared through ArcGIS as live maps.

The site names County of Kauai, HI, Sunriver Utilities, OR, City of Orem, UT, and Lake Apopka Natural Gas District, FL, among its customers. Novotx says it has helped public works teams modernize their operations for over 20 years. A headline on the site reads that Novotx joins Accela to expand value across the asset lifecycle.

paragraphs: Neumo sells government automation and cloud software to state and local agencies across North America. Product lines listed on the site cover revenue compliance, justice, public administration, payments, and DMV. The company describes coverage running from revenue compliance and court management to DMV services and integrated payments.

The revenue compliance page covers tax and licensing, short-term rental compliance, compliance auditing, and unclaimed property in one system. Neumo says it connects with current financial platforms, ERP systems, and legacy databases through an API-first design, without requiring a full replacement.

The Tax & Licensing product manages multiple tax types, registrations, renewals, and payments for governments in one system. An online taxpayer portal provides access for filing, payments, and renewals, and reduces paper processing. The same page says businesses can register, renew, and pay online.

quote.text: Neumo provides software that powers transactions and interactions between government and the communities they serve.

paragraphs: Orlo sells a community engagement platform for the public sector, bringing social media management, social media listening, media monitoring and surveying together with responsible AI. Orlo works with over 400 public sector organisations, including local government and central government, NHS trusts, charities, universities and the UK Police Force. The platform is set out in three areas: social media management, voice of the community, and customer service.

Social media management covers scheduling and posting to channels including Nextdoor, Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, with analytics and a content calendar. Voice of the community combines surveys, social listening, consultations and media monitoring. Customer service handles resident enquiries through chatbots, live chat and a centralised inbox.

Orlo Insights builds on social listening and media monitoring with AI developed for the public sector. Orlo's trust indicator is described as measuring the driving factors of trust and distrust amongst citizens. Insights draws on sources reached through a partnership with LexisNexis, including online news sites, blogs and forums as well as print media.

paragraphs: OpenGov sells a cloud platform for cities, counties, and state agencies that connects budgeting, finance, permitting, and asset management in one system. The Public Service Platform brings ERP and Community Operations products together, spanning Financial Management, Budgeting & Performance, Procurement & Contract Management, Permitting & Licensing, 311 Request Management, Utility Billing, and Payroll. OG Assist is the AI assistant built into every product, helping staff find answers, draft documents, and complete guided actions across the platform.

Software is built specifically for cities, counties, and state agencies, and the pages say over 2,000 governments run day-to-day operations on it. The buyers named are cities, counties, townships, special districts, school districts, utilities, and state agencies across the United States. Compliance controls built in cover GASB, FEMA, HUD, ARPA, and FLSA, and the platform is stated to be SOC 2 compliant.

OpenGov states 4,500+ government software implementations completed, with timelines that vary by product and organizational complexity, typically ranging from 3 to 6 months. Government App Builder is a no-code platform that lets IT teams build custom forms, workflows, and citizen-facing apps, with permissions, audit logs, and version history.

quote.text: The Public Service Platform is the one-stop-shop for government software.

provenance.quote: The OpenGov Public Service Platform connects budgeting, finance, permitting, asset management, and more in one system built for state and local government, so departments run on the same data instead of disconnected tools.
The Public Service Platform brings OpenGov’s ERP and Community Operations products together in one place, so your teams, data, and workflows finally connect.
OG Assist — AI built into every product, helping staff find answers, draft documents, and complete guided actions across the platform.
Software built specifically for cities, counties, and state agencies.
OpenGov serves cities, counties, townships, special districts, school districts, utilities, and state agencies across the United States.
Compliance controls built in for GASB, FEMA, HUD, ARPA, FLSA
Implementation timelines vary by product and organizational complexity, typically ranging from 3 to 6 months.
OpenGov Government App Builder is a no-code platform that lets IT teams build custom forms, workflows, and citizen-facing apps in days instead of months

paragraphs.quote: Provides a user-friendly interface for transportation operators to manage their displays

paragraphs.text: It can be integrated with existing transit data systems so that display content is updated remotely.
paragraphs.quote: Can be integrated with existing transit data systems, allowing operators to provide real-time information to passengers and make updates to the display content remotely.

before.name: Onflo
before.why: The pages state plainly what Onflo sells and that it is built for school districts, but they name no individual customer district and no pricing.
before.evidence: https://www.onflo.com

paragraphs.text: Onflo sells a service operations platform for K-12 school districts, bringing IT, asset management, facilities, transportation, HR, telephony and workflow automation onto one platform.
paragraphs.quote: Bring IT, Asset Management, Facilities, Transportation, HR, Telephony, AI Phone Agents, AI Chatbots, and Workflow Automation together on one unified platform.

paragraphs.text: The pitch is consolidation, since districts are described as running dozens of separate service systems, one per department.
paragraphs.quote: Most districts operate dozens of disconnected service systems for IT, Facilities, HR, Transportation, and constituent services.

paragraphs.text: The core product is a service desk that captures a request on any channel, routes it to the responsible team, and measures the outcome.
paragraphs.quote: However people reach out, Onflo captures it, routes it to the right team, and measures the outcome

paragraphs.text: The platform pages describe IT service management with automated ticket routing, self-service resolution and SLA tracking.
paragraphs.quote: AI-powered automated ticket routing and self-service resolution

paragraphs.text: A separate asset management product holds a central record of district hardware and tracks each device from setup to retirement.
paragraphs.quote: Central repository for managing all IT hardware assets

paragraphs.text: The pages also list integrations with SIS, HRIS, MDM, finance and ERP systems.
paragraphs.quote: Supercharge your service operations by integrating Onflo with all enterprise systems: SIS, HRIS, MDM, Finance, ERP & more.

paragraphs.text: The stated buyer is the school district, and the pages say the product is built for districts rather than adapted from generic enterprise software.
paragraphs.quote: Unlike generic enterprise platforms adapted for education, Onflo is built specifically for how school districts deliver service.

paragraphs.text: Requests handled are not limited to IT, and include transportation, HR and facilities work.
paragraphs.quote: Grow synergies and split tickets across IT and non-IT requests covering transportation, HR, facilities and more.

quote.text: Onflo replaces fragmented service delivery with one connected operating platform for the entire district.

paragraphs: Placemetry drives a city and captures photos from the public right-of-way, then analyzes properties and roadways with AI so departments can get ahead of problems rather than react to them. Each vehicle is equipped with three high-resolution cameras, one facing forward and one facing to each side, capturing street-level imagery in a single drive. Forward-facing cameras deliver per-segment pavement condition, an asset inventory, and safety screening in a single pass.

Side cameras capture a wide view of the public right-of-way in one pass, including properties, yards, sidewalks, trees, and vegetation. The same dataset feeds Code Enforcement, Economic Development, and Forestry & Parks. All imagery is captured from the public right-of-way, faces and license plates are blurred, and the city owns the data.

One cadence is a single citywide survey with no subscription required. Another is a quarterly or bi-annual citywide sweep in which Placemetry teams drive every street and the AI scores properties. A third option puts cameras on city vehicles the city already operates, so garbage trucks and street sweepers capture passive citywide coverage. Delivery runs through direct API integrations, standard spreadsheet downloads, or a secure web app, with REST API Endpoints and Webhooks.

paragraphs: Populus sells cities a software platform for managing streets, curbs, and shared mobility fleets. Populus states that it delivers data in over 100 cities around the world. The curb side of the platform covers data analysis, regulation inventorying, and active management tools.

Parking Insights pulls curb activity data from a city's meters, payment kiosks, mobile payment applications, sensors, and cameras into one platform for geospatial analysis. It includes Rate Analyzer, which projects the financial impact of rate adjustments and estimates revenue from new rates using historical parking data. Curb Regulations turns a city's existing curb and parking data into standardized formats such as the Curb Data Specification, and keeps that inventory up to date. Cities can then publish a Curbs API to delivery companies and autonomous vehicles, with Populus providing hosting and delivery of that API.

Digital Smart Zones let a city share dynamic curb policies with commercial and on-demand delivery vehicles and launch hardware-free permit programs that collect revenue from parking activity. Mobility Manager integrates and analyzes data from shared bikes, scooters, carshare, mopeds, and other shared fleets, with live data views of micromobility in a city. A policy toolkit lets staff create permanent and temporary rules, monitor compliance automatically, and calculate fees with fleet operators.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Managed Cybersecurity & CMMC Compliance for DIB & Regulated Industries" URL is correct - fetched https://radicl.com, live, company's own primary domain, and it matches the given description 'Cybersecurity for defense suppliers' precisely: 'Fully Managed Compliance and Cybersecurity-as-a-Service' built around CMMC and NIST 800-171. ANSWERING THE SLED QUESTION YOU ASKED, and the answer is no: RADICL's own site shows no state or local government market. Its stated mission is 'Giving SMBs that serve America's Defense Industrial Base(DIB) and Critical Infrastructure (CI) affordable access to strong, enterprise-grade cyber security protection', and its defense industry page says 'RADICL provides vSOC-led cybersecurity for defense contractors in the Defense Industrial Base'. The customer logos are defense and aerospace firms (ACS, Aerial Machine & Tool, Agile Space Industries) - no state or local agencies. The only 'government' association I found is a Carahsoft reseller page listing RADICL for federal/state/local buyers, but that is an aggregator/reseller listing (deprioritized per rule 6) and Carahsoft catalogs vendors for government purchasing generally; it is not evidence RADICL sells to SLED. RECOMMENDATION: the URL is right, but RADICL appears to be a federal-defense-supply-chain vendor

paragraphs: Rain adapts military and civil autonomous aircraft to perceive, understand, and suppress wildfires. The company says the technology equips fire agencies with a new layer of safety for human-piloted missions and supports command of a network of uncrewed aircraft prepositioned in remote areas. Its wildfire mission autonomy system perceives the fire, reads its behavior, size and direction of spread, and uses that information to design a suppression strategy.

Rain and Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, have demonstrated autonomous wildfire suppression technology in a representative wildfire environment in California. That work included communication interoperability of an autonomous aircraft with a human-piloted helicopter in the same Fire Traffic Area, supervised by an Orange County Fire Authority air tactical group supervisor aircraft. The two companies also said they would explore how Sikorsky's MATRIX autonomy suite operating with Rain's Wildfire Mission Autonomy System can launch uncrewed helicopters to drop water on wildfires within minutes of detection.

Rain announced a partnership with Brothers Air Support, a private Black Hawk firefighting operator, to equip their helicopter with Rain's wildfire perception system. The work goes back to 2019, when Bryan, Ephraim and Max started building the MK1 prototype. That prototype produced a fully autonomous demonstration of a drone system detecting and suppressing a wildfire ignition in approximately 40 acres of forest.

paragraphs: PSD Citywide sells an enterprise SaaS platform to municipalities and public sector organizations, unifying asset management, maintenance, permitting, planning, licensing, budgeting, and GIS in one system. The Citywide Platform shares data across all modules rather than relying on third-party applications.

Citywide Assets tracks roads, water, fleet, facilities, and linear assets with condition assessments, GIS integration, and capital planning. Citywide Maintenance is a CMMS covering work orders, inspections, and preventive maintenance across roads, facilities, and utilities. Citywide EGIS is a managed GIS server environment with desktop and web access, and a viewer module inside the platform maps assets and starts service requests from a location.

Advisory services are aimed at asset-intensive organizations including local governments, water and wastewater authorities, and parks and conservation authorities. Departments named include public works, utilities, finance, parks, and facilities. PSD Citywide is listed as an approved Sourcewell vendor.

paragraphs: Quarterhill designs, develops, and deploys technology systems for the intelligent transportation systems industry, with a presence throughout North America and Europe. Its tolling work covers toll collection, and its safety and enforcement work covers commercial vehicle enforcement, freight compliance, and active transportation management. Multi modal solutions cover container tracking and port planning, border crossings, and axle-load and track monitoring on rail lines and highway corridors.

Rail products built on Sensor Line fiber optic sensors cover speed measurement, weigh in motion, flat wheel detection, track bed analysis, axle and wagon counting, and vibration analysis. These sensors are used for predictive maintenance and for detecting changes to track and rolling stock.

Customers named on the site include government agencies, toll operators, and private sectors, along with Departments of Transportation, logistics providers, local governments, and law enforcement agencies. Enforcement agencies use the commercial vehicle inspection technologies in over 2000 lanes worldwide to prevent weigh station congestion. The company handles over 2 billion toll transactions each year for toll authorities in the United States.

before.name: PRG Insight
before.description: Performance measure data collection and dashboard system for federal grantees, including SAMHSA SUPRT and SPARS reporting - exhibited at NatCon 2026

after.name: PRG Insight
after.description: Performance measure data collection and dashboard system for federal grantees, including SAMHSA SUPRT and SPARS reporting - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: PRG Insight is a data management and visualization system built for organizations that receive federal grants. The system collects performance measure data and structures it in dashboards describing client characteristics, participation, and targeted behavior change. Dashboard tabs can be filtered by teams, sites, or dates for site-level performance analysis or funder inquiries about specific performance periods.

The pages address CSAT and CMHS grantees using GPRA and NOMS for client-level data collection who are required to use SUPRT. The Insight system is described as including an electronic SUPRT form, follow-up and tracking alerts, and automatic upload to SPARS. Automated uploads to federal performance measure portals are presented as removing duplicate data entry, with validation tools built into the data entry tools.

Training for the electronic data entry tools and dashboard system is offered through web-based tutorials, a user guide, and an email help desk. PRG Insight comes from The Policy & Research Group, a research and evaluation firm that conducts data collection and analysis for SAMHSA-funded grant projects. Partner Feedback on the page carries testimonials attributed to a Data Evaluation Coordinator at the Minnesota Department of Human Services and to a director at Odyssey House Louisiana.

quote.text: Reduce the burden of performance data reporting and visualize structured data

provenance.quote: PRG Insight is a data management and visualization system that empowers agencies to make data-informed decisions.

paragraphs: RunwayStats sells an airport traffic tracking system built on a receiver placed on the airfield and a dashboard, so that every aircraft touching the airport is counted, identified, and stored. Every takeoff, landing, touch and go, go around, helicopter operation, and airspace transition at the airport is detected automatically and logged in real time. Each logged operation carries the time, registration, callsign, runway used, weather conditions, aircraft make and model, and owner, and the data can be filtered, searched, and downloaded to CSV.

Reports run for any day, month, or year on demand or on a schedule, with delivery to an inbox, a board, or a state DOT. Stretches of road are then compared and ranked by quality, and color-coded on the web-based platform.

The about page traces the company to a founder who was offered audio only tools despite having significant residual vision.

The app is offered in two forms, ReBokeh for Organizations and ReBokeh for Individuals. ReBokeh All-Access uses geofencing technology to unlock the full set of features for anyone in a partner space, on their own personal device.

The home page carries testimonials naming MIA, the Houston Museum of Natural Science and the Art Museum of South Texas. A quote from the Miami-Dade County Mayor says that MIA is the first airport in the world to provide the app to travelers with vision challenges.

paragraphs: RedZone Robotics sells robotic sewer inspection, large-diameter cleaning, and asset management for underground wastewater infrastructure. paragraphs: Reassurance Solutions sells ReassureHub, a cloud-based correctional health monitoring platform that aggregates data from contactless vital sign sensors and wearable devices into a single real-time dashboard. The contactless ReassureSense (XK300) sensor monitors heart rate, respiratory rate, motion, and presence without a wearable or physical contact. The ReassureBand adds a wearable option for individuals who may move throughout the facility, and its data streams into the same dashboard. ReassureAID is an overdose response kit integrated with ReassureHub for teams responding to abnormal vital-sign readings.

Reassurance Solutions says the platform is deployed in county jails, state correctional facilities, and regional detention centers across the United States. The site states deployment in over 200 correctional facilities across the United States. The platform is described as giving jail administrators and medical staff continuous visibility into inmate health. It is also described as built for the way correctional facilities actually operate and designed to be used by officers, not just medical staff.

Listed features include cell-level and block-level monitoring views and automated incident logs with timestamped response records. The platform is presented as integration-ready for jail management systems, with HIPAA-compliant data storage and role-based access controls. Pricing is presented on the site as inmate vital sign tracking beginning at just $1 a day.

paragraphs: Rep'd describes itself as the AI communications platform for local government. The platform offers short video messages that staff send to residents, with built-in CRM tools and email templates. Residents submit questions, and typeahead suggestions route them to answers that already exist.

Recording runs through a teleprompter mode meant for one take. A question can be shared with any staff member, which the site presents as a way to highlight experts on staff. The pages also list a real-time analytics dashboard for seeing what residents care about. A social media management suite is listed for creating, sharing and tracking posts.

Rep'd was built by Mike Baumwoll and Mark Friese, who worked together at Twitter. The founders describe the product as an AI-powered video chatbot that humanizes local government. Officials quoted in the case studies include a city manager and a mayor.

paragraphs: SilverRide runs an assisted transportation platform for older adults and people with disabilities, licensed as a Transportation Network Company in 18 states. The driver network is made up of credentialed independent contractors using their own vehicles across 35+ major metro areas.

The company works three ways: paratransit partnerships with transit agencies, contract services for PACE and healthcare organizations, and direct booking for riders and their families. For transit agencies the service is ADA-compliant paratransit at scale, including complementary service, overflow capacity, premium tiers, and same-day trips. For PACE programs and healthcare organizations the service is door-through-door, with the driver escorting riders from inside the pickup location into the destination.
SilverRide was founded in 2006 by Jeff Maltz and Susan Steiner Saal. The company reports more than one million rides every year with 95% on-time performance.

paragraphs: SmartCover sells remote monitoring and controls for sewer, lift stations and stormwater infrastructure. The company describes the offering as turning real-time remote infrastructure data into insights for utility customers who want to minimize OpEx and reduce CapEx. Stated uses include overflow prevention, cleaning schedules, I&I identification, and chemical optimization.

The pages present satellite communication as what keeps the system visible. Alarms and notifications are described as giving advance notice so staff can prepare and respond. Installation is described as needing no confined space entry, with the work done in shop. A mobile app is offered, with system insights available wherever the user is.

A published case study covers the City of Kelowna in British Columbia. That city is described as using the technology for overflow prevention, optimization of high frequency cleaning, and ongoing I&I studies. Other departments in the city are described as using it for H2S monitoring, leachate at the solid waste facility, and stream level monitoring.

quote.text: Uninterrupted visibility of the system reduces risks, avoids damages and fees, and encourages efficiencies.

paragraphs: Spider Strategies sells Spider Impact, a strategy management product that its homepage says can gather data in one place, update it automatically, and provide insights toward shared goals. The homepage describes connecting top-level strategy to departmental priorities and team-level performance so that work at each tier is visible. Listed capabilities include visibility into key performance indicators and strategic initiatives, with tracking of progress and trends. The site also describes visualization tools that turn strategic data into charts, graphs, and interactive maps.

The homepage places the product across industry, government, and nonprofit. The about page states a mission to help businesses, governments, and nonprofits improve their performance. A customer story on the homepage credits Spider Impact with providing a transparent Common Operating Picture for the U.S. Army.

Spider Strategies began as a software consulting company and entered the Corporate Performance Management market in April 2004 with a product called Scoreboard. In September 2020, the company released Spider Impact, bringing QuickScore and Scoreboard together into one performance management solution. The company describes a worldwide network of partners, some of whom resell the software.

before.name: HydroPoint Data Systems
before.description: WeatherTRAK smart irrigation and water management for public agencies

paragraphs: HydroPoint sells smart water management covering both indoor and outdoor use. That means round-the-clock water use analytics and leak detection alongside irrigation control. Two irrigation brands sit under the company: WeatherTRAK, for portfolio-wide remote management and visibility, and Baseline, which offers sensors and two-wire technology.

A third product, WaterCompass, provides real-time visibility into indoor water use. The company says its solutions typically deliver payback in as little as 24 to 36 months. It also claims benefits past the water bill, including reduced labor and operational costs and prevention of overwatering.

HydroPoint was founded in 2002 by technology entrepreneurs Chris Spain, Peter Carlson, and Chris Manchuck. In 2016 it expanded by acquiring Baseline Systems. One published case study reports that the City of Boise has seen up to 70% water savings on its Baseline sites compared with previous watering methods. Across its customers, the company reports saving over 27 billion gallons of onsite water and over $213 million in water costs in 2025.

before.name: Edulog
before.description: Longtime standard for school bus routing and planning software

paragraphs: Edulog sells transportation software that school districts use to route buses, track vehicles, and account for the students who ride them. The company presents routing and planning as the base of the system, with add-on modules layered on top as a district needs them.

Alongside the software, an advisory group takes on the questions districts face away from the keyboard, such as reducing transportation costs. That group is staffed with former district transportation directors and data analysts. Its work covers bell-time optimization, district policy and contract analysis, demographics and redistricting, and operational assessments.

Edulog states that it created the first routing and planning software for school districts more than forty years ago. By its own account, its client districts run from as few as 57 students to as many as 1.8 million. It reports work with districts and transportation providers across 49 US states and four Canadian provinces.

paragraphs: RideCo sells on-demand transit software that agencies use to plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing transit costs. The software covers paratransit and microtransit, and the company attributes it to patented technology.

Products listed on the site include the Passenger App, the Driver App, Operations Center, Data Insights, Profile Manager, and Flex Fleets. The Passenger App lets riders request on-demand trips, preschedule them, or book recurring rides, and it is available on smartphones and on a standard web browser. Operations Center is a dashboard suite for streamlining operations and service monitoring in a transit dispatch center, with standardized and custom reports inside it.

Customers named on the site include MTA New York City Transit, which awarded a contract for its Access-A-Ride paratransit service. Other agencies named include the Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada and Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority, both for paratransit service.

quote.text: Together with RideCo, transit agencies can transform mobility for today and tomorrow.

paragraphs: NEOGOV sells human resources software for government agencies, built around public sector hiring, onboarding, and compliance. Products named on the site include Insight for applicant tracking, Attract for candidate relationship management, and Onboard for employee onboarding.

Insight is presented as an applicant tracking system that automates and centralizes recruitment activities for public sector hiring. Insight supports civil service requirements such as minimum qualifications screening, canvassing letters, and ranked eligibility lists, according to that page. Attract is a candidate relationship management system for agencies to engage candidates who have expressed interest in government jobs.

GovernmentJobs.com is offered as a job board built for public sector recruitment, with jobs posted in Insight published there automatically. The site also lists onboarding, performance management, learning management, custom forms, background investigations, and compliance management among the functions covered.

paragraphs: AIMS is parking management software from EDC Corporation, built to handle citations, permits and field enforcement for whoever runs the parking operation. The company writes that the system is meant to scale whether the buyer runs a city, a university, a hospital campus or an airport.

Citations are entered in real time from the field, with photos, GPS coordinates and notes attached to each one. Permits can be virtual or physical, and the software carries waitlists, renewals and permit prioritization. Fixed and mobile plate recognition cameras push reads, hits and occupancy data back into the system as they happen. A self-service portal gives the public round-the-clock access to payments, permits and appeals.

The site states that more than 300 clients in the United States and Canada use the software. A move onto the platform is described as taking twelve to sixteen weeks. The company describes the system as PCI and SOC 2 compliant. It also says the developers who write the software are the ones who support it.
