paragraphs: PaymentWorks sells software that organizations use to create and maintain vendor records inside their ERP. The company describes the platform as a front door to the ERP that combines vendor onboarding and maintenance, ACH risk transfer, and check-to-digital payment conversion. It is sold into healthcare, higher education, K-12, state and local government, and enterprise.

Each vendor is vetted through what the company calls a proprietary onboarding system before a payment is approved. That onboarding sits on top of a payee network the site puts at more than 1.5 million authenticated payees. Compliance work is automated alongside it, covering sanctions checks, continuous monitoring, W9 and 1099 information, and audit trails. The site states that ACH payments made through the platform are indemnified, with additional coverage available.

Published case studies include the University of North Texas. Another describes a county that fell victim to a $2.5M scam after a request to change vendor banking details. The company says it offers a payments security warranty for fraudulent payments. Its about page introduces a leadership team including a co-founder whose patent work in data management led to the founding of the company.

before.description: Telematics devices and fleet tracking software for public fleets

hiring.note: no jobs parsed from iCIMS portal

paragraphs: CalAmp sells telematics devices and cloud software that organizations use to monitor, track, and protect vehicles, equipment, and cargo. The company describes covering the whole chain, from the user experience down to the platform and the edge devices themselves. Its telematics cloud is pitched at fleet operators, logistics companies, equipment manufacturers, and the systems integrators who build on top of it.

Devices on the vehicle collect location, speed, engine health, driver behavior, and outside sensor readings in real time. The cloud then turns protocols such as CAN bus, J1939, OBD-II, and Modbus into clean, structured output. Customers pull that data through APIs, a cloud connector, or event-driven alerts. A device management layer lets administrators assign roles governing who can view, change, or execute particular management functions. Software can be prototyped, tested, and deployed to devices over the air.

CalAmp says the platform is built for commercial fleets and software providers in construction, trucking, utilities, the public sector, and equipment manufacturing. The company states it has been in business for 40 years, with thousands of customers and more than 275 approved or pending patents. For data handling it cites SOC 2 Type II certification along with GDPR and SB327 compliance.

paragraphs: CSched sells scheduling services and software tools to public transit agencies, private operators, and school boards, whatever their size or mode of transportation. The company is the exclusive authorized reseller of GIRO's HASTUS software in North America.

Its scheduling and operations modules are built on the HASTUS platform. When an agency is short of schedulers, its Rent-a-Scheduler service supplies coverage from the short term to the long term. Training runs from foundational courses to advanced HASTUS workshops. Consulting work covers efficiency audits, labor negotiations, and tender bids. The firm also advises agencies adapting their scheduling practices for the shift to electric buses.

Transit agencies worldwide have relied on CSched since 2008. The site says more than 4,650 buses run every day on schedules developed with its software or services. CSched calls itself the only consulting firm fully dedicated to public transit scheduling. It operates globally with a strong presence in North America, serving agencies, school boards, and private operators. Its experts are described as bringing over 100 years of combined hands-on experience.

paragraphs: Forerunner sells software it calls a geospatial intelligence layer. The platform unifies geospatial data, field operations, and AI-powered workflows in one place. Local government is a core buyer, with compliance work across stormwater, floodplain, and code enforcement programs. The company also markets to energy and infrastructure operators handling inspections across active sites and assets.

At the base sits a map-first view holding every asset, permit parcel, violation, and environmental layer. On top of it run configurable workflows for inspections, permits, violations, and grant tracking. Inspection findings then generate corrective actions, and permit deadlines trigger notifications. The company says adoption brings no rip-and-replace projects and no major workflow disruptions. It claims teams are up and running in weeks.

Published case studies name the Puerto Rico Planning Board, which the company says replaced paper forms and spreadsheets for field inspections and code compliance. Another states that Lee County saves approximately 16 hours of staff time per week. A further case study describes Ponce Inlet centralizing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System workflows to reclaim 10 or more hours per week.

before.name: Cylus
before.description: CylusOne rail OT cybersecurity: threat detection for signaling, trackside, and onboard networks

paragraphs: Cylus makes cybersecurity software for railways, built to continuously monitor, detect, and protect every layer of rail operational technology. Its product, CylusOne, covers mainline, urban, and freight rail operations.

The system integrates passively into an operator's network and existing monitoring tools. It automatically discovers and classifies all assets in the operational networks. Vulnerabilities are prioritized and scored by analyzing their severity in the rail environment. Detection runs continuously using deep packet inspection and machine learning to identify and classify threats across railway and IT protocols. Coverage reaches trackside and wayside networks, train-to-ground communications, operational control and maintenance centers, and station networks.

The company says the product lets operators prove compliance with frameworks including IEC 62443-3-2, NIST 800-82, and EN TS 50701. It describes CylusOne as the first rail cybersecurity solution certified to IEC 62443-4-2 at Security Level 3. Cylus says it works with technology providers, integrators, and rail experts worldwide. For passenger rail, detection is tuned to separate expected supervision and control traffic in ERTMS environments from anomalous behavior.

quote.text: CylusOne enables teams to investigate and contain threats without disrupting service, integrates with existing SOC processes, and keeps freight rail operations at the center of decision-making.

before.name: Gatekeeper Systems
before.description: Intelligent video, AI stop-arm analytics, and cloud safety platforms for transit and school districts - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026, NAPT Summit 2026
before.source: APTA 2026; AAAE 2026; CTAA EXPO 2026; NAPT Summit 2026

paragraphs: Gatekeeper Systems sells video recording and data systems for transportation, meant to make travel safer for children, passengers, and public safety personnel across several modes. The company says it uses AI, video analytics, thermal cameras, and mobile data collectors to inter-connect public transit assets within intelligent transportation systems.

Its mobile data collectors gather video and audio along with GPS tracking and door open and close events, analyzing the data on the bus itself. Those units are ruggedized and crashworthy, serving as black boxes that hold data for accident investigations. Recorders take analog and IP channels at up to 1080P and 30 frames per second, with independently selectable resolutions. Drive caddies have passed MIL SPEC 810F for shock and vibration, and a thermal system warms the hard drive to its prescribed operating temperature before writing or reading in cold weather.

Fleet software called G4 Vision centralizes system health checks, driver behavior analysis, video management, live streaming, GPS, routing and mapping, and student tracking. An Automated Lane Enforcement product for transit buses is named on the home page. The company describes a Platform-as-a-Service business model. Testimonials on that page are attributed to school district transportation directors.

quote.text: Smart video and data solutions for transit and rail safety and effeciency.

provenance.quote: intelligent video and data solutions designed to provide a safer transportation environment for children, passengers, and public safety personnel on multiple transportation modes

paragraphs: MPS sells smart parking technology products for cities, campuses, and marinas. The SafetyStick platform is built to enforce illegal parking, improve parking behavior, and keep streets safe at no cost. The MPS Meter uses LPR technology and charges only for the time used when a parker leaves.

The sticks run on solar-generated energy, and each stick has a solar panel designed to operate around the clock. paragraphs: PayByPhone sells a mobile app for paying for parking in a few taps, without coins or hunting for the machine. It is available in over 1,200 cities across North America and Europe, including universities and colleges.

A driver connects a credit or debit card to a PayByPhone account and pays from the phone. Where available, Google Pay or Apple Pay can complete the transaction instead. A session can be extended from the app, with no need to run back to the car to feed the meter.

The company dates its start to 2001 and a plan to take the pain out of parking. It now describes a mission spanning three continents. The home page puts all-time users at more than 125 million. Ownership sits with Lightyear Capital, a New York-based private equity firm with over US$8 billion in assets under management. The press page also announces a global partnership with SKIDATA covering parking and access control solutions. Jonny Combe is named as President and Chief Executive Officer.

before.name: Axon Vibe
before.description: Mobility behavior platform powering operator apps: journey detection, BIBO ticketing (built the MTA app)

paragraphs: Axon Vibe sells a smartphone-based, multi-modal mobility platform to public transport operators and authorities. The idea is to match a rider's predicted travel patterns against real-time traffic on roads and rail, then offer more efficient and less polluting travel options.

Patented location tracking predicts what people are going to do next, and psychological communication interventions are used to shift their behaviour. Riders who respond are rewarded with travel fare incentives financed by green governmental funds, plus rewards provided by local merchants. The platform is also sold to enable automatic ticketing, incentivise behaviour change and optimise customer flow management. For cities, understanding why and how people travel in real time is presented as the basis for more accurate planning.

Door-to-door journey detection powers Deutsche Bahn check-in and be-out ticketing, for example in Greater Nuremberg. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority launched its official MTA app in March 2024. Founded in 2014, the company describes a team of more than 100 software engineers, data scientists, location analytics experts, psychologists and communication specialists. Its predecessor Endoxon delivered core technology for Google Maps and was acquired by Google in 2006.

before.name: Spare
before.description: AI microtransit and ADA paratransit operations: scheduling, dispatch, rider app, analytics - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: Spare sells operations software that a public transit agency runs its service on. The modes it covers include paratransit, microtransit and fixed route, along with asset management.

In one system an agency handles scheduling and dispatch, the rider experience, fleet health, and compliance and reporting. Because paratransit trips are often contracted out, the platform pulls trips from different providers into one place. Eligibility applications and rider records are digitized, which the company says speeds up the review process. On the fixed route side, an agency can plan service, publish a GTFS feed, build schedules and run live operations together. A voice assistant answers rider calls for bookings, arrival times and common questions.

The platform is described as built to meet ADA, NTD and grant reporting requirements. It connects through open APIs, GTFS, AVL feeds and single sign-on rather than replacing what a technology team already runs. Spare puts its reach at more than 230 communities. Its fixed route page describes coordinating a large event shuttle for LA Metro.

paragraphs: Polimorphic sells a platform for government service delivery that the company describes as carrying work from intake to resolution in one connected system. The homepage describes a voice option that can answer questions, route calls, take voicemails, or resolve common issues instead of a phone tree. Alongside the voice and chat channels, the platform page describes a native CRM for case management and a drag-and-drop workflow builder that non-technical staff can modify.

The pages say the platform works across planning, public works, finance, recreation, and more, and that leadership gains real-time visibility across departments. Published case studies name city, county and special district customers, among them Suisun City, CA, Castle Pines, CO, Polk County, NC, and the City of Tangent, OR.

One case study reports that a water conservancy district handled over 600 seasonal inquiries through the platform without a single one being transferred to staff. The platform page states that the AI ingests local municipal codes and GIS layers to answer address-specific regulatory questions.

quote.text: Polimorphic unifies operations so residents get fast answers, staff reclaim focus, and leaders finally see what's happening.

provenance.quote: From intake to resolution, manage the complicated demands of government services with one connected platform.
Faster than a resident can navigate through a phone tree, Poli can answer questions, route calls, take voicemails, or resolve common issues.
let non-technical staff modify complex service flows without IT intervention

before.name: DEVNET Inc
before.description: Property tax, assessment and county financial software for local government

paragraphs: DEVNET sells property tax and land records software to local government, under an Edge product line covering mass appraisal, assessment administration, billing, collection, permitting, records management and mapping. Its applications are meant to give a comprehensive view of the entire property tax life cycle from appraisal to collection.

The suite also reaches personal property, mobile homes, special assessments, tax calculation, distribution and delinquent tax processing. EdgeMaps provides real-time GIS integration, with configurable web maps powered by the Esri ArcGIS platform living inside DEVNET software. A public portal lets residents and outside agencies reach property and appraisal data and pay tax bills online. The maintenance agreement includes future releases, upgrades, bug fixes, training, support, travel and legislative changes at no additional cost.

DEVNET is privately held and was founded in 1997 to supply integrated software and hardware to local government. It serves over 120 jurisdictions across Illinois, Iowa, Michigan, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Virginia and Wisconsin. The company says its solution values and collects revenues for over 4.5 million parcels each year. Staff include former county government officials alongside developers. DEVNET is a member of the International Association of Assessing Officers.

before.name: Accela
before.description: Permitting, licensing, and code enforcement platform for state and local government - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NRPA 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026

paragraphs: Accela sells software that government agencies use to run permitting, licensing, and asset management from a single system. Its applications are built for individual government service workflows and can operate together or be deployed only where an agency needs them.

For building departments, intake, plan review, inspections, and permit issuance sit in one workflow rather than in separate disconnected steps. Reviewers from different departments work the same record at once, with annotations and approvals tracked as they happen. Planning teams get the same shared review model, plus automated public notice generation, hearing schedules, and agency notifications. Applicants can see where a case stands and receive consolidated feedback from every reviewing department.

The company says it has thirty years of government expertise built into the product. Testimonials on the site are attributed to municipal staff, including a chief building official in McAllen, Texas. Residents and businesses who encounter Accela through a local agency are directed to that agency rather than to the company.

quote.text: The end-to-end platform for permitting, licensing, asset management and more. Built for high performing agencies.

provenance.quote: The end-to-end platform for permitting, licensing, asset management and more.

before.name: Optibus
before.description: AI scheduling, rostering, and planning platform for bus networks

paragraphs: Optibus sells an end-to-end, AI-powered platform for planning and operating more equitable, sustainable, and efficient public transportation. The site groups its buyers into authorities and cities, operators, shuttles, and consultancies.

One platform covers everything from planning and scheduling to real-time depot operations and sharing information with drivers and passengers. Planning tools let a team plan, analyze, and optimize a network to improve service quality and performance. The scheduling side creates optimal crew and vehicle schedules. Optibus Agent runs inside the platform, connected to real operational data and built around real workflows. That agent is included for all customers at no additional cost.

The company states that it is ISO 27001:2022 certified and SOC 2 compliant, using advanced encryption. It connects with existing CAD/AVL, HR/payroll, and on-board hardware. For electric fleets it offers tools that account for battery range, charging infrastructure, and grid constraints.

before.name: eleven-x
before.description: Smart parking sensors and LoRaWAN networks for cities

paragraphs: eleven-x sells a smart parking system to cities, campuses, and private organizations. The product, eXactpark, monitors occupancy in real time and turns it into data for whoever manages the spaces.

Occupancy readings come from a sensor the company says is designed to withstand even the harshest climates. Drivers are told where available spaces are. Operators get real-time overstay alerts to support enforcement. The platform is also aimed at performance parking, dynamic pricing, and curbside management.

Buyers are municipalities, campuses, and other organizations. For public agencies and schools, the company lists cooperative purchasing through Sourcewell. eleven-x was founded in 2014 as a wireless solution provider. It is headquartered in Waterloo, Ontario. Since 2020 its focus has been parking.

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AI-Powered Solutions Helping ALL First Responders Do Their Best Work" Fetched https://www.govworx.ai. The site is branded GovWorx and the quoted headline ties it directly to the 'software for first responder agencies' description. The buyer is named precisely — 911 Emergency Communications Centers: 'We deliver AI-powered solutions that help ECCs automate tasks and strengthen, guide, and support first responders.' Named products corroborate the sector rather than a same-name firm elsewhere: the CommsCoach suite (QA and call evaluations, pre-hire testing, training and simulations, real-time call guidance) plus MedAssist for paramedics and BluAssist for law enforcement, with claimed scale of 1.2M+ evaluations monthly across 475+ customers. Own primary domain. No concerns.

paragraphs: GovWorx sells CommsCoach, an AI-powered software platform that emergency communications centers use to hire, train, evaluate and support 9-1-1 telecommunicators. It is aimed at the ECC leaders responsible for improving the performance of 9-1-1 professionals. Its modules follow a telecommunicator from candidate through career, linking HIRE, TRAIN, QA and ASSIST in one system, with PROMOTE added for choosing supervisors.

CommsCoach HIRE measures aptitude, resilience, accuracy and composure through structured testing and AI-supported scoring, with tests run onsite or remotely. QA automatically pulls every eligible call and radio transmission, matches transcripts to CAD event data and scores them against the agency's own policies. During live calls, ASSIST listens, transcribes and prompts the call-taker with the policy-specific questions the situation requires. PROMOTE is an evidence-based assessment that identifies leadership potential in supervisor candidates and pairs each result with a personalized development pathway.

An emergency communications administrator at the O'Fallon Police Department in Missouri is quoted saying call-taking compliance rose from single digits to 96% with ASSIST, APCO guidecards and complete QA. In June 2026 APCO International and GovWorx announced a partnership to bring APCO's communications protocols into CommsCoach ASSIST. In August 2026 GovWorx added NEAL, an adaptive non-emergency call handling tool that escalates to a human telecommunicator whenever judgment is needed.

before.name: GovWell
before.description: AI permitting and licensing platform: 24/7 resident assistant, AI code-compliance review - exhibited at NLC City Summit 2026, Maryland Municipal League 2026
before.source: ICMA 2025; NACo 2026; ICMA 2026; NLC City Summit 2026; Maryland Municipal League 2026

paragraphs: GovWell sells software that city and county governments use to run permitting, licensing, planning, and code enforcement work. Residents and businesses use the same system to reach services, pay, and get answers outside office hours.

Permits, plan review, and inspections are handled together in one place for staff. Licensing runs online too, with applicants filing, paying, and renewing while staff keep records and approvals on their side. Code enforcement officers track cases, schedule inspections, and follow issues to closure. The company argues that AI can do real work in these processes, reviewing applications against local code, answering resident questions, flagging violations in plans, and routing inspections.

GovWell says it was founded by the son of a general contractor who watched his father struggle to get permits quickly. Its case for existing is that local governments cannot hire software engineers at competitive salaries. Deployment strategists and configuration tooling are meant to shorten implementations against older systems.

quote.text: Then you try to file a building permit.

provenance.quote: Municipal and county governments in 40+ states use GovWell's AI-powered platform

before.name: Ridango
before.description: Account-based fare collection and validators for public transit operators

paragraphs: Ridango is a mobility technology group built around automated fare collection, payments and real-time information systems for public transport. It sells to transport authorities and operators, working with them on the efficiency, accessibility and sustainability of their transit services.

The account-based ticketing platform is modular, pulling customer management, fare models, products, media, sales channels, device control and reporting into one configurable environment. Authorities and operators are meant to define their own products and fare matrixes and push updates without waiting on the vendor. Ridango also makes the hardware, including a self-service validator that reads contactless bank cards, EMV smart cards and QR mobile tickets. A compact handheld device covers both ticket inspection and on-board ticket sales.

The group is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden and was established in 2009 in Tallinn, Estonia. It reports that more than 150 public transport authorities and operators use its systems, across more than 25 countries. Among the customers named on the solutions page is a mobility authority in Vilnius. Under recognitions and memberships the site describes the International Association of Public Transport, a non-profit advocacy organization for public transport authorities and operators.

before.buyer: transit agencies and municipalities (customers named on site include Houston METRO, SEPTA, RTC Las Vegas, MARTA, Kansas City)

paragraphs: RideCo sells on-demand transit software that agencies use to plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing transit costs. The software covers paratransit and microtransit, and the company attributes it to patented technology.

Products listed on the site include the Passenger App, the Driver App, Operations Center, Data Insights, Profile Manager, and Flex Fleets. The Passenger App lets riders request on-demand trips, preschedule them, or book recurring rides, and it is available on smartphones and on a standard web browser. Operations Center is a dashboard suite for streamlining operations and service monitoring in a transit dispatch center, with standardized and custom reports inside it.

Customers named on the site include MTA New York City Transit, which awarded a contract for its Access-A-Ride paratransit service. Other agencies named include the Regional Transportation Commission of Southern Nevada and Metropolitan Atlanta Rapid Transit Authority, both for paratransit service.

quote.text: Together with RideCo, transit agencies can transform mobility for today and tomorrow.

provenance.quote: Our software is designed to help you plan, operate, and optimize service productivity while reducing your transit costs.
With patented technology, RideCo’s on-demand paratransit and microtransit software is changing the way agencies deliver mobility to their communities.
In-vehicle driver facing application for automated vehicle location, mobile data communication, and real-time dispatch and data collection.
Using the Passenger App, riders can request on-demand trips or preschedule them in advance, book recurring rides, or schedule multiple trips at a time.
Reporting within Operations Center provides user-driven access to both standardized and custom reports.

before.name: SimpliGov
before.description: Workflow automation, online forms and eSignature for state/local agencies - exhibited at Healthcare IT Connect 2026

paragraphs: SimpliGov sells a workflow platform for government agencies, built around the applications, approvals and casework that programs run on. Its stated scope is anything that moves through approvals, whatever the department.

Intake starts with online forms that meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Program teams lay out the steps on a drag-and-drop stage builder instead of writing custom code. The engine routes applications and decisions by rule, data threshold and the agency organizational structure. Approvals are signed inside the workflow with native e-signature tools. Dashboards track processing times, bottlenecks and audit trails.

Agency examples include New Castle County processing $322.8 million in emergency grants and passing its audit with zero findings. Another describes a California city automating more than 70 workflows and saving 17,000 labor hours a month. The forms page cites a federal accessibility mandate, 28 CFR Part 35, that larger public entities must meet by April 26, 2027. The platform is described as cloud-native and meeting government data privacy, security and accessibility mandates.

paragraphs: Piper Networks is a rail engineering solutions provider and systems integrator working in transportation technologies. Five primary product lines cover Vital Train Positioning, Maintenance of Way (MOW) Protection, Automatic Train Protection (ATP), Grade Crossing Safety, and Passenger Information Display Systems (PIDS). Those systems combine real-time location technologies including UWB, BLE, GPS-RTK, LTE, RFID, HD cameras and LiDAR.

Amtrak selected the Limits Compliance and Collision Avoidance System (LCCAS) to protect and monitor Maintenance of Way vehicles. Piper is equipping Amtrak vehicles in the Northeast corridor with LCCAS devices and delivering real-time telematics data to the dispatch system. Piper developed the technology behind the MTA countdown clocks at B Division station platforms and mezzanines. Piper and Thales were awarded a Pilot Program for an Ultra-Wideband Based Train Control System to be installed on the 7 (Flushing) Line.

The UWB train control system received a CENELEC Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL-4) Certification from independent safety assessor TÜV SÜD. Piper states that its multi-sensor system has an accuracy of less than 5cm.

quote.text: Piper provides advanced solutions for train navigation, MOW vehicle protection and railway safety.

Piper is equipping hundreds of Amtrak’s rail-bound and hi-rail equipped vehicles in the Northeast corridor with Piper’s advanced LCCAS devices and delivering real-time telematics data to Amtrak’s dispatch system.
Piper developed the technology that runs the new MTA countdown clocks at B Division station platforms and mezzanines.
Piper, in partnership with Thales, was awarded a Pilot Program for an Ultra-Wideband Based Train Control System to be installed on the 7 (Flushing) Line.
Recently, Piper Networks received a CENELEC Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL-4) Certification for its Ultra Wideband (UWB) train control system from independent safety assessor, TÜV SÜD.
Piper’s multi-sensor system has an accuracy of less than 5cm; ample precision for busy train yards and work zones.

paragraphs: Blaise Transit sells software for running transit without a fixed route or a fixed schedule. It was built to equip municipalities, cities, transit agencies, and transit operators. One platform covers demand-responsive service, paratransit, fixed-route integrations, and private shuttles.

The system comes in three parts. Blaise Engine lets operators set the vehicles, drivers, stops, and payment options that make up a transit system. A passenger app is available on Android, iOS, and as a website, where riders book, pay, and follow live vehicle locations. A driver app supplies turn-by-turn navigation on optimized routes and a passenger manifest at each stop. A separate simulations service recommends which transit models to implement and the parameters for each service.

Blaise was started in 2018 by a small group of transit-loving engineers. The site says more than 70 communities have chosen it to optimize their transit services. It reports working with agencies serving a few hundred rides a month up to a few million. Its optimization models are described as patent pending and customizable.

paragraphs: Chevin Fleet Solutions sells FleetWave, fleet management software meant to be the single source of truth for a fleet. The promise to buyers is to save time, save money and stay compliant.

FleetWave is described as a single, integrated platform that connects every part of operations to give teams full operational control. A code-free integration tool called Smart Integrate comes as standard. SmartForms builds custom forms, automates processes and captures data in real time at no extra cost. FleetWave Driver is a mobile application included within the SaaS subscription. Field teams use it for bespoke forms, data capture and virtual paperwork on the go. The software comes in three editions, Lite, Core and Advanced, for businesses of any size or complexity.

Chevin describes itself as a UK-based business with global reach and hundreds of North American clients. It says it manages over one million vehicles and associated assets across the world. It lists ISO 9001 and ISO 27001 accreditation. Offices are named in the United Kingdom, United States, Australia, France and Belgium.

paragraphs: Knaq sells hardware sensors and cloud software that monitor industrial equipment which is not otherwise connected. The sensors are made in house, installed without invasive work, and send data over cellular connections. They capture vibration, temperature, runtime, and operational behavior, and the stated install time is 30 to 120 minutes on legacy and modern equipment. A cloud dashboard shows live status and asset health across a portfolio, and machine learning models identify early signs of degradation before failures occur.

Knaq describes the equipment it monitors as critical infrastructure across airports, transit systems, hospitals, universities, and industrial facilities. For transit agencies the stated value is early identification of failures that lead to station outages and accessibility violations. Large real estate portfolios are listed as another buyer group, with tenant disruption and contractor performance named as concerns.

The about page names Sound Transit as a client that paired the platform with its own maintenance operation to reduce elevator and escalator unreported time. The platform connects to CMMS platforms and BMS through the Knaq API, so equipment data reaches systems facilities teams already run.

before.name: IVU Traffic Technologies
before.description: IVU.suite planning, scheduling, dispatch, and ticketing for transit and rail operators

paragraphs: IVU develops integrated IT systems for public transport, and says it has done so for more than fifty years. The customers are bus and rail operators of any size, from five vehicles to fifty and from two routes to two hundred. Its product, IVU.suite, covers planning, dispatch, fleet management, ticketing, passenger information and the settlement of transport contracts.

Timetabling runs from setting up route networks to publishing services and supplying operation control and passenger information systems. Vehicle scheduling is handled by IVU.run, which supports the entire schedule planning process. Duty scheduling merges thousands of duty elements, crewing guidelines and qualifications through optimisation algorithms. For electric fleets the system weighs charging times, ranges, route lengths and depot or opportunity charging. In daily operation it monitors vehicle status, the timetable situation and the current deployment of vehicles and staff. The whole suite is also offered as a hosted service.

The company says more than 500 customers worldwide use the standard products of the suite. Named deployments include the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority. It reports as IVU Traffic Technologies AG and has published preliminary results for the first half of 2026.

quote.text: More than 500 customers worldwide rely on the standard products of IVU.suite.

provenance.quote: IVU has been developing integrated IT systems for an efficient and environmentally friendly public transport for over 50 years.
Whether they have five vehicles or fifty, a dozen employees or ten thousand, two routes or two hundred, transport operators provide valuable contributions every day.

before.name: ClassLink
before.description: Single sign-on, rostering and usage analytics for public school districts - exhibited at CoSN 2026, EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: ClassLink sells identity, access and analytics software to school systems that have accumulated more educational technology than they can easily manage. The best known piece is LaunchPad, a single sign-on portal that puts a student or teacher's apps behind one login with multi-factor authentication.

Behind the portal, OneSync handles account creation and management and is pitched at tech teams losing hundreds of hours to that work by hand. Roster Server delivers class rosters and carries 1EdTech certification for interoperability. An add-on called DataGuard masks personally identifiable fields before roster data leaves for a vendor. A separate product, ThreatScan, watches the dark web for district credentials that have already been exposed. Analytics reports digital engagement from the district level down to the individual student.

The company says over 3,000 school systems use its products. It describes itself as the single sign-on platform chosen by over 25 million users. ClassLink states that it connects to more than 6,000 digital learning resources.

quote.text: Identity first schools are safer, faster, and easier to run

provenance.quote: From access and analytics to cybersecurity and identity management, ClassLink’s affordable and reliable solutions help you use technology in ways that promote and support learning.
LaunchPad provides quick SSO access to a personalized portal of digital apps and resources while protecting sensitive data with secure Multi-Factor Authentication
OneSync takes the guesswork out of managing student data and saves tech teams from spending hundreds of hours on manual account creation and management
Roster Server is 1EdTech Certified for interoperability
DataGuard allows schools to mask and replace key PII fields with meaningless letter scrambles before sending data to a vendor through ClassLink Roster Server.
ThreatScan automatically scans the dark web for compromised accounts linked to your school district.
ClassLink Analytics and Analytics+ present this data from the district level, down to the individual student
See why over 3,000 school systems love learning with ClassLink.
the SSO platform chosen by over 25 million users
ClassLink connects to more than 6,000 digital learning resources

before.name: Swiftly
before.description: Real-time transit data: arrival predictions and on-time performance

paragraphs: Swiftly sells a cloud platform to public transit agencies for sharing real-time passenger information, running daily operations, and improving service performance. The company puts its customer count above 200 agencies. Those agencies are described as large and small, around the globe.

The platform combines GTFS schedule data with whatever real-time vehicle location feed an agency already has. It then analyzes billions of data points to say where a vehicle was, where it is, and where it will be next. Operations staff use it to make real-time adjustments for on-time performance and headway adherence. Schedulers work from actual run times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times. APIs push the same data out to rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.

Customer service teams are another audience, answering rider questions from the same information. The site carries comments from transit staff, including an operations technology lead at the MBTA in Boston. Another comes from a transportation planner at MDOT MTA in Baltimore. Jonny Simkin co-founded the company and is its chief executive. Swiftly describes itself as a transit reliability platform meant to keep public transportation a fast and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

provenance.quote: Agencies rely on Swiftly’s cloud-native platform to share real-time passenger information, manage day-to-day operations, and improve service performance.
Trusted by 200+ agencies
Swiftly is improving public transit at agencies large and small around the globe.
Swiftly combines GTFS and any other available real-time vehicle location data in our data engine
Swiftly analyzes billions of data points to create the industry’s most accurate information about where a vehicle was, is, and where it will be next.
Boost on-time performance and headway adherence with real-time adjustments for your operators and historical insights for operations staff.
Optimize your schedule using actual run-times, vehicle speeds, and dwell times.
Swiftly's APIs make it simple to integrate with the entire transit ecosystem, including rider-facing apps, vehicle hardware, and internal tools.
your customer service team can instantly answer any question a rider has about your system

Swiftly is a transit reliability platform to keep public transportation a fast, frequent, and attractive alternative to the private vehicle.

before.name: Hayden AI
before.description: Bus-mounted AI cameras enforcing bus lanes and stops for transit agencies

paragraphs: Hayden AI mounts cameras on transit buses so cities can catch vehicles that block bus lanes and stops. The system pairs vision AI with hardware built for the vehicle and reads the street around it as the bus drives.

Automated bus lane enforcement is the flagship product, meant to clear unauthorized parking and raise bus speeds. The catalog also lists automated bike lane enforcement. Double parking gets its own product, aimed at a habit the company blames for crashes and lost time on transit routes. The platform is described as identifying objects rather than people.

Cities buy it for outcomes on bus routes, and the company frames the payoff as fewer collisions. Leadership comes from artificial intelligence, data science, transportation, and government technology. The company reports six GovTech 100 wins between 2021 and 2026.

quote.text: Illegal parking or driving in bus lanes delays entire bus routes

provenance.quote: By detecting parking and moving violations with technology installed on transit buses
combines advanced vision AI with purpose-built, vehicle-mounted hardware to analyze urban environments in real time
flagship product, Automated Bus Lane Enforcement , increases transit bus speeds, efficiency and ridership by helping cities clear unauthorized parking in bus lanes
Automated Bike Lane Enforcement Solution
Just one double parked vehicle can increase the likelihood of crashes and wreaks havoc on traffic and public transit on-time performance.
mobile perception platform is focused on identifying objects, not people
Bus-mounted camera enforcement leads to fewer collisions along bus routes.
Led by a team of experts in artificial intelligence, data science, transportation, and government technology.
Hayden AI is a six-time winner (2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026) of the GovTech 100 award

paragraphs: BRINC sells drone hardware, software and services built exclusively for public safety agencies and supported by one partner. The company was founded in response to the 2017 Las Vegas Shooting. An indoor tactical drone was developed over dozens of callouts with the Las Vegas Metro Police Department SWAT team.

The company's 911 response drone responds to calls 24/7/365 and covers 200 square miles. The site says calls for service can be cleared without dispatching a unit, so drones clear non-priority calls while agencies focus elsewhere. Drones can deliver Narcan, AEDs, EpiPens, cell phones and other equipment anywhere in seconds. For tactical use, a drone can enter dangerous places, generate floor plans mid-flight and de-escalate from a distance with two-way audio.

BRINC products are deployed by over 900 public safety agencies globally to initiate contact without force. The company states its drones are designed, supported and made in the USA and are NDAA, CJIS and SOC2 compliant. It offers help across a program's stages, from policy development and Part 107/COA work to training, staffing, maintenance and upgrades. BRINC opened a Seattle, WA headquarters to scale out engineering and manufacturing.

before.name: Fybr
before.description: IoT parking sensors and smart city occupancy data for municipalities

paragraphs: Fybr sells parking technology and an operations platform built on privacy by design. It turns anonymous, real-time parking activity into the tools that run an operation and the insights to improve it. The range covers every space, facility, and curb.

The foundation is the FybrPuck, the company's own fourth-generation occupancy sensor, a compact, self-powered, wireless edge device. It covers on-street and off-street spaces, loading zones, no parking zones, ADA spaces, and EV charging stations. Occupancy status feeds real-time guidance through a mobile application, web browsers, and dynamic wayfinding signage. For enforcement, officers can be directed to potential violations rather than running continuous sweeps. Where an ordinance requires vehicle identification, license plate recognition scans vehicles for compliance. Payment is pay-per-use inside the mobile application. A dashboard tracks turnover, session duration, dwell times, rule compliance, peak demand, and utilization trends.

The homepage carries testimonials from municipal staff, one crediting the real-time enforcement app with helping officers identify issues and respond to violations. Another says the sensor technology improved parking enforcement operations in Marysville. A third says that after the parking system was implemented, spots could be found easily through the app.

before.name: Vix Technology
before.description: Fare collection and transit operations systems for agencies

paragraphs: Vix Technology builds intelligent transportation systems, automated fare collection and transit analytics. Its customers are transit agencies and operators. The company takes a modular approach so that existing partners and technologies can be embedded into a new system.

Operators get operations management tools and detailed performance reporting meant to help optimize services. Riders get live updates through physical displays, audio outputs, websites and mobile apps. Mobile ticketing lets passengers find, buy and use travel accounts, tickets and passes. The analytics side is pitched at spotting gaps in demand or late running services.

The team is over 350 people working from hubs in APAC, Europe and North America. The company says it has helped 200 cities and deployed 500,000 devices. It cites over 35 years in public transit. Vix is part of the ICM Mobility Group, which focuses on private and public transport. It lists BSI ISO certification in quality, health and safety, environment, service management and information security. It also states a commitment to net zero emissions in line with the UK government timeline.

before.name: Genfare
before.description: Fareboxes, validators, TVMs, and Genfare Link cloud fare software for 400+ NA transit agencies (SPX)

paragraphs: Genfare sells fare collection systems to public transit agencies, and describes itself as a partner to transit agencies of every size across the United States and Canada for more than forty years. Its systems cover fixed route service, microtransit, paratransit, ferries, and light rail.

The company is moving its Genfare Link platform to a fully cloud-based software-as-a-service model. Transaction, ridership, and device monitoring data from fareboxes, mobile apps, e-Fare portals, and retail channels are consolidated in one central location. For riders paying with a contactless bank card or phone, existing Fast Fare fareboxes can be upgraded for open payment, or an Open Link validator can be mounted next to the farebox. The Mobile Link application and the e-Fare online ticketing system use open APIs to work with microtransit and shared ride providers.

before.acquisition_note: Acquired by IPS Group, Inc. in Nov 2025, per Populus's own blog post: 'Populus has been acquired by IPS Group, Inc., a global leader in smart parking and curb management solutions.' Site states products/services and core teams continue unchanged.

paragraphs: Populus sells cities a software platform for managing streets, curbs, and shared mobility fleets. Populus states that it delivers data in over 100 cities around the world. The curb side of the platform covers data analysis, regulation inventorying, and active management tools.

Parking Insights pulls curb activity data from a city's meters, payment kiosks, mobile payment applications, sensors, and cameras into one platform for geospatial analysis. It includes Rate Analyzer, which projects the financial impact of rate adjustments and estimates revenue from new rates using historical parking data. Curb Regulations turns a city's existing curb and parking data into standardized formats such as the Curb Data Specification, and keeps that inventory up to date. Cities can then publish a Curbs API to delivery companies and autonomous vehicles, with Populus providing hosting and delivery of that API.

Digital Smart Zones let a city share dynamic curb policies with commercial and on-demand delivery vehicles and launch hardware-free permit programs that collect revenue from parking activity. Mobility Manager integrates and analyzes data from shared bikes, scooters, carshare, mopeds, and other shared fleets, with live data views of micromobility in a city. A policy toolkit lets staff create permanent and temporary rules, monitor compliance automatically, and calculate fees with fleet operators.

paragraphs: AngelTrax sells mobile video surveillance systems built for transportation safety. The company describes its customers as student transportation, mass transit, fleet, locomotive, and waste operations.

On a school bus, interior, exterior, stop-arm, and windshield views cover students, drivers, and transportation staff. Footage leaves the vehicle two ways, and a cellular link carries live view, active tracking, and instant notifications. Wi-Fi handles automated downloads once vehicles return to range. Video and data can be hosted by AngelTrax at its secure U.S. data center rather than handed to a third party. Its online software covers live view, downloads, vehicle location, health reporting, stop-arm workflows, and driver behavior. Driver behavior events arrive with video meant to support coaching, claims response, and accountability.

The company page dates the business to 2006. It reports 250,000 active systems operating worldwide. It also states $2.5M spent on research and development yearly. The same page describes a SOC 2 Type II-compliant data center for data security.

before.name: Ecolane
before.description: Paratransit and microtransit scheduling software for public transit agencies

paragraphs: Ecolane sells scheduling and dispatch software designed for public transit agencies that operate paratransit, non-emergency medical transportation, and microtransit services. Whichever way a trip is booked, the optimization that follows is autonomous and does not require manual intervention from a human.

The software optimizes service at the individual trip level and updates schedules as conditions change during the service day. That lets agencies account for no-shows, cancellations, delays, and staffing changes without rebuilding schedules manually. Eligibility rules, reporting, and compliance are integrated into daily operations. Managers can capture data for every vehicle, including rides per hour, run utilization, on-time performance, and deadhead. For medical trips, the platform helps agencies locate providers, verify rider eligibility, and schedule trips with vehicles equipped to accommodate rider needs.

Agencies supported by city, county, state, or federal funds are the intended buyers. The company says it is a U.S.-based company with U.S.-based product, engineering, and support teams. It states that its self-service applications are compliant with the Americans with Disabilities Act and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.1 Level AA. It also says it holds three clean Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates. The hosted service is described as providing significant cost savings for transit agencies.

Citizens and tourists can pay with smart cards, contactless Visa, MasterCard or UnionPay, mobile wallets, and QR codes.

These pages say the platform is sold to transport agencies, governments and merchants for self-service digital ticketing across their cities. For operators, account-based ticketing is described as reduced costs, improved efficiency and easier fare management. Fares can be based on route, type of transport or service, or traveller status such as student or senior.

Deployment options include on-premise, PaaS, SaaS or fully managed operations, on existing transport or merchant terminals. A case study on the platform page describes Bishkek moving away from the use of cash. Another case study describes a Ministry of Transport automating public transport fare collection.

paragraphs: Ontra Mobility sells a planning platform that transit agencies use to model travel demand and generate optimized routes and on-demand zones before committing to service changes. The platform encodes budget, fleet, service standards, and agency feedback as constraints, and builds phased rollout plans for pilots and long-term planning. Analysis tools in the platform map origin-destination trip flows, load factors by route and time period, isochrone coverage, and census data.

A second product is a white-labeled trip planner app that carries the operator's branding and ingests GTFS and GTFS-RT feeds for schedules, vehicle positions, and service alerts. Ontra also sells operations software for bus, shuttle, and paratransit services, with a monitor app for fleet visibility, a driver app, and a rider app for on-demand trips. The operations stack also includes rider and driver applications for iOS and Android plus dashboard, analysis, and admin tools.

The white-label app is aimed at transit agencies, universities and campuses, hospitals and medical centers, corporate campuses, events and conferences, and apartment complexes. Ontra Mobility partners with the City of Fresno on a Transit On-Demand Feasibility Study. Ontra was selected for Transit Tech Lab to conduct a proof of concept with agency partners including MTA NYCT and LIRR.

before.name: Acusensus
before.description: AI cameras detecting phone use, seatbelt, and speed violations for road authorities

paragraphs: Acusensus sells automated traffic enforcement systems to the road authorities and police agencies that are trying to cut deaths and injuries on the road network. Its main product, Heads-Up, detects drivers illegally using a mobile phone and captures evidence intended to stand up in a prosecution.

The same camera pass picks up other behaviours, so one deployment can address seatbelt non-compliance and speed measured at a point or averaged over a distance. A companion product sends live alerts to officers working the roadside. Assessment happens at the roadside, and images of drivers who are not offending are discarded almost immediately. Evidence that is kept is encrypted so that only the customer agency can open it.

The company says the government of New South Wales used its technology in a program enforcing against illegal phone use by drivers. Its list of delivered work includes an Arkansas speed enforcement program covering work zones. Acusensus also reports ISO accreditation for occupational health and safety, quality, environmental and information security management systems.

quote.text: Acusensus provides advanced traffic enforcement solutions to change behaviours and prevent road trauma.

provenance.quote: Acusensus provides advanced traffic enforcement solutions to change behaviours and prevent road trauma.
Acusensus Heads-Up uses patented technology to detect and capture prosecutable evidence of drivers illegally using mobile phones whilst driving.

paragraphs: Niche Technology sells NicheRMS365, a records management system for police agencies, which use it to share information and eliminate siloed systems. The company says the system captures every aspect of policing from the front line to the courtroom. It describes the product as designed for multi-agency use and calls large projects its specialty.

Sworn officers in over 180 agencies worldwide use NicheRMS365. Recent announcements on the site include South Yorkshire Police, which plans to implement NicheRMS365 to modernize crime recording and strengthen data integrity. Durham Constabulary and Warwickshire Police have each selected the system as a platform that centralizes operational data. The Toronto Police Service chose it as its records management system. Orange County, New York won a 2025 Government Experience Award from the Center for Digital Government for its NicheRMS project.

Founded in 1992, Niche Technology is a private Canadian corporation based in Winnipeg, Manitoba, with additional offices in Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom. It is wholly owned by its founders, who remain active in day-to-day operations. In the United States, NicheRMS365 is available to federal agencies through the General Services Administration Information Technology Schedule 70. It is also offered through the New York State Umbrella Contract and the Dell National Government Contract.

paragraphs: PowerSchool sells software that school districts run from home to classroom to central office, covering the records, communication, and back-office work of running a school system. The company says its software reaches over 60 million students in 90 countries.

The student information side pulls scattered records into one accurate student record, so staff and families are working from the same source. Teaching and learning products sit alongside it, among them a learning management system. For the central office, finance, human resources, and operations are brought into one connected system. A separate data practice centralizes information that would otherwise sit in district silos.

PowerBuddy, the company's AI assistant, is described as built for students, families, teachers, and administrators. It is also pitched at IT staff and data analysts working with district data. PowerSchool states that PowerBuddy won a 2024 GESS Education Award. In districts already using its products, the company says teachers are reclaiming at least 10 hours a week.

before.description: AI voice agents answering non-emergency calls for 911 centers - exhibited at APCO 2026

paragraphs: Aurelian builds software for the 911 centers known as public safety answering points. One of its two products answers non-emergency calls instantly, so callers are not left on hold. The other sits with call-takers during emergencies and gives real-time, context-aware guidance without taking control.

The automated line resolves routine calls on its own. It detects and escalates emergencies to a person. During live calls, the guidance tool surfaces the relevant SOP checklist for the incident. It also flags missing information before the call ends. The company says the system learns a center's workflows, SOPs, and systems in order to support the full call flow. Aurelian states that humans remain in control of emergencies and decision-making.

The customers page says PSAPs around the country use Aurelian to cut non-emergency workload and return time to their teams. Published stories include Hamilton County 911 automating more than 300 non-emergency calls a day. The about page says the founders, Max and James, were building call automation technology for hair salons before starting the company. That insight led them to pivot to public safety and build for PSAPs.

paragraphs: OpenGov sells a cloud platform for cities, counties, and state agencies that connects budgeting, finance, permitting, and asset management in one system. The Public Service Platform brings ERP and Community Operations products together, spanning Financial Management, Budgeting & Performance, Procurement & Contract Management, Permitting & Licensing, 311 Request Management, Utility Billing, and Payroll. OG Assist is the AI assistant built into every product, helping staff find answers, draft documents, and complete guided actions across the platform.

Software is built specifically for cities, counties, and state agencies, and the pages say over 2,000 governments run day-to-day operations on it. The buyers named are cities, counties, townships, special districts, school districts, utilities, and state agencies across the United States. Compliance controls built in cover GASB, FEMA, HUD, ARPA, and FLSA, and the platform is stated to be SOC 2 compliant.

OpenGov states 4,500+ government software implementations completed, with timelines that vary by product and organizational complexity, typically ranging from 3 to 6 months. Government App Builder is a no-code platform that lets IT teams build custom forms, workflows, and citizen-facing apps, with permissions, audit logs, and version history.

paragraphs: Tannery Creek Systems sells autoChalk, an automatic license plate recognition system built for parking enforcement work. The company describes patented size, shape, and color analysis that flags overstaying vehicles even when a license plate is not visible, presented as an alternative to tire chalking. autoChalk also verifies pay-by-plate sessions and permit-by-plate credentials in real-time as officers patrol, connecting to a customer's payment and permit providers.

The product line runs from vehicle-mounted units to a fixed camera solution for parking structures and surface lots, plus autoChalk Office for citation management and policy configuration. autoChalk Mobile scans 2 vehicles per second while driving up to 60 km/h and applies parking policy by zone using GPS and geofencing. autoChalk Handheld is an Android application for on-foot officers that issues citations in 6 steps and keeps working without cellular coverage. autoChalk Compact is a vehicle-mounted plate recognition system for operations that prefer a smaller visual footprint without the full LIDAR solution.

Tannery Creek Systems states that each customer gets a separate database on isolated infrastructure, with no shared plate network and no cross-agency search. Municipalities, downtown authorities, universities, hospitals, and private operators are named as the buyers for the product line, across the United States and Canada.

before.name: Connixt
before.description: iMarq mobile asset maintenance and MRO platform for transit, rail, and fleets

paragraphs: Connixt sells iMarq, a mobile-first application built for field crews, technicians and mechanics to digitize and automate data collection, paperwork, processes and workflows. The company aims it at fleets, rail, transit, manufacturing, heavy engineering and facilities.

There are native apps for iOS and Android. They run on phones and tablets, both online and offline. Crews record asset details in the organization's own forms, on their own devices, in real time. An assistant called iBot puts institutional knowledge, troubleshooting guidance and compliance support in front of frontline teams, while reporting lets users reach their data on any device and track asset status.

Public agency case studies include a transportation department whose traffic signal division used the customizable mobile app to digitize work orders and improve transparency. Another covers Metrolink, which automated the train delay reporting its conductors had been doing on paper. The company reports winning two Progressive Railroading Reader's Choice Awards for a second consecutive year. It is run by two co-founders, Satish and Prabhu, described as industry veterans, and the site cites a 4.8 rating on Capterra.

before.name: Recidiviz
before.description: Data and case-management tools for state corrections and supervision agencies

paragraphs: Recidiviz is a non-profit that partners with criminal justice agencies on technology and data. Its customers are state departments of corrections and the staff who run prisons and community supervision.

The Corrections Platform is modular, so an agency can replace its legacy software entirely or plug in modules as it wants them. Underneath, the organization joins disconnected agency databases into one standardized data layer that feeds the tools above it. Those tools surface people who are eligible for programs, reclassification, or release.

Day-to-day users are administrators, case managers, and officers, whom the team says it goes into the field to talk with before designing anything. The organization says it works with 19 state departments of corrections responsible for almost 1 in 2 people in U.S. prisons and on community supervision. It began as a volunteer project at Google. In 2019 it became a standalone non-profit.

before.name: Stellic
before.description: Degree planning, advising, transfer pathway and registration software for public universities, community colleges and private institutions - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Stellic makes software for colleges and universities that turns the route to a degree into something a student can actually see and an office can support. It pitches itself across the range of institution types, from large public schools and community colleges to small private and research universities.

One package tracks degree progress and gives students room to plan ahead. One is built for advisors, giving them a way to step in early rather than after a student has fallen behind. A third is aimed at transfer and prospective students, matching them to a path based on goals and the credits they already carry. Transcript processing is automated to cut manual data entry.

The company says it has supported over a million students so far. It describes itself as a partner to schools of every size. The platform is named for Mark Stehlik, the advisor who helped the founders picture the system while they were still students. The site also states that the product is certified for accessibility.

before.name: Prepared
before.description: Assistive AI for 911 centers: transcription, translation, text-to-911, and video

paragraphs: Prepared builds assistive artificial intelligence for 911 centers, aimed at the people who answer emergency calls and send help. The company states that it is now the intelligence layer of Axon 911, an emergency communications platform it describes as covering the full lifecycle of a call.

During a call the software transcribes speech as it happens, captures details automatically, and translates, so staff can watch the caller rather than the keyboard. Incoming audio is translated automatically in more than 40 languages, according to the homepage. The call-taking page claims support for over 200 languages for callers who do not speak English. Call-takers can also request a livestream from the caller to see the scene. A separate voice assistant answers non-emergency lines and converses with callers in English or Spanish.

Buyers are public safety answering points, the centers that take 911 calls. Prepared describes the product as a cloud based platform laid over existing systems, with no rip and replace required. Supervisors get automated quality assurance and keyword triggers for visibility into the operation. Its chief executive, Michael Chime, appears in a recorded discussion with three 911 leaders about non-emergency calls.

before.name: K16 Solutions
before.description: Scaffold platform for LMS migration, course archiving, and data warehousing across LMS, SIS, and CRM systems at colleges and universities - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: K16 Solutions sells data software to colleges and universities, prying campus information out of the systems that hold it and handing it back in usable shape. Everything runs on one patented platform called Scaffold, spanning data warehousing, live LMS course backup, and student data archiving. A fourth product moves online course content from one learning management system to another.

The warehouse product connects to a campus LMS, SIS, CRM, and ERP through public and private APIs. Data lands in a structure specific to higher education, so a student, a course, and an enrollment get defined once instead of differently in every report. The copy lives in the institution's own governed environment, built on Snowflake and hosted on AWS. Staff can ask in plain language, and the SQL the system writes is shown rather than hidden.

Campus customers named on the site include San Diego State University. The company reports more than 12 million courses archived, and says its founders worked together for over 18 years across multiple higher education institutions. For institutions facing audits, it lists ISO 27001 certification by Schellman, SOC 2 Type II, data masking, and FERPA-aligned handling of student records.

paragraphs: SilverRide runs an assisted transportation platform for older adults and people with disabilities, licensed as a Transportation Network Company in 18 states. The driver network is made up of credentialed independent contractors using their own vehicles across 35+ major metro areas.

The company works three ways: paratransit partnerships with transit agencies, contract services for PACE and healthcare organizations, and direct booking for riders and their families. For transit agencies the service is ADA-compliant paratransit at scale, including complementary service, overflow capacity, premium tiers, and same-day trips. For PACE programs and healthcare organizations the service is door-through-door, with the driver escorting riders from inside the pickup location into the destination.
SilverRide was founded in 2006 by Jeff Maltz and Susan Steiner Saal. The company reports more than one million rides every year with 95% on-time performance.

before.name: Littlepay
before.description: Contactless open-loop transit payment infrastructure for 400+ providers in 30+ countries

paragraphs: Littlepay sells payments infrastructure for transit, and public transit providers and vendors of all sizes use it to accept payments in person or online and simplify ticketing for passengers.

Open APIs allow flexible configuration of its capabilities alongside existing AFC and ABT fare collection systems. A single data platform gives operators visibility of passenger behaviour across vehicles, gates, kiosks, mobile apps and web. Risk models optimised across global volumes are meant to minimise losses from fraud and uncollected payments. Advanced PAN and PAR deny lists target card flipping fraud. Multi-operator brokerage services connect operators and agencies in a region under unified customer ticketing.

The company set out in 2016 with a vision to make contactless bank card acceptance faster, cheaper, and less complex for the public transit sector. It now describes working with over 400 transport and mobility providers in over 30 countries, powering payments on local buses, city networks and national public transport systems. One published case study describes Monterey-Salinas Transit deploying a contactless transit fare payment system in May 2021, the first of its kind in California.

quote.text: Why can a retail store set up a payment system in a matter of minutes for a few hundred dollars, while transit agencies take years and spend millions of dollars to do essentially the same thing?

before.name: Clever Devices

paragraphs: Clever Devices builds technology for public transportation providers, meant to help them run more efficiently, spend less and deliver the service riders expect. The company says agencies with anywhere from 50 to 5,000 vehicles have chosen it over more than thirty years.

At the center is CAD/AVL software that gives dispatchers real-time information to monitor and manage the fleet. A vehicle health monitoring product is aimed at cutting repair costs and stretching the mean distance between failures. Onboard, automated passenger announcements are synced with LED signage so riders know where they are. Service planning is handled by the MAIOR scheduling suite, a modular set of planning and optimization tools. For agencies that would rather not run servers, CleverCloud takes on the on-premises hosting burden.

The company tells an unusual origin story, beginning in the early 1980s in the basement of a bar on Long Island. It turned to transit in 1990 when the Americans with Disabilities Act passed. The first product automated the stop announcements bus drivers were required to make. Today the company reports over 600 employees across 12 locations in the United States, Canada, Brazil and Italy. It puts more than 30,000 vehicles on its transportation systems technology. The homepage announces that Hitachi Rail has completed its acquisition of the company.

profile_research.description:
Granicus sells cloud software and services that governments use to communicate with the public, publish and stream meetings, run websites and forms, and manage records and permits. Its own site frames the offering as two platforms: the Government Experience Cloud (GXC), split into Service Cloud ("Deliver services without friction"), Engagement Cloud ("Grow and activate audiences") and Operations Cloud ("Automate workflows and reduce costs"), and the Destination Experience Cloud (DXC) for destination marketing. Layered on those are Government Experience Agent (GXA), described as an AI-powered digital agent built for government, a Federal Experience Cloud, and the GXI Enterprise and GXI Foundations intelligence tiers. The solution pages group the underlying products into agenda and meeting management, websites and CMS, digital services and forms, digital communication and engagement, permitting and licensing, and public records and short-term-rental compliance. The product directory names each tool with its legacy brand in parentheses: Communications (govDelivery), Websites & CMS (govAccess, OpenCities, Intranet), Records Request Management (GovQA and GovQA Legal), Short-Term Rentals (Host Compliance), Forms & Workflow (OpenForms), Service Request Management (govService and OneView), Permitting, Compliance & Licensing (AMANDA and SmartGov), Land & Official Records (govRecords), Sentiment & Feedback (EngagementHQ), Video (self-managed, and Swagit partially and fully managed), Boards and Commissions, and agenda management under the Legistar, OneMeeting and Peak names. The buyers named under "Who we serve" are local government, state government, federal government, education, special districts, elected officials and destinations, with country sites for Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia & New Zealand, India, and Latin America & the Caribbean. Granicus also sells consulting and digital agency work through the Granicus Experience Group (GXG).

Granicus is the parent of this family rather than a member of one. Its company page states "more than 2,000 employees across the globe supporting more than 7,000 public sector organizations," and the careers page repeats "about 2,000 of us" spread across "eight countries" in a remote-first workplace; that page's "Explore roles" button points at careers-granicus.icims.com, the iCIMS board the Simpleview careers page also lands on. The homepage figure block claims 7,000+ public sector customers, 360M people in the Granicus subscriber network, 100% of U.S. federal cabinet-level agencies, 48 of the 50 largest U.S. cities, 30B digital experiences and 22B government messages delivered annually, 8B government website views, 3.5M online forms submitted, 2M record requests served and 123K government meetings streamed each year. paragraphs: Clariti sells community development software to local governments, pitched at any size and budget. One edition is permitting software for large local governments. A second, Launch, is aimed at small to mid-sized local governments. A third product, CivCheck, uses AI to guide applicants toward a complete and compliant submission and staff through every check.

The software keeps the permit counter online, where applicants apply, pay, and track status. It also tracks code violations from report to resolution, with automatic case assignment and links to local zoning and codes. Staff can build a report, adjust a page layout, or create a new permit type themselves. The large-jurisdiction edition runs on the Salesforce Platform, whose APIs let a government connect its other tools. Launch customers can copy a peer's permitting workflows using a cloning tool. On the AI side, staff have to approve every interpretation the software makes.

The company says the large-jurisdiction product was built with input from government customers over 16 years. Its home page names Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Orange County among the cities and counties using Clariti. Launch pricing is stated as based on population rather than user count.

paragraphs: Concourse Tech builds software for public institutions, tailored to how each organization actually works. The company names state agencies, cities and counties, and school districts among the bodies it serves. Its offering is organized as a module library rather than a single product.

paragraphs: Securly sells student safety software to K-12 schools and districts, bringing content filtering and wellness visibility into a single platform. The company describes itself as parents, former educators, and technologists working on school safety.

Its content filter is described as the first cloud-native filter built specifically for K-12. A safety monitoring product analyzes online activity for signs of cyberbullying, self-harm, and violence. A classroom tool lets teachers share screens, lock devices, and push resources during a lesson. A digital hall pass product now folds in tardy management, visitor management, and PBIS. A newer layer puts guardrails on student AI use in the same way the web is filtered.

Published case studies name districts such as Ysleta ISD, which the company says uses its AI transparency tools across 34,000 students. For evidence of how widely it is used, Securly cites the EdTech Top 40 report from LearnPlatform by Instructure. Its board includes a managing director from Golden Gate Capital.

paragraphs: Peregrine builds what it calls Operational AI for High-Criticality Organizations. The product is a full-stack platform that turns disconnected data into complete operational context and puts actionable intelligence in front of every person in an organization. Law enforcement is listed as a solution area, and the platform is positioned for public safety work.

The site lists organizations that include the Atlanta Police Department, the Cuyahoga County Prosecutor's Office, Eagle Fire Department, and Northern Arizona University. Also named are Manatee County Emergency Management, East Pierce Fire-Rescue, the Merced County District Attorney, and Pinellas County Safety & Emergency Services. The Fairfax County Police Department is quoted alongside a case described as a child abduction suspect identified in 13 minutes.

The platform is laid out in numbered steps: forward deployed engineering, data ingestion and enrichment, organizational context, semantic ontology, intuitive interfaces and AI, and data governance. On governance, the company states that a customer keeps complete control over its data, full visibility into how that data is used, and granular access controls. A banner on the site announces a $250 million Series D.
