before.name: Beep
before.description: Turnkey autonomous shuttle operations for transit agencies, airports, and communities

paragraphs: Beep plans, deploys and manages autonomous shuttles for private and public communities. The services answer demand for alternative modes of transportation within communities, campuses and municipalities. Routes run inside geo-fenced areas at a controlled speed.

Deployments are built around first and last-mile trips, linking retail to residential areas, remote parking to campus amenities, and underserved communities to transit stops and stations. The service portfolio runs from upfront analysis, planning and design through turnkey operation of an autonomous mobility network. Underneath sits AutonomOS, a vehicle-agnostic platform for multi-passenger autonomous mobility services. It plans service modes from fixed route to demand-responsive variants. In-cabin monitoring built on machine learning lets remote supervisors react to a passenger safety or roadway issue.

The platform is built for public transit operators and authorities. The company reports deployments in six states and two dozen deployments overall. The purpose-built shuttles carry ADA-compliant wheelchair ramps and restraints. One announced project, ATL Spoke, is a pilot with Atlanta Beltline that the company says is in service and open to the public.

before.description: Digital textbook and courseware delivery platform for colleges, universities, and school districts - exhibited at NACUBO 2026

paragraphs: BibliU sells a course materials platform to colleges and universities, automating the workflow behind digital textbooks and courseware. It also runs campus stores, pairing that content with physical and online retail.

The platform comes in three named parts: Learn, Engage and Automate. Faculty choose titles and adaptive courseware from thousands of publishers and open educational resources, so the selection stays with academics. The company says the access model cuts textbook costs by 30 to 50 percent. Students can read on any device, online or off. Staff get reporting that tracks content usage and student engagement. A separate procurement option is built for libraries, with flexible pricing and broad title access.

The site says more than 170 institutions worldwide use the company. Dual credit students are called out as one group served, with the same first-day access to required materials. Dave Sherwood is co-founder and chief executive. He started the company while at Oxford University. A case studies page collects customer stories from across higher education.

quote.text: The future of higher education is about ensuring all students have affordable access to their class content.

before.name: BusPas
before.description: Solar smart bus stops with edge AI plus the ORA platform: signage, lane enforcement, passenger counting

paragraphs: BusPas upgrades, connects and modernizes urban furniture, starting with bus stops. It equips that furniture with sensors and edge computing meant to improve transit, protect user privacy and enhance security. The buyers are municipalities and transit agencies looking to optimize operations and improve services.

The ORA Ecosystem is the platform side, giving public transit agencies, cities and their officials access to data services linked to infrastructure within their municipality. The stops display real-time bus wait times and occupancy, count waiting passengers, and track boarding and alighting to analyze connections and origins and destinations. The system can also send specific requests to control traffic lights for buses and emergency vehicles. SaferSmart Zones is a turnkey bus and transit lane enforcement offering. Solar panels are added to minimize dependence on the grid. The products are described as a modular ecosystem of solar-powered, AI-enabled street infrastructure for transit reliability, safety, enforcement and passenger experience.

The company says it started in 2017. It works through standing contracts, so new legislation or an RFP is not required. A statement on the site is attributed to the mayor of Sainte-Julie, Québec. A headline says its smart stop technology was deployed across the TTC network ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2026.

quote.text: Every city needs a digital twin to test the efficacy and impact of programs and make data based decisions.

before.name: Emovis
before.description: Tolling operations and back-office payment services for toll agencies

paragraphs: Emovis sells tolling and mobility technology and operating services to road operators and transport agencies around the world. Its remit covers the tolling chain from roadside systems and revenue collection through enforcement and customer service.

The products bring together vehicle identification and classification, data analytics and back-office software to process large volumes of tolling transactions. An operational back office takes the data captured at the roadside and makes it accurate, enriched and ready for billing. A manual image review service pairs automated processing with human checking to validate vehicle passage records. The gantry-based Identify system reads passing vehicles using video tolling or pay by plate, so no physical barrier is needed.

Buyers are public entities and private companies that need a partner to run tolling operations. The company reports more than 850 experts worldwide and over four decades of experience. It is backed by Abertis Group, which it describes as managing 5000+ miles of motorways with over 17,000 employees. Emovis says it has helped clients in the mobility and transportation industry in more than 10 countries.

before.name: CivicSmart
before.description: Smart parking meters and occupancy analytics for municipalities

paragraphs: CivicSmart sells cities a curb management system spanning smart hardware at the space, real-time intelligence on every event, enforcement, and the operations software that ties them together. It also aims at universities and campuses. Airports and transit hubs are another target, where rideshare zones, cell lots and passenger loading need managing.

Product lines run from single-space and multi-space meters with integrated sensor options. Curb sensors report real-time occupancy, plate capture, and evidence-grade detection. LaneMaster devices provide automated lane management for loading, pickup-dropoff, rideshare and commercial corridors. Officers write citations on AutoISSUE handhelds. PEMS unifies every meter, sensor, handheld and citation into one dashboard. It publishes open REST endpoints so cities can bring their own BI, GIS and analytics tools.

CivicSmart, Inc. describes itself as a Wisconsin company founded in 2015 around the idea of reimagining the curb. It says it acquired Duncan Parking Technologies from Duncan Solutions in 2015 and renamed it CivicSmart Parking Technologies. The site claims more than 1,500 cities and agencies served. It also claims more than 15 million parking meters shipped. The company says its team holds patents globally for vehicle-detection sensors and parking technologies.

before.name: Authorium
before.description: Document-driven workflow for government procurement, budget and HR processes

paragraphs: Authorium sells government agencies a platform meant to connect the flow of public funds across the administrative functions that carry it. The company builds only for government and describes itself as a public benefit company. State and local governments are named as buyers.

On the procurement side, bids are submitted, vendors scored, and evaluation workbooks kept inside the application. Contracts are tracked from request, to award, to obligation management, to renewal. Workflows, templates, rules, and role-based access are meant to be configured without an ongoing technical service contract. A legislative module imports bills and amendments, then tracks them and distributes them to departments and teams for analysis. A smaller product, Authorium Direct, covers direct and non-competitive purchasing in a single, low-cost portal. It is built on AWS GovCloud.

The company says 60% of its staff worked in government themselves. It reports having completed a SBIR phase II with the U.S. Air Force. Implementation is handled by an in-house team. Authorium says it has been named to the GovTech 100 for a third consecutive year.

before.name: ADS Environmental Services (IDEX)
before.description: Sewer flow monitoring and I&I analytics for municipal wastewater utilities - exhibited at WEFTEC 2026, StormCon 2026

paragraphs: ADS Environmental Services provides flow, level and rainfall monitoring for wastewater, storm and surface water systems. The buyers are municipal owners who need to know what is happening in their collection systems when it rains. The problems addressed include sanitary sewer overflows, sewer cleaning, combined sewer overflows and inflow and infiltration.

Monitors in the sewer feed software for visualizing, analyzing and managing the network. An agency can buy the equipment and run the program with its own staff. At the other end of the range, the company handles everything from placing the equipment to sending the alerts. A newer offering applies machine learning to spot developing blockages early enough to act on them.

Peter Petroff established the company in 1975 after a NASA career as a lunar guidance system engineer. A network of more than 400 monitors in Sydney, Australia in 1990 is described as a milestone in the company history. Product quality management certifications have been held since 1994, including an ISO 9001:2015 certificate issued by CSA Group. Offices sit across North America and Australia, with the corporate office in Huntsville, Alabama, and open roles are posted within IDEX Corporation.

before.name: Autura
before.description: Towing lifecycle software for city towing programs and impound management (ex-AutoReturn + TSD)

paragraphs: Autura sells software to the people who handle towing on public roads, from the officers and dispatchers who order a tow to the impound teams who store and release the vehicle. The company says it supplies towing management and unclaimed vehicle auction software to public safety agency leaders and towing and recovery business owners.

On the agency side, the product handles tow requests and rotation, and Autura says it gives agencies complete control over their towing program. Impound work is pulled into a single compliant system covering storage lookup, regulated fees, and lien and notification workflows. roles.title: Account Manager - Fixed Term Contract, 12 months
Business Development & Senior Key Account Manager – Paris, petite-couronne and Private Parking Operators

paragraphs: Arrive sells urban mobility technology to city governments, parking operators and businesses. On the parking side that means demand insight and digital payments for parking and EV charging.

Drivers start, stop, extend and pay for a session from an app. Operators run payment stations and in-car integrations from the same platform. License plate recognition can start and end sessions automatically as cars enter and leave. The company says its EV solutions connect with more than 400 charge point operators. For city planners, dashboards report parking use, traffic trends and mobility patterns to guide planning.

Arrive describes itself as a coming together of Flowbird Group, EasyPark Group, Parkopedia and others. The about page dates the story back to 1955. That timeline opens with Cale installing its first parking meters. Within the group, Flowbird is described as delivering mobility solutions in over 6,000 cities across 80 countries. EasyPark is described as present in over 4,000 cities across more than 20 countries.

before.name: Lightspeed Systems
before.description: Web filtering and student safety monitoring for school districts - exhibited at CoSN 2026

paragraphs: Lightspeed Systems sells a connected platform of K-12 edtech products that give schools visibility and control across safety, security, compliance, device management, and analytics. Its filter covers every digital interaction on and off the network, protecting students from cyber risks and distractions while keeping access and compliance in place.

Filtering is enforced on the device itself, with an on-device SmartAgent and SmartShield DNS filtering covering school-managed, BYOD, and IoT devices. Lightspeed Alert monitors online activity, flags concerning behaviors, and enables intervention before a tragedy occurs. Those alerts are backed by round-the-clock monitoring from the company's own safety specialists. Lightspeed Classroom gives teachers visibility into and control over student activity to minimize distractions and maximize instructional time. Lightspeed StopIt is an anonymous reporting system for safety, misconduct, or compliance concerns. An analytics product shows granular app and device usage down to the grade and student level.

The company states that 28 of the 50 largest US school districts use its software, naming Los Angeles Unified, Houston ISD, Miami-Dade County Public Schools, and Fairfax County Public Schools. It puts the wider count at 31,000 schools around the world. The filter is described as designed for CIPA, FERPA, and NIST-aligned environments, with exportable audit trails and long-term retention.

before.name: Via
before.description: On-demand transit, paratransit, and network planning software for agencies - exhibited at CTAA EXPO 2026

paragraphs: Via sells software and operating services for public transportation, working with the agencies and cities that run it. The company says it works with more than 700 partners around the world, from rural counties to large transit agencies.

Its on demand microtransit is pitched for first and last mile connections and for places with little transit service. For paratransit, the system optimizes routes and taps other accessible modes when they fit. An eligibility tool automates paratransit applications, approvals, and renewals. A planning product, Remix, is for visualizing data and testing network concepts before a redesign goes live. A student transit product provides scheduling and routing software meant to get every student to school on time.

Via also runs service itself under what it calls a transportation as a service model, rather than only supplying software. Its site carries comments from riders, mayors, agency leaders, planners, and dispatchers. A newer offering, Via Intelligence, is described as giving city and agency leaders recommendations and automations to lift efficiency and service performance.

before.name: Partage
before.description: Turnkey 'library of things' sharing programs sold to cities, property managers, and employers

paragraphs: Partage Club sells an app for sharing everyday items, and the site pitches it as a way to borrow what a household needs instead of buying it. Joining is free, and the site says a member creates a profile, finds an item nearby, requests it, and returns it. Coverage is described in terms of reimbursement up to a set amount if something happens during a share.

The homepage sorts visitors into paths for citizens, cities and municipalities, business and organization, and building your own platform. For cities, the offer is described as a fully supported, turnkey sharing solution that empowers citizens to share, save, and connect. A parallel offer aims at employees and members inside businesses and organizations. The platform option is a customized sharing platform powered by the company's technology, with infrastructure, a safety framework, and expertise supplied for deploying a sharing ecosystem tailored to an industry.

The mission page states the goal as making sharing the obvious choice so every community can unlock its collective abundance. The frequently asked questions page shows question headings for damage, late returns, giving items away, selling items, and account deletion.

paragraphs: Interloc Solutions sells consulting and software for IBM Maximo, and the company describes a complete focus on Maximo across its services. before.name: Axon Vibe
before.description: Mobility behavior platform powering operator apps: journey detection, BIBO ticketing (built the MTA app)

paragraphs: Axon Vibe sells a smartphone-based, multi-modal mobility platform to public transport operators and authorities. The idea is to match a rider's predicted travel patterns against real-time traffic on roads and rail, then offer more efficient and less polluting travel options.

Patented location tracking predicts what people are going to do next, and psychological communication interventions are used to shift their behaviour. Riders who respond are rewarded with travel fare incentives financed by green governmental funds, plus rewards provided by local merchants. The platform is also sold to enable automatic ticketing, incentivise behaviour change and optimise customer flow management. For cities, understanding why and how people travel in real time is presented as the basis for more accurate planning.

Door-to-door journey detection powers Deutsche Bahn check-in and be-out ticketing, for example in Greater Nuremberg. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority launched its official MTA app in March 2024. Founded in 2014, the company describes a team of more than 100 software engineers, data scientists, location analytics experts, psychologists and communication specialists. Its predecessor Endoxon delivered core technology for Google Maps and was acquired by Google in 2006.

before.name: IVU Traffic Technologies

paragraphs: IVU develops integrated IT systems for public transport, and says it has done so for more than fifty years. The customers are bus and rail operators of any size, from five vehicles to fifty and from two routes to two hundred. Its product, IVU.suite, covers planning, dispatch, fleet management, ticketing, passenger information and the settlement of transport contracts.

Timetabling runs from setting up route networks to publishing services and supplying operation control and passenger information systems. Vehicle scheduling is handled by IVU.run, which supports the entire schedule planning process. Duty scheduling merges thousands of duty elements, crewing guidelines and qualifications through optimisation algorithms. For electric fleets the system weighs charging times, ranges, route lengths and depot or opportunity charging. In daily operation it monitors vehicle status, the timetable situation and the current deployment of vehicles and staff. The whole suite is also offered as a hosted service.

The company says more than 500 customers worldwide use the standard products of the suite. Named deployments include the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority. It reports as IVU Traffic Technologies AG and has published preliminary results for the first half of 2026.

paragraphs: Consat Telematics is a Swedish provider of public transportation systems, founded in 1986 and operating across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Australia, Canada, and Brazil. The wider Consat group reports offices on five continents and more than 250 employees.

The transit offering is modular, covering electromobility for electric fleet monitoring and smart charging as well as traffic control and monitoring for real-time fleet oversight and incident management. The hardware and software are installed on more than 40,000 vehicles globally. Named customers include Skyss in Norway, Tide Buss in Sweden, Ventura Bus Lines in Australia, and Din Tur in Sweden. paragraphs: NDI Recognition Systems sells Automatic License Plate Recognition products to law enforcement agencies worldwide. The same products are positioned for homeland security, where the company says they deliver data and recognition technology for defense analysis and prevention. Commercial uses include city parking ordinances, private and public parking garages and gas stations, and NDI also works with HOAs.

The company says it has worked with cities and countries securing borders, with technology built to perform 24/7 in harsh weather. NDI describes what it offers as a turnkey solution for all of a customer's ALPR needs.

A chief in South Carolina credits the ALPR with an arrest of individuals who broke into 25 cars. A crime analyst in Florida says camera data combined with witness statements, surveillance footage and DMV databases helped solve crimes.

provenance.quote: Our ALPR product solutions help law enforcement agencies worldwide prevent crime and protect their city borders.
NDI ALPR product solutions help defend the nation by delivering vital data and recognition technology for defense analysis and prevention.

Commercial ALPR uses are ideal for reinforcing city parking ordinances, private and public parking garages, and monitoring high-crime targets such as, gas stations. NDI also partners with HOAs to reduce neighborhood crime and congestion.

NDI Recognition Systems® has collaborated with both cities and countries looking to secure their borders with the very best in License Plate Recognition technology. ALPR Technology that could withstand the harshest weather conditions and still perform 24/7.
NDI Recognition Systems® is proud to offer our customers a turnkey solution for all their ALPR needs.
We have had many successes with the ALPR, including the arrest last week of individuals who broke into 25 cars last week & stole one of them.

By combining the data we receive from our cameras with witness statements, surveillance footage, DMV databases, and information uncovered by investigating officers, we’ve been able to solve numerous crimes.

paragraphs: Magnet Forensics sells software and hardware that investigators use to recover, analyze, and report on data from mobile devices, computers, cloud accounts, and vehicles. The company says it has more than 6,000 customers worldwide. The analysis product, Magnet Axiom, brings computer, mobile, cloud, vehicle, and acquired data into a single case.

Magnet Graykey handles access, preservation, and extraction of data from iOS and Android devices. Graykey goes to agencies only: the company states it is restricted to select countries, is not available to the private sector, and asks that inquiries come from an agency-issued email. Graykey Fastrak runs simultaneous extractions on multiple workstations to scale a lab. A vehicle product, Magnet Autokey, pulls data from infotainment systems over USB rather than through teardowns or chip-off extraction. Autokey is included with Graykey Premier online licenses in the US.

For private sector work, Magnet Verakey performs consent-based full file system, logical, and category extractions from mobile devices. It captures employee consent and notifies administrators on every extraction. Collected data exports to analysis tools including Magnet Axiom Cyber. Scott Ferro, an examiner at the Rochester Police Department, is quoted saying Graykey makes life a whole lot easier in accessing data on iPhones.

paragraphs: CalAmp sells telematics devices and cloud software that organizations use to monitor, track, and protect vehicles, equipment, and cargo. The company describes covering the whole chain, from the user experience down to the platform and the edge devices themselves. Its telematics cloud is pitched at fleet operators, logistics companies, equipment manufacturers, and the systems integrators who build on top of it.

Devices on the vehicle collect location, speed, engine health, driver behavior, and outside sensor readings in real time. The cloud then turns protocols such as CAN bus, J1939, OBD-II, and Modbus into clean, structured output. Customers pull that data through APIs, a cloud connector, or event-driven alerts. A device management layer lets administrators assign roles governing who can view, change, or execute particular management functions. Software can be prototyped, tested, and deployed to devices over the air.

CalAmp says the platform is built for commercial fleets and software providers in construction, trucking, utilities, the public sector, and equipment manufacturing. The company states it has been in business for 40 years, with thousands of customers and more than 275 approved or pending patents. For data handling it cites SOC 2 Type II certification along with GDPR and SB327 compliance.

paragraphs: Videray Technologies, founded in 2018 by a group of engineers in Boston, Massachusetts, develops non-intrusive inspection and imaging technology. Its home page describes what it makes as a portable handheld backscatter X-ray imager. The buyers it names are law enforcement officials who face criminal techniques while performing their duties in the field.

The company attributes image depth to 140 keV of power and its optics, which it says allow seeing through more material. The product is called the PX1, and Videray credits it with advanced image processing and image clarity. Portability and connectivity are presented as ways to speed up inspection, allowing quick scans and dispositioning of potential threats.

Videray positions the system for mission-critical imaging work where the overall system footprint or the scan standoff distance may be constrained. Paul Bradshaw is the chief executive officer. Headquarters are at 529 Main Street, Suite 100, Charlestown, MA 02129.

quote.text: Videray is a proud American company formed to disrupt the market with its advanced non-intrusive inspection and imaging technologies deployed worldwide.

paragraphs: Apptegy sells a communications platform to K-12 school districts, gathering the tools and training that district staff use to reach families. The pitch to district leaders is that the school brand stays at the front of every message.

Districts get a branded website managed through a drag-and-drop editor with page permissions for contributors and analytics. A district-branded mobile app for iOS and Android carries school information and two-way messaging for families. Alerts go out by email, push notification, SMS, text-to-speech, voice call and social media from one place. Automated translation is offered for more than 100 languages, and websites are built to meet WCAG 2.1 A and AA standards.

The home page states that 5,273 districts have switched to the platform for their communications. Beyond software the company publishes SchoolCEO magazine, with guides and original research for district leaders. One study listed there was done jointly with NSPRA on the relationship between superintendents and school communicators.

paragraphs: CampDoc sells camp and youth program software built for registration, health management, and day-to-day operations. The buyers are organizations that run programs for children and students, and the company says it powers more than 1,250 camps, youth programs and school programs. Signups, payments, rosters and family-facing workflows sit in one place.

On the health side, staff collect health forms, manage medications, document incidents, and keep records accessible when they need them. The health forms are digital and use conditional logic. Medication administration runs through an eMAR. Attendance, communication, reporting and daily program operations are kept together in one place. Rosters and health records stay aligned across the system.

For IT and compliance reviewers, the company points to SOC 2 Type II controls, role-based access to PHI, single sign-on for organizations that require it, and multi-factor authentication. It also states that the platform is HIPAA and FERPA compliant. Plans start at $355 per month. Onboarding, training, support and compliance are included in every plan, according to the pricing section. Published customer stories include a municipal parks and recreation department that replaced paper forms and manual tracking.

paragraphs: Extra Duty Solutions administers extra duty programs for public safety agencies such as police departments, sheriff offices, state agencies, and fire departments. It also gives law enforcement agencies access to public safety scheduling software from Jivasoft, its IT division. Today it provides scheduling software and administrative support for agencies across the country.

The about page dates the business to 2015, when it served large corporations and coordinated extra-duty officers for executive protection, factory security, and logistics needs. In 2016 the focus shifted to serving the agencies themselves. In 2017 the company exited the corporate market entirely, which it says removed the conflict of interest that arises when one firm represents both the agency and the corporate customer.

Extra Duty Solutions acquired Jivasoft, a Texas-based company in law enforcement scheduling software, which brought the On-Duty and Xtra-Duty platforms into its lineup. Milestones listed on the same page include initiating service with a 100th agency. Later entries record surpassing $150M in annualized extra-duty invoicing. The most recent listed milestone is a 250th agency partnership. According to its own news release, the company was ranked No. 2740 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies in America.

before.name: Avail Technologies
before.description: myAvail enterprise transit management ITS and CAD/AVL for mid-size US agencies

paragraphs: Avail Technologies sells enterprise transit management software to public transit agencies. The company states that its target market is transit operators with medium-sized fleets.

The myAvail platform covers vehicle location, dispatching, workforce management, reporting, and rider communications, so a team works from one connected system rather than several tools. A single shared database moves data throughout the organization. Dispatchers see where every bus and driver is, and incidents are tracked as they occur. Business intelligence dashboards report metrics in real time, which the company frames as a way to improve efficiency, justify funding requests, and demonstrate compliance. Features can be added to the platform as an agency's needs grow, and the company says myAvail ships multiple platform updates a year.

Founded in 1999, Avail describes a family-oriented staff working hand-in-hand with transit professionals. It says it has stayed a mid-sized company by design. An announcement on the site names Rick Spangler as president and chief executive as the company continues a transition to full employee ownership.

before.name: Cyclomedia
before.description: Vehicle-captured 360 street imagery and lidar with AI analytics for local governments and utilities

paragraphs: Cyclomedia sells geospatial data built from street-level imagery, lidar point clouds, and aerial data covering public space. Public authorities are a core market, using it to manage streets, buildings, and public assets. Utility and energy providers use it to plan, inspect, and manage their networks.

Street Smart, the company's viewer, brings 360 degree imagery, lidar, and map layers into one browser-based workspace. From the desk, users measure distances along facades, pavements, and openings. Automated analysis detects pavement defects, surface types, and deterioration in high-resolution imagery. Property valuation is another stated use, supported by current visual evidence and measurements. Open integrations and APIs connect the data to existing GIS and asset management systems.

The company says it has worked in geospatial capture and visualisation for more than 40 years with public authorities across Europe and beyond. Specialised capture vehicles survey cities and regions throughout the year. Routes are coordinated with local authorities to limit disruption. Its case studies page lists a digital twin created for the London Borough of Harrow from street imagery and lidar.

quote.text: Shift more work from the field to the office by using Street Smart and work more efficiently.

paragraphs: TRM Labs sells blockchain intelligence data, software and AI agents to government agencies and financial institutions that work against crypto crime. The company says 600+ of them across 75 countries rely on it. Its data maps the criminal economy across 40+ categories of illicit activity. Investigators use the platform to detect, investigate and disrupt crypto-related crime.

The investigation tool is TRM Forensics, and an AI investigator called Co-Case Agent is built into it. The agent reasons across blockchain records, threat-actor intelligence and victim reports to cluster syndicates, build freeze packages and triage tipline leads. Compliance teams get Compliance360, which the company says covers 184+ chains and 840+ cross-chain bridges. Regulators get Supervision360 for licensing, supervision and enforcement work. National security organizations get NatSec360, which adds the BLOCKINT API and TRM Bulk Data. Through the Beacon Network, VASPs are notified in real time when law enforcement flags illicit funds reaching their services, so they can hold them.

Law enforcement users can also join LEO Labs, a monthly working group the company runs for law enforcement only. TRM says its intelligence has supported convictions, asset freezes and OFAC designations in multiple jurisdictions. Strategic partners named on the national security page include Flashpoint, Magnet Forensics, Searchlight Cyber and i2.

before.name: Forerunner
before.description: Floodplain management software: NFIP/CRS compliance, elevation certificates; $26.3M Series B - exhibited at StormCon 2026

paragraphs: Forerunner sells software it calls a geospatial intelligence layer. The platform unifies geospatial data, field operations, and AI-powered workflows in one place. Local government is a core buyer, with compliance work across stormwater, floodplain, and code enforcement programs. The company also markets to energy and infrastructure operators handling inspections across active sites and assets.

At the base sits a map-first view holding every asset, permit parcel, violation, and environmental layer. On top of it run configurable workflows for inspections, permits, violations, and grant tracking. Inspection findings then generate corrective actions, and permit deadlines trigger notifications. The company says adoption brings no rip-and-replace projects and no major workflow disruptions. It claims teams are up and running in weeks.

Published case studies name the Puerto Rico Planning Board, which the company says replaced paper forms and spreadsheets for field inspections and code compliance. Another states that Lee County saves approximately 16 hours of staff time per week. A further case study describes Ponce Inlet centralizing National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System workflows to reclaim 10 or more hours per week.

paragraphs: Ekin Smart City Technology sells monitoring devices and software that law enforcement agencies use to enforce the laws of their communities. The product list runs from an Automatic License Plate Reader, or ALPR, to red light enforcement and speed and traffic enforcement. All of those devices feed data captured at the edge to maestro, the company's backend platform, which analyzes it in real time. Violations can then be issued automatically and monitored from a central dashboard.

One product, Ekin Patrol G2, is a modular AI-powered bar that attaches to vehicles, so a patrol car carries the sensors instead of fixed infrastructure. The company says it can detect and process speeding and parking violations in real time. It can also alert officers when someone approaches the vehicle. Ekin markets similar monitoring to neighborhoods, where the systems watch vehicles, pedestrian traffic and large wildlife around the clock in all weather.

Ekin designs and manufactures its own hardware and develops its software in-house. It states that it has used machine learning and artificial intelligence for more than 15 years. Both the law enforcement and neighborhood pages point to a case study of Coral Gables, Florida. A December 2025 press headline announces a $25M U.S. expansion and a transition to U.S.-based manufacturing.

paragraphs: Unison sells software for the business of federal government, running from acquisitions through to budgeting. It sells to both sides of the transaction: agencies buying goods and services, and the companies bidding on and managing government contracts.

Its contract writing product is built for federal contracting professionals and aims at strict adherence to the Federal Acquisition Regulation. That product covers the whole acquisition process and is configurable to each agency's own needs. A separate set of AI modules addresses requirements development, acquisition package assembly and offer evaluation. Those modules are meant to run alongside existing systems of record rather than displace them. A third line handles cost engineering, helping agencies and contractors produce lifecycle estimates that are traceable and defendable.

The company says its contract writing product is used by 15 civilian, intelligence and defense cabinet-level agencies and dozens of defense programs. It cites a FedRAMP authorization and a DISA provisional authorization at impact level 5. The AI modules are listed as FedRAMP certified and authorized at defense impact level 4. Its cost models draw on 50 years of ongoing cost research by a dedicated team.

paragraphs: Echodyne designs, manufactures and delivers commercial radar systems built around a technology it calls MESA. Its customers are systems suppliers, integrators and end users in defense, government, critical infrastructure protection, C-UAS and UAS/AAM markets in more than 40 countries. MESA stands for metamaterials electronically scanned array, and the company holds global patents on those radar architectures.

The radars are aimed at counter-UAS and multi-domain missions, where the company says they improve safety and security outcomes. Configurations range from fixed installations to rapid setup portable kits, and Echodyne describes MIL-STD reliability at COTS availability. The company has announced an Android Team Awareness Kit plugin that lets users configure, control and visualize data from its radars within ATAK.
Radars are manufactured outside Seattle, Washington, in the United States. Echodyne is AS9100 and ISO 9001 certified. AS9100 is a standardized quality management system for the aerospace industry.

paragraphs: Veritone sells enterprise AI software that converts unstructured video, audio, and text into data for models and automated workflows, across commercial media, public sector, and talent acquisition lines. Veritone Investigate acts as a central hub where an agency stores digital evidence from disparate locations, and Veritone Redact automates redaction of sensitive data from audio, video, and image-based evidence. Veritone Tracker tracks persons of interest across videos using similarity scores rather than facial recognition, and Veritone Illuminate searches Electronically Stored Information for early case assessment. Veritone Contact collects and reports stop data for California AB 953 Racial Identity and Profiling Act (RIPA) compliance, and Veritone IDentify uses a booking database to identify subjects. notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "Systems & Methods, Inc. (SMI) is a family-led business in its second and third generations." Fetched https://www.smi-inc.com. Company named verbatim in the quote, matching the board name exactly including the ampersand form. Description match on both halves: child support — "Through SMART™, we disburse child support payments for 18 states and 16 Tribal Nations"; and government payment processing — the site describes custom disbursement solutions for "dozens of U.S. state and local agencies" with "20+ years in state disbursement unit (SDU) operations". Independent company on its own domain, no parent-site issue.

paragraphs: Systems & Methods, Inc. sells government payment acceptance, processing, disbursement, and customer service, and its SMART child support solution disburses child support payments for 18 states and 16 Tribal Nations. The company operates state disbursement units in 16 states, processing more than 76 million payments annually with a 99.99% accuracy rate. Calls are not outsourced, and the service model ranges from full-service customer service centers and IVR functionality to collection and disbursement information only.

A second line is prepaid debit cards: the smiONE Visa Prepaid Card reaches more than two million families in 16 states and 15 Tribes. SMART Pay takes online payments from non-custodial parents, employers, and others by credit and debit card, ACH, digital wallet, text, and cash. Kudzu is an online banking app for individuals, with no monthly or overdraft fees, a budgeting and saving toolkit, and learning courses.

A third line, SMILE, is a government accounting system that has been the financial system of record for the Georgia Department of Human Resources for more than 40 years. Since 1978 it has covered budgeting, asset management, general ledger, employee payroll, travel and leave, child welfare, auditing, and payment processing for state, local, and client funds.

before.name: Amazon Web Services (AWS)
before.description: Cloud computing platform - exhibited at ICMA 2025, NACM 2026, AIRA 2026, EDUCAUSE 2026

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "AWS is the world's most comprehensive cloud, enabling organizations to accelerate innovation, reduce costs, and scale more efficiently" The URL is factually correct and does NOT violate the parent-domain rule: aws.amazon.com is AWS's own canonical property (its own brand, console, pricing, docs and its own careers page at https://aws.amazon.com/careers/, HTTP 200), not Amazon's corporate site at amazon.com. The govtech tie is on-domain too: https://aws.amazon.com/government-education/ (HTTP 200) is AWS's public sector page, and the homepage names 'AWS GovCloud (US-East)' and 'AWS GovCloud (US-West)'. MY JUDGMENT ON WHETHER THE BOARD SHOULD CARRY THIS AT ALL - the URL passes but the record is still risky, for a reason the URL check cannot fix: aws.amazon.com/careers/ does not host jobs, it hands off to https://www.amazon.jobs/en/business_categories/amazon-web-services. That feed is tens of thousands of global AWS engineering/PM/ops roles, of which SLED account executive roles are a tiny fraction. Any homepage- or careers-page-level scrape of this record will flood SLED JOBS with irrelevant listings - the same practical damage the parent-domain rule exists to prevent, arriving by a different route. Recommendation: keep the URL if AWS is wanted on the board, but the record must be wired to

before.name: Sagitec Solutions
before.description: Pension, unemployment insurance and workforce systems for state agencies - exhibited at SNA ANC 2027

paragraphs: Sagitec describes itself as a global software provider focused on solving complex, business-rule-driven problems with proven technology. Its pension administration software, Neospin, is a browser-based system for administering pension benefits, and has served public and private pension funds since 2004. Neosurance covers unemployment insurance, disability insurance, and paid family medical leave tax, benefits, and appeals administration.

WorkforceNXT connects agencies, employers, and job seekers, and supports job matching, case management, and training programs. Neotrient handles meal eligibility, claims processing, and compliance tracking for child nutrition programs. A separate eligibility and enrollment system for Medicaid runs on the Xelence platform. Services listed alongside the products include training and development, enterprise content management, and hosting on Microsoft Azure Government.

Buyers named on these pages include state agencies, state workforce agencies, school districts, and Managed Care Organizations. One government customer is named, the Maine Public Employees Retirement System, whose project the company says it has been awarded. The company states a core focus on the public sector.

before.name: For The Record (FTR)
before.description: Digital court recording and record management technology for judiciaries

paragraphs: For The Record makes recording technology for courts, capturing what is said in a proceeding and turning it into text that can be searched. One audience is court administrators trying to keep operations running at lower cost. Judges are a second audience, able to pull up audio, video, and speech-to-text without leaving the bench.

Recording runs on multiple audio channels, so individual speakers stay distinct even when they talk over one another. Courts that need local infrastructure can run the FTR Gold software in the courthouse rather than in the cloud. The cloud option is described as centralized storage built to NIST 800-53 Rev. 5 with more than a thousand security and privacy controls. Access is governed by role-based permissions, audit trails, and encryption of both transmission and storage.

The company says it supports courts in more than 80 countries. Its software is API-ready and meant to sit alongside the case management and evidence systems a court already runs. The work extends past software into specifying equipment and installing courtroom hardware.

quote.text: A court record is the official, permanent account of a legal case.

provenance.quote: advanced audio capture, real-time speech-to-text, secure cloud-based storage, and instant access to records
help court administrators run more efficient, economical, and resilient operations
Instantly access audio, video, and speech-to-text transcripts without leaving the bench.
Multi-channel audio capture isolates speakers for clarity, even with overtalk in noisy environments.
Reliable, on-premises recording for courts with local infrastructure needs
Centralized, secure storage meeting NIST 800-53 Rev. 5 standards with 1,200+ security and privacy controls
role-based access, audit trails, and encrypted transmission and storage
Supporting courts in more than 80 countries around the world

paragraphs: RTA Fleet360 is a fleet maintenance and management system built to centralize work orders, streamline preventive maintenance, and manage parts and fuel. Asset management in Fleet360 covers vehicles, equipment and tools, with digital profiles tracking availability, repairs, warranties and costs across shops. Parts and inventory features let parts managers track usage, automate inventory and warranty tracking, and simplify ordering.

Budgeting and cost tools cover asset lifecycle planning, maintenance and repair costs, inventory cost, fuel cost per mile, and technician labor hours. Reporting includes business intelligence dashboards, a Fleet Success Scorecard, and customizable reporting tools for fleet managers. A mobile app brings Fleet360 to a device so managers and technicians can handle work orders, inventory, inspections and fleet performance on the go.

The homepage describes the product as an FMIS for public sector fleets. Beyond the software, the company offers fleet consulting and training delivered online or in person. Purchasing is offered through purchasing partners, where members qualify for pricing on software, hardware and consulting services.

before.name: Fast Enterprises
before.description: Unemployment insurance, labor and revenue systems for state agencies - exhibited at NASWA 2025, NCSEA 2026

paragraphs: Fast Enterprises builds the administrative systems government agencies use to run public-facing programs. The company says it began in 1997 around the idea of all-in-one software for government agencies.

Its tax product, GenTax, is stated to be in use by more than sixty tax and revenue agencies worldwide. A driver and vehicle system covers licensing, identity services, titling, registration and permitting. Another product handles unemployment insurance and paid leave across tax, benefits and appeals. A child support system brings program management into a single place. Audit, collections and identity verification are offered alongside the software as services.

The buyers are national, state or provincial, and local government agencies. The company states its core software is in production at more than a hundred government agencies worldwide. It describes its own aim as being a provider of software and consulting services to government agencies.

before.name: Protech Solutions
before.description: Child support enforcement and HHS case systems for state agencies - exhibited at NCSEA 2026

paragraphs: Protech Solutions, Inc. is headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas, and has developed enterprise-level systems for large, statewide agencies for 30 years. The stated focus is child support systems, homelessness, corrections, and fatherhood programs, with enterprise-level systems provided to government agencies worldwide. The pages describe an international child support system built in collaboration with The Hague Convention.
In AR, the pages claim the first web-based child support platform in the nation. A complex 46-county CSE system in SC is presented as work taken on where larger vendors failed.

Analytics are credited with boosting child support collections in the State of Maine. Hawaii's CSE system is being replatformed to better serve children and families. Digital integration is credited with revitalizing NJ's SNAP & TANF systems.

quote.text: For 30 years, we’ve transformed government technology across social services.

provenance.quote: Protech Solutions, Inc., headquartered in Little Rock, Arkansas, has been at the forefront of GovTech for 30 years.

We specialize in GovTech solutions, with a deep focus on child support systems, homelessness, corrections, fatherhood programs, and more. Our team has decades of experience, providing enterprise-level systems to government agencies worldwide.
While we work with U.S. clients, our reach extends internationally, with notable projects like the international child support system in collaboration with The Hague Convention.
In AR, we built the Nation’s first web-based Child Support platform.
Where larger vendors failed, we succeeded on a complex 46-county SC CSE System.
Our analytics helped boost child support collections in the State of Maine.
We are replatforming Hawaii’s CSE system to better serve their children & families.
Our digital integration revitalized NJ’s SNAP & TANF systems.

before.name: Stellarware Corporation
before.description: Child support lien network, new hire reporting and Medicaid recovery web systems for state child support and labor agencies - exhibited at NCSEA 2026

paragraphs: Stellarware Corporation was founded in 1997 as a web design firm and now builds web systems for government and private sector organizations. Core business areas listed are project management and operation for insurance intercept, Medicaid, financial institution data match (FIDM), real property data match, new hire reporting and web design. Stellarware operates the Child Support Lien Network, hosted by the State of Rhode Island, and works with the states of Rhode Island and Texas on the Medicaid Recovery Network.

New Hire Reporting projects are managed in the District of Columbia, Georgia, Minnesota, Rhode Island, Virginia and Wisconsin, among other states. Those projects help employers work with state government through Internet based systems, including a Child Support Portal. Plug-in solutions named on the site include a Lump Sum Payment Module and electronic distribution of Income Withholding Orders.

The Child Support Lien Network has assisted 32 U.S. state agencies in collecting over $2.4 billion in past-due child support. New Hire projects processed over 17 million new hire reports in the year 2023, and the Medicaid Recovery Network has collected over $33.8 million in Medicaid costs for State government.

paragraphs: Adobe sells creative software, and the tools it names first are Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere. A second line covers documents, using AI to make edits, answer questions, share information and produce polished content. For companies the pitch is to unify data, content and workflows and to personalize at scale.

Firefly is the generative AI piece, a creative space for making and editing images, video, audio and vector graphics from text prompts. It carries Adobe's own models next to partner models from Google, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Luma AI and Runway. Adobe says those models are trained on licensed Adobe Stock and public domain content, and that it does not train on users' personal or generated content. Prompts are accepted in more than 100 languages, and audio and video translation covers more than 20.

The audience Adobe names for Firefly is designers, photographers, video editors, marketers and social media creators. Students and teachers are offered a discount on the creative tools. On provenance, Adobe co-founded the Content Authenticity Initiative in 2019, described as a coalition of over 3,300 members. The company says Firefly has been used to generate over 18 billion assets globally. Its catalog page notes that a purchase can be cancelled within 14 days for a full refund.

before.name: SaltyCloud
before.description: Isora GRC risk assessment, vendor review and compliance workflow software for higher education and public sector security teams - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Isora GRC is software that gives security teams one connected workspace to run assessments, manage vendors and assets, track risks, and prove compliance. It is positioned against spreadsheets and against enterprise GRC platforms that require months of setup, dedicated admins, and consultant-driven configuration. Questionnaires are structured and aligned to frameworks such as NIST, CIS, GLBA, and HECVAT, and contributors upload evidence inline and route responses for approval.

For third-party work, the platform connects vendor questionnaires, inventory records, risk findings, and reporting in one workspace. Vendor assessments cover HECVAT, SIG, and CAIQ, and a one-click HECVAT uploader imports completed spreadsheets, matches responses, and scores automatically. Findings flow into a collaborative risk register carrying lineage from questionnaire to control to risk, where owners are assigned and remediation is tracked.

The solutions index describes the product for public sector institutions, for financial institutions such as banks and credit unions, and for information security teams. Higher education institutions managing hundreds of vendors are described as using it as their primary vendor assessment platform.

before.name: ITO Health
before.description: Medicaid eligibility screening, benefits enrollment and social needs care management software for government agencies, FQHCs and payers - exhibited at NatCon 2026

paragraphs: ITO Health is a Public Benefit Company built by clinicians and health professionals. It makes tools that help care workers and benefits specialists connect people to the support they need. The customers are health and social care organizations running the workflows behind eligibility decisions, enrollment, and ongoing coordination.

HealthBase and HealthWorks are the core offerings, sibling configurations of the same platform for different operational needs. HealthBase turns client information into completed benefit applications and real-world actions rather than referrals. HealthWorks is the employer-facing version, a benefit navigation platform for workforces. Eligibility decision support applies deterministic logic across more than 120 federal, state, and local programs to produce auditable determinations.

HealthBase is built for social service organizations, federally qualified health centers, community health centers, and healthcare systems that coordinate benefits enrollment and social care. The products page puts current eligibility and enrollment coverage at more than 75 federal and local programs. The platform supports HL7 FHIR, custom API integrations, and connections to electronic health records. The company states that it is a HIPAA-compliant organization. It says clinicians founded it.

paragraphs: Intrado sells call handling and management systems for emergency response. It describes itself as the connective tissue that gets the right help to the right location as quickly as possible.

Alongside the call center products, one line keeps employees safe wherever they work while meeting state and federal regulations. Another covers incident management for schools from prevention through response and recovery. Network services are offered to improve call routing and data sharing and to deliver on i3 compliance. ECaTS, the Emergency Call Tracking System, generates descriptive reports from 9-1-1 call data.

The company puts its history in the emergency services industry at 45 years. That history includes acquisitions of Lucent Public Safety, Positron Public Safety Systems, ECaTS, 911 ETC and 911 Enable. Headquarters are in Longmont, Colorado, with a manufacturing site in Montreal, Quebec. The company reports approximately 950 employees worldwide, most of them in the Longmont and Montreal regions.

paragraphs: Aurigo Software sells capital program management software to government agencies that plan, build and maintain public infrastructure. It also serves facility owners in areas such as data centers, life sciences, manufacturing, and energy and utilities. The company's platform, Masterworks, brings planning, execution, financials, right of way and analytics together in one system.

On the delivery side it coordinates contracts, schedules, costs and field work so teams can hold to the original plan and keep a complete audit trail. Compliance, funding transparency and governance are meant to sit inside everyday work so public money stays accountable. Agencies can change forms, workflows, business rules and dashboards through configuration rather than code. An AI layer called Lumina supports decision-making with compliance and governance built in, and the company says every insight and recommendation it produces can be audited and traced.

Cities, counties, transit agencies and transportation departments across North America use the platform to manage capital programs, replace legacy systems and automate federal reimbursements. The company claims more than 300 customers and over 20 years of capital program expertise behind the product. It also says the software monitors project signals to catch cost, schedule and delivery risks before they turn critical.

before.name: Carbyne
before.description: Cloud-native 911 call handling with live video, location, and AI triage

paragraphs: Carbyne builds and supports Axon 911 Core, a cloud-native infrastructure layer deployed in agencies across the United States and internationally. Its call-handling product, APEX, pulls call management capabilities into a single user interface for telecommunicators.

Patented live video lets responders see through the eyes of a caller. Location tools pinpoint a caller and track movement as permitted. AI-powered translation arrives directly on the call taker's screen. During call surges, an AI triage tool sorts through calls to identify redundant bystander and onlooker reports, freeing call takers for other emergencies. A continuity option has the AT&T Resolution Center redirect 911 calls and texts to devices running APEX Continuity. That reroute is triggered manually by the center rather than automatically.

The company states 99.999% call-handling uptime in the cloud. It describes the platform as providing the security of AWS GovCloud. Carbyne counts more than 100 partners and over 40 integrations on its open platform. The site names Orleans Parish Communication District as a center using its Emergency Call Triage.

before.name: Miovision
before.description: Traffic data collection and smart intersection technology

paragraphs: Miovision sells traffic data collection tools meant to give planners the accurate, verifiable data their mobility plans depend on. It also sells detection equipment that improves signal performance by responding to real-world road user demand, from bicycles to articulated trucks. Its Opticom line clears the path for emergency fleets without re-timing entire corridors.

Portable devices capture comprehensive multimodal count data including cars, trucks, pedestrians and bikes. A newer optimization product replaces manual five-year retiming cycles with iterative, objective-based optimization that the company says cuts manual effort by up to half. Engineers compare plans side-by-side, validate against industry standards, and push updates directly to field controllers without manual data re-entry.

The company says that since 2005 it has had 2,000 customers in 68 countries and 13,000 cities, with 30 billion vehicles and 1.5 billion pedestrians counted. It lists more than 300 detection customers in North America. Detroit partnered with Miovision to upgrade over 600 intersections. In San Rafael, police and fire vehicles now receive signal priority at 53 intersections.

before.description: Dedicated public safety broadband network - exhibited at IACP 2026

notes.text: Website verified 2026-08-25 by an independent check that was asked to reject it. Page says: "© AT&T Intellectual Property. All rights reserved. FirstNet and the FirstNet logo are registered trademarks and service marks of the First Responder Network Authority." Fetched https://www.firstnet.com. The entity question in the CAUTION resolves cleanly: the footer copyright is AT&T's ('© AT&T Intellectual Property'), while the FirstNet marks are acknowledged as belonging to the First Responder Network Authority — i.e. this domain is the AT&T-operated commercial service, which is exactly the board entity 'FirstNet, Built with AT&T'. I confirmed the split by also fetching the federal side: firstnetauthority.gov states 'The First Responder Network Authority is an independent agency within the U.S. Department of Commerce's National Telecommunications and Information Administration' and sends users elsewhere for service with 'Access my FirstNet account (FirstNet.com).' So .gov is the agency, .com is the AT&T service. On rule 3: firstnet.com is NOT the parent's corporate domain (that is att.com) — it is the product's own dedicated domain with its own branding, plans and support, so it is acceptable. FLAG for the board operator, though: FirstNet does not recruit as a separate employer. Sales roles on this product are posted as AT&T requisitions, so a scraper pointed at firstnet.com will like

before.description: Cloud digital collections management and public discovery platform for archives, public libraries, museums, and heritage sites - exhibited at PLA 2026

paragraphs: Recollect sells a cloud-based Collection Management System for galleries, libraries, archives, museums, academic institutions and heritage sites. The product is presented as management and discovery for a digital collection, held in a single digital repository built to support staff, students, and researchers. Metadata and contextual information configure the site and link assets together, and content of any format is reached from any device.

The about page lists the organisations the platform supports, beginning with libraries, archives and museums wanting to digitise and share their collections. That list also names local government bodies preserving public records. It further names indigenous and marginalised communities seeking tools for managing culturally sensitive materials, and educational institutions providing students and researchers with accessible resources.

The same page states that by 2020 the company became a standalone entity, expanding into the USA, UK, Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong. It reports support for over 160 sites globally. Case studies name the Museum of Flight, Palos Verdes Library District, the State Library of Oregon and Denver Public Library.

before.name: Ad Astra Information Systems
before.description: Academic scheduling, course demand analytics, and room and event management software for colleges and universities - exhibited at EDUCAUSE 2026

paragraphs: Ad Astra sells scheduling and academic planning software to colleges and universities. One platform covers course scheduling and campus event management for higher education institutions.

Schedulers build sections on a visual grid, handling buildings, spaces, faculty and room assignments in the same workflow. Recommendations drawn from historical enrollment patterns point to changes that ease course bottlenecks. Finished schedules and later edits publish straight to the campus student information system. Event requests and approvals run through workflows the institution sets up. Public event calendars can be viewed by category and embedded on a campus website.

before.name: Electro Scan
before.description: Machine-based pipe defect and leak assessment for municipal sewer and water - exhibited at AWWA ACE 2026

paragraphs: Electro Scan sells leak detection and lead pipe location work for water and sewer systems. The company says municipal sewer utilities and sewer contractors use it to pin down the location, measurement and flow of defects inside a pipe before a repair or replacement job.

The method rests on a simple claim: pipe defects that leak water also leak electricity, so a defect shows up whether or not it happens to be leaking during the inspection. A low voltage conductivity probe travels through the pipe at 45 to 60 feet per minute, locating and measuring defects as it goes. Crews can then create summary and detail level reports for a team to review. The flagship probe is built for gravity mains between 6 and 30 inches in diameter, and the company says agencies and contractors use it worldwide.

Electro Scan lists ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management systems. Its case studies page includes a North American benchmark study comparing closed-circuit television inspection with focused electrode leak location on gravity sewer mains. Other write-ups describe a Florida utility dealing with excessive inflow and infiltration in its gravity collection system.

before.name: FUNDVIEW
before.description: Fund accounting and ERP software for cities and local governments, covering financials, payroll, utility billing and municipal court - exhibited at GFOA 2026

paragraphs: FUNDVIEW sells an ERP platform to local governments, covering finance, workforce, utilities, community development, and court and citizen services. The pitch is aimed at cities running several disconnected systems and entering the same figures by hand in each one.

Every module posts into the same real-time general ledger, which is what removes the second entry. The finance side covers budgets, purchasing, payables, reconciliation, assets, cash receipting and reporting. Workforce management joins payroll, human resources and employee time onto one record. Court receipts reach finance as they are taken rather than at month end.

The company says more than 180 Texas local governments run on the platform. It states that fund accounting, financial statements and audit documentation follow GASB and GAAP standards. Payroll reporting covers 941, TMRS, TWC, E-Verify, new hire and year-end wage filings.

paragraphs: CITIZ3N Government Solutions builds modular platforms for government agencies that oversee Affordable Care Act marketplaces, Medicaid, health and human services programs, and health benefits for government employees. before.name: Envisio
before.description: Strategic planning, performance measurement, and public dashboards built for local government

paragraphs: Envisio makes software for public agencies that need to turn a strategic plan into tracked work and reportable results. It is built for the public sector and, the company says, only the public sector. Customers span government, education, healthcare and nonprofit organizations.

Plans can be laid out as a cascade, a Gantt chart, tags or scorecards, depending on how the organization works. Staff get scheduled reminders to submit progress and performance updates. Those updates roll up automatically into reports covering actions, projects, measures and narrative. The same material feeds public dashboards a community can read. Every package includes unlimited users.

More than 200 organizations use Envisio, by the company's count. Example dashboards on the site include the City of Rockville's climate action plan, which tracks emissions reduction and renewable energy adoption. The company frames its purpose around a stated decline in trust in public institutions. It points to recognition as a GovTech 100 company. Chief executive Craig Ross was previously interim CEO at Euna Solutions and CEO of eCivis.

quote.text: Too often, those plans get stuck in spreadsheets, and nothing changes.

paragraphs: Mission Driven Data sells Janet, a tool that automates replication of a Credible database into a standard SQL database format, updated every night or on demand. Hundreds of agencies use the Credible EHR to record information about services, schedule appointments, process billing and financial transactions, and e-prescribe. Janet adds a wraparound layer over that system, with reporting and analytics on Microsoft Power BI dashboards, data integration and warehousing, notifications and workflow optimization.

The agencies addressed on the homepage offer a wide range of mental health and social services, some supporting rural areas with a staff of a few dozen and others serving thousands of clients a year. Janet also delivers the WHO-5 Well-Being Index to agency clients weekly by automatic text message, connecting that survey data to the agency Credible data. The about page states that leaders at over 50 behavioral health agencies and organizations nationwide rely on Janet.

before.name: Tantalus Systems
before.description: Smart grid AMI and grid analytics for public power utilities and co-ops

paragraphs: Tantalus is a technology company selling grid modernization systems to public power and electric cooperative utilities. It has been delivering data-centric products to that market for more than 35 years.

The products sit on the Tantalus Grid Modernization Platform, a modular architecture meant to move data across devices, systems and vendors. One piece is edge-computing metering infrastructure aimed at resiliency, reliability and lower total cost of ownership. Another handles load management and distributed energy resources sitting behind the meter. A gateway device fits any ANSI meter socket and adds visibility and control behind the meter without replacing the meter itself.

Utilities across North America partner with the company on distribution grid work, with published case studies including one in Bolivar, Tennessee. Tantalus Systems trades on the TSX under the symbol GRID and on OTCQX. It is based in Burnaby, British Columbia. Recent announcements include a debt restructuring and an annual survey of how utilities view grid modernization.

before.name: SmartCover Systems
before.description: Remote sewer level and overflow monitoring for municipal collection systems

paragraphs: SmartCover sells remote monitoring and controls for sewer, lift stations and stormwater infrastructure. The company describes the offering as turning real-time remote infrastructure data into insights for utility customers who want to minimize OpEx and reduce CapEx. Stated uses include overflow prevention, cleaning schedules, I&I identification, and chemical optimization.

The pages present satellite communication as what keeps the system visible. Alarms and notifications are described as giving advance notice so staff can prepare and respond. Installation is described as needing no confined space entry, with the work done in shop. A mobile app is offered, with system insights available wherever the user is.

A published case study covers the City of Kelowna in British Columbia. That city is described as using the technology for overflow prevention, optimization of high frequency cleaning, and ongoing I&I studies. Other departments in the city are described as using it for H2S monitoring, leachate at the solid waste facility, and stream level monitoring.

quote.text: Uninterrupted visibility of the system reduces risks, avoids damages and fees, and encourages efficiencies.

before.name: Regroup Mass Notification
before.description: Emergency and routine mass notification for cities, counties and schools

paragraphs: Regroup sells a mass notification platform that organizations use for emergency alerts and for everyday operational messages in one place. Government buyers use it to reach residents quickly and to improve communication among their own staff.

Alerts go out by text message, email, voice call, and social media. Messages can be aimed at a specific area through geofencing. Recipients can reply, so senders learn who is safe and who needs help. The platform also connects to federal and regional public warning systems. For larger incidents, a dashboard gives one interface for monitoring every part of an event as it unfolds.

Regroup dates its service to 2006. The company says onboarding, unlimited training, and around the clock support come at no extra cost. Comments published on the site come from county emergency management offices, among other customers. Schools and campuses are another audience, with alerts for lockdowns and similar emergencies.
